definition_zh: 公担（一百公斤）；英担（约一百一十二磅）；[旧] 谷物计量单位
definition_en: a unit of weight equal to a hundred kilograms, or an older hundredweight
core_image: 一只麻袋被吊上磅秤，指针停在一百公斤的刻度
scene: 粮仓的会计在表格上写下一百公斤，旁边标注单位是公担。 The granary clerk wrote one hundred kilograms in the column and marked the unit as a quintal.
sceneCN: 这里 quintal 指公担（第 1 个义项：一百公斤的重量单位）；句意为粮仓的会计在表格上写下一百公斤，旁边标注单位是公担。

pos.zh: 公担；英担；谷物计量单位

senses.title: A metric quintal
senses.definition: a hundred kilograms, used in metric trade
senses.definitionCN: 公制贸易中使用的一百公斤
senses.example: The granary clerk wrote one hundred kilograms in the column and marked the unit as a quintal.
senses.exampleCN: 粮仓的会计在表格上写下一百公斤，并在旁边标注单位是公担。
senses.why: The first sense is the modern metric unit.
senses.whyCN: 第一个义项是现代的公制单位。

senses.title: An imperial quintal
senses.definition: about a hundred and twelve pounds, the old hundredweight
senses.definitionCN: 约一百一十二磅，即旧的英担
senses.example: The old ledger still measured wool by the imperial quintal.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧账仍以英制英担计量羊毛。
senses.why: The same word covers a slightly heavier unit.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词覆盖了一个稍重的单位。

senses.title: A Spanish quintal
senses.definition: a Spanish unit of about forty-six kilograms
senses.definitionCN: 西班牙约四十六公斤的单位
senses.example: The Spanish quintal was roughly half the metric one.
senses.exampleCN: 西班牙公担大约是公制公担的一半。
senses.why: Local meanings made the word dangerous in trade.
senses.whyCN: 地方性的含义让这个词在贸易中很危险。

senses.title: A Portuguese quintal
senses.definition: a Portuguese unit of about fifty-nine kilograms
senses.definitionCN: 葡萄牙约五十九公斤的单位
senses.example: The Portuguese quintal varied by region until it was fixed.
senses.exampleCN: 葡萄牙公担在固定之前因地区而异。
senses.why: The word records how weights travelled badly.
senses.whyCN: 这个词记录了重量单位怎样在传播中走样。

senses.title: Quintals of grain
senses.definition: a way of counting harvests in bulk
senses.definitionCN: 以整批方式计算收成的方法
senses.example: The mill bought grain by the quintal, not by the sack.
senses.exampleCN: 磨坊按公担买谷物，而不是按麻袋。
senses.why: The plural is the usual commercial form.
senses.whyCN: 复数形式是常见的商业用法。

senses.title: A price per quintal
senses.definition: a quoted price for each hundred kilograms
senses.definitionCN: 每百公斤的报价
senses.example: The price per quintal doubled after the poor harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 歉收之后，每公担的价格翻了一倍。
senses.why: Commodity markets still quote in this unit.
senses.whyCN: 大宗商品市场仍以这个单位报价。

senses.title: A historical weight
senses.definition: one of many old units that preceded the metric system
senses.definitionCN: 公制之前众多旧单位之一
senses.example: Historians convert the quintal before comparing two markets.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家在比较两个市场之前会先换算公担。
senses.why: The sense is about the history of measurement.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项关乎度量衡的历史。

senses.title: Versus hundredweight
senses.definition: the metric hundred kilos, as opposed to the imperial hundred and twelve pounds
senses.definitionCN: 公制的一百公斤，与英制的一百一十二磅相对
senses.example: A quintal is round; a hundredweight is not.
senses.exampleCN: 公担是整数，英担却不是。
senses.why: The pair separates two systems that share a name in part.
senses.whyCN: 这一对词把两个部分同名的体系分开。

intro.en: Quintal comes from Latin centenarius, 'of a hundred', through Arabic and Spanish.
intro.cn: quintal 经阿拉伯语与西班牙语，源自拉丁语 centenarius（百的）。

items.en: Centum was the Latin word for a hundred.
items.cn: centum 是拉丁语里的「一百」。

items.en: Arabic qintar named a hundred-pound weight.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 qintar 指百磅重。

items.en: Spanish took the word and fixed a local weight.
items.cn: 西班牙语接收这个词并固定了本地重量。

items.en: English traders imported the unit with the goods.
items.cn: 英语商人随货物把单位一并引入。

items.en: The metric system redefined it as a hundred kilograms.
items.cn: 公制把它重新定义为一百公斤。

note.en: The look-alike group is the quint- family; the near-meaning group separates hundredweight, tonne, bushel and stone.
note.cn: 形近组是 quint 词族；近义组把「英担」「公吨」「蒲式耳」「英石」分开。

entries.definition: a group of five.
entries.definitionCN: 五人一组。

entries.definition: a set of five.
entries.definitionCN: 五个一组。

entries.definition: one of five statistical cuts.
entries.definitionCN: 统计上的五个切点之一。

entries.definition: one of five born together.
entries.definitionCN: 五胞胎之一。

entries.definition: about 112 pounds in Britain.
entries.definitionCN: 英国约一百一十二磅。

entries.definition: a metric ton of 1000 kilograms.
entries.definitionCN: 一千公斤的公吨。

entries.definition: a dry measure of grain.
entries.definitionCN: 谷物的干量单位。

entries.definition: fourteen pounds of weight.
entries.definitionCN: 十四磅的重量。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a sack on a scale stopping at a round number.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一只麻袋在磅秤上停在整数刻度」的画面。

normal.en: Quintal hides centum, hundred: it is the hundred-kilo unit.
normal.cn: quintal 藏着 centum（百）：它就是百公斤单位。

normal.en: Picture a grain sack lifted by a hook and a pointer at 100.
normal.cn: 想象一只谷物袋被钩子吊起，指针停在 100。

normal.en: Say KWIN-tl; the last syllable is barely heard.
normal.cn: 读 KWIN-tl，最后一个音节几乎听不见。

normal.en: The same word meant different weights in different countries.
normal.cn: 同一个词在不同国家指不同的重量。

normal.en: It is a trade word: prices are quoted per quintal, not per bag.
normal.cn: 这是个贸易词：报价按公担，而不是按袋。

abstract.en: A quintal is a hundred kilos pretending to be a natural unit.
abstract.cn: 公担是一百公斤在假装成一个自然的单位。

abstract.en: Every unit hides a decision about what to count and for whom.
abstract.cn: 每个单位都藏着一个决定：数什么，为谁数。

abstract.en: The word's history shows how trade smooths differences and then forgets them.
abstract.cn: 这个词的历史显示，贸易抹平差异，然后忘记差异。

examples.en: The mill bought grain by the quintal, not by the sack.
examples.cn: 磨坊按公担买谷物，而不是按麻袋。

examples.en: The price per quintal doubled after the poor harvest.
examples.cn: 歉收之后，每公担的价格翻了一倍。

examples.en: Historians convert the quintal before comparing two markets.
examples.cn: 历史学家在比较两个市场之前会先换算公担。

dict_mnemonic.text: quint（五）音近 centum（百）：一百公斤的一担。

root: 拉丁语 centum（百）→ 阿拉伯语 qintar → 西班牙语 quintal

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses weigh the same unit across systems: metric, imperial, Spanish, Portuguese, grain, price, history and the contrast with hundredweight.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项称量同一个单位在不同体系里的样子：公制、英制、西班牙、葡萄牙、谷物、价格、历史，以及与英担的对照。

core.en: A SACK STOPPING AT ONE HUNDRED
core.cn: 停在「一百」的麻袋

branches.en: The metric and imperial readings of one word.
branches.cn: 同一个词的公制与英制读数。

branches.en: Local weights that made trade uncertain.
branches.cn: 让贸易变得不确定的地方重量。

branches.en: Bulk counting and quoted prices.
branches.cn: 整批计数与报价。

branches.en: The unit as a historical object.
branches.cn: 作为历史对象的单位。

branches.en: A round hundred set against an odd hundredweight.
branches.cn: 整数的一百与零碎的英担相对。

intro.en: The quint- family counts to five in music and statistics, though quintal itself counts to a hundred through an older root.
intro.cn: quint 词族在音乐与统计里数到五，不过 quintal 本身通过更古老的词根数到一百。

latinIntro.en: Centum, 'hundred', became qintar in Arabic and quintal in Spanish; the spelling changed more than the meaning did.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 centum（百）在阿拉伯语变成 qintar，在西班牙语变成 quintal；拼写的变化大过词义的变化。

definition_zh: 代数的；用代数方法的；由代数符号表示的
definition_en: relating to algebra or to its methods; expressed or solved by means of symbols rather than by arithmetic
core_image: 纸上一个未知量被圈出，四周的项被依次搬到等号另一边，符号像被搬动的棋子
scene: 草稿纸上一个未知量被圈住，四周的项被逐项搬到等号另一边，符号像被搬动的棋子。 The relation is algebraic, so it can be rearranged without knowing any of the numbers.
sceneCN: 这里 algebraic 指「属于代数的、用代数符号处理的」（第 1 个义项：与代数方法相关）；句意为这个关系是代数式的，不必知道任何具体数字就能变形。图中可辨识物件：草稿纸、圈出的未知量、等号、搬动的项。

pos.zh: 代数的；用代数方法的；代数符号表示的

senses.title: Belonging to algebra
senses.definition: relating to algebra as a branch of mathematics
senses.definitionCN: 与作为数学分支的代数有关
senses.example: The relation is algebraic, so it can be rearranged without knowing any of the numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个关系是代数式的，不必知道任何具体数字就能变形。
senses.why: The plainest reading attaches the branch's name to whatever is described.
senses.whyCN: 最朴素的用法把分支之名挂到所描述的对象上。

senses.title: Written in symbols
senses.definition: expressed by letters and signs instead of by worked-out numbers
senses.definitionCN: 用字母与记号表达，而非用算好的数字表达
senses.example: She rewrote the sentence as an algebraic expression.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那句话改写成一个代数式。
senses.why: Whatever is put into symbolic form takes the adjective, because the symbols are the visible mark of the branch.
senses.whyCN: 凡被写成符号形式的东西都带这个形容词，因为符号是这门分支的可见标记。

senses.title: Solvable by root extraction
senses.definition: describing an equation that can be solved by the operations of algebra, as opposed to one needing new kinds of numbers
senses.definitionCN: 描述可用代数运算求解的方程，以区别于需要新数类的方程
senses.example: Every quadratic equation is algebraic, but not every equation is.
senses.exampleCN: 每个二次方程都是代数可解的，但并非每个方程都如此。
senses.why: Historians of the subject needed a word for the solvable class, and the branch's name supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 这门学问的史家需要一个词来指「可解」的那一类，分支之名便提供了它。

senses.title: Of a root of a polynomial
senses.definition: describing a number that is a root of a polynomial with whole-number coefficients
senses.definitionCN: 描述作为整系数多项式之根的数目
senses.example: The square root of two is algebraic, though it is not a fraction.
senses.exampleCN: 二的平方根是代数数，尽管它不是分数。
senses.why: This technical sense sorts numbers by how they can be reached from whole numbers.
senses.whyCN: 这一技术义按「能否由整数到达」来给数分类。

senses.title: Of a formal structure
senses.definition: describing a set with operations that obey stated rules, studied as an object in itself
senses.definitionCN: 描述一个带有满足既定规则的运算的集合，被当作对象研究
senses.example: A ring is an algebraic structure with two operations.
senses.exampleCN: 环是一种带两个运算的代数结构。
senses.why: Modern mathematics treats rules themselves as objects, and the adjective marks that level of abstraction.
senses.whyCN: 现代数学把规则本身当作对象，这个形容词标记那一抽象层次。

senses.title: Of a branch built on algebra
senses.titleCN: 代数几何、代数拓扑等分支的
senses.definition: used in the names of fields that combine algebra with geometry or topology
senses.definitionCN: 用于代数与几何或拓扑结合而成的领域名称
senses.example: She works in algebraic geometry, where shapes are described by equations.
senses.exampleCN: 她研究代数几何，那里用方程描述形状。
senses.why: When a field joins two subjects, the name of the contributing branch becomes its modifier.
senses.whyCN: 当一个领域结合两门学问时，贡献方之名便成为它的修饰语。

senses.title: Abstract to the point of symbols
senses.titleCN: 抽象到只剩符号的（比喻）
senses.definition: used of reasoning so abstract that it seems to be only manipulation of signs
senses.definitionCN: 描述抽象到仿佛只在摆弄记号、别无其他的推理
senses.example: His explanation was too algebraic for the committee to follow.
senses.exampleCN: 他的解释过于代数化，委员会跟不上。
senses.why: The figurative use criticises work that keeps the form of algebra while losing its connection to anything concrete.
senses.whyCN: 比喻用法批评那种保留了代数外形、却与具体事物脱节的做法。

senses.title: Treatable by symbolic manipulation
senses.definition: capable of being handled by rearranging symbols according to rules
senses.definitionCN: 能够按规则重排符号来处理的
senses.example: Once the problem became algebraic, a machine could rearrange it overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 问题一旦变成代数形式，机器就能连夜把它重排。
senses.why: Anything reducible to symbols can be processed without knowing the values, which is the practical power the adjective marks.
senses.whyCN: 凡可化为符号者都能在不取值的情况下被处理，这正是这个形容词所标的实用力量。

intro.en: The adjective is the borrowed Arabic noun plus a Latin adjectival ending, formed in European Latin before English used it. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是借入的阿拉伯语名词加拉丁形容词词尾，先在欧洲拉丁语中构成，后为英语所用。年代均为约数。

items.en: The Arabic noun meant a reunion or restoration of broken parts, and named the operation of completing a deficient side of an equation.
items.cn: 这个阿拉伯名词意为把破碎部分接回或复原，并指把方程中不足的一边补齐的操作。

items.en: Twelfth-century translators brought the word into Latin as algebra, where it named the technique of restoring and balancing.
items.cn: 十二世纪译者把它作为 algebra 带入拉丁语，指补全与平衡的技术。

items.en: The adjectival suffix -icus, inherited from Greek -ikos, was added to the borrowed stem to make a describing word.
items.cn: 形容词后缀 -icus 承自希腊语，被加到借来的词干上以构成描述词。

items.en: Scholars formed the adjective in Latin before it appeared in English, so the word came in already built.
items.cn: 学者先在拉丁语中构成这个形容词，然后才进入英语，因此它是整体借入的。

items.en: English uses the adjective for equations, expressions, structures and numbers, always attaching it to something the branch can describe.
items.cn: 英语把这个形容词用于方程、式子、结构与数，总是挂到这门分支所能描述的对象上。

items.en: In modern mathematics it also marks the class of numbers and equations reachable by algebraic operations. First date uncertain: this narrowing developed gradually, with no agreed first citation.
items.cn: 在现代数学中，它还标记可由代数运算到达的那一类数与方程。首见年代不确定：这一收窄是逐渐形成的，没有公认的最早书证。

note.en: Group one separates the adjective from words of the same family; group two separates other adjectives of method.
note.cn: 第一组辨析这个形容词与其同族词；第二组辨析其他表示方法的形容词。

entries.definition: The branch itself; the adjective differs only by its ending, which is easy to overlook in a quick scan.
entries.definitionCN: 指分支本身；形容词只差词尾，快速扫读时容易忽略。

entries.definition: A worker in the branch; the ending marks a person rather than a property.
entries.definitionCN: 指该分支的工作者；词尾标出人而非性质。

entries.definition: An older and longer adjective found in older texts; modern usage prefers the shorter form.
entries.definitionCN: 见于较早文献的更长形容词；现代用法多用较短形式。

entries.definition: From the scholar's name rather than from the noun for reunion: it describes procedures, not symbol systems.
entries.definitionCN: 来自那位学者的名字而非表示接回的名词：它描述步骤，而非符号系统。

entries.definition: Describes anything that stands for something else; algebraic work is symbolic, but symbolic work need not be algebra.
entries.definitionCN: 描述任何以某物代表另一物的东西；代数工作是符号性的，但符号性工作未必是代数。

entries.definition: Describes work done with actual values, the opposite of keeping everything in letters.
entries.definitionCN: 描述用实际数值所做的工作，与把一切留在字母里相反。

entries.definition: Describes work that follows stated rules of symbol manipulation regardless of interpretation.
entries.definitionCN: 描述按既定符号操作规则进行、不问解释的工作。

entries.definition: Describes what is separated from particular cases; algebraic structures are abstract, though not every abstract thing is algebraic.
entries.definitionCN: 描述与具体事例脱开之物；代数结构是抽象的，但并非每个抽象物都是代数的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The adjective is the branch's borrowed name plus a Latin ending, so it marks whatever the branch can describe.
normal.cn: 这个形容词是分支借来的名称加拉丁词尾，因此标记这门分支所能描述的一切。

normal.en: Its home phrases are equation, expression, structure and number, four things the branch handles.
normal.cn: 它的常用搭配是方程、式子、结构与数，正是这门分支处理的四样东西。

normal.en: The family runs algebraic, algebra, algebraically, algebraist, and the older algebraical.
normal.cn: 同族词包括代数的、代数、用代数方法、代数学家，以及更旧的形容词形式。

normal.en: Algebraic numbers are those reachable from whole numbers by polynomial equations, which is a boundary rather than a compliment.
normal.cn: 代数数指能由整数经多项式方程到达的数；这是一条界线，而不是一句称赞。

normal.en: The word can also dismiss an argument: too algebraic means correct in form but empty of meaning.
normal.cn: 这个词也可用来否定一个论证：太代数化意味着形式正确却空洞。

abstract.en: Picture chess pieces moved by rule alone, with no board and no opponent.
abstract.cn: 想象棋子只按规则移动，却没有棋盘也没有对手。

abstract.en: Picture a letter standing in for a name that nobody has yet been told.
abstract.cn: 想象一个字母代替一个还没人被告知的名字。

abstract.en: Picture a lock made of symbols, opening only when the signs are shifted in the right order.
abstract.cn: 想象一把由符号构成的锁，只有按正确次序搬动记号才打开。

examples.en: The two quantities are linked by a simple algebraic relation.
examples.cn: 这两个量由一个简单的代数关系连起来。

examples.en: Students translate word problems into algebraic form.
examples.cn: 学生把应用题转成代数形式。

examples.en: Algebraic methods settled the question without any measurement.
examples.cn: 代数方法无需任何测量就解决了这个问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 记作「接回碎块的」：阿拉伯语名词加拉丁形容词尾巴 → 代数的

root: 阿拉伯 al-jabr「接回、复原」经中世纪拉丁 algebra 进入欧洲，加拉丁形容词后缀 -icus 构成；英语整体借入，用于方程、式子、结构与数，并在现代数学中收窄出「代数可解」与「代数数」等技术义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses radiate from one adjective: belonging to the branch, written in symbols, solvable by its operations, describing algebraic numbers, naming formal structures, modifying sister fields, sounding emptily abstract, and reducible to rule-governed rewriting.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个形容词辐射开：属于该分支、写成符号、可由其运算求解、描述代数数、命名形式结构、修饰姊妹领域、听起来空洞抽象，以及可化为按规则重写。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one circled unknown, with the surrounding terms carried across an equal sign like chess pieces.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个被圈出的未知量，四周的项像棋子一样被搬到等号另一边。

branches.en: The branch and its writing: whatever is put into letters belongs to algebra.
branches.cn: 分支与写法：凡被写成字母者都属于代数。

branches.en: Reachability: equations that its operations can solve, and numbers that its polynomials can reach.
branches.cn: 可到达性：其运算能解的方程，与其多项式能到达的数。

branches.en: Rules as objects: a structure studied for itself, and any problem reducible to rewriting.

latinIntro.cn: 阿拉伯语名词提供意义，拉丁后缀提供词类，英语只添了读音。

definition_zh: 模仿；仿制品；赝品；仿冒
definition_en: the act of copying someone or something, or a copy made in this way
core_image: 一个人对着一面旧铜镜，把镜中人的动作一笔一笔描下来
scene: 博物馆商店里，一只古代陶俑被做成巴掌大的钥匙扣，价签上写明依照原件比例缩小复制。 The label described the key ring as an imitation of the original figurine.
sceneCN: 这里 imitation 指「照原件做出的复制品」（第 3 个义项：物品的复制品）；句意为价签把这个钥匙扣称作原件小雕像的仿制品。

pos.zh: 模仿；仿制品；赝品；仿冒（可数或不可数）

derivatives.zh: 模仿的；仿效的（由模仿词干加形容词后缀，表示具有模仿性质）
模仿者（由模仿词干加表示人的后缀，语义从行为落到人身上）
以模仿的方式（由 imitative 加副词后缀，把仿效性质转成动作方式）
模仿性（由 imitative 加名词后缀，指仿效的倾向或性质）

senses.title: The act of copying behaviour
senses.definition: the act of doing what another person or thing does
senses.definitionCN: 照着别人或别物去做的行为
senses.example: Children learn much of their speech by imitation.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童很大一部分语言是通过模仿学会的。
senses.why: Imitation starts with the eye: a model is taken in, and the hand or voice repeats it.
senses.whyCN: 模仿从眼睛开始：先接收一个样板，再由手或声音把它重复出来。

senses.title: Mimicry of a person
senses.definition: a performance that copies someone's voice, manner or appearance
senses.definitionCN: 复制某人嗓音、举止或外表的表演
senses.example: His imitation of the teacher made the whole class laugh.
senses.exampleCN: 他对老师的模仿让全班都笑了。
senses.why: Here the copy is aimed at a person's style rather than at a thing, and the aim is often amusement.
senses.whyCN: 这里的复制对象是一个人的风格而不是物件，目的常常是好笑。

senses.title: A copy of an object
senses.definition: a thing made to look like another thing, often at a smaller scale
senses.definitionCN: 做成与另一件东西相像的物品，常常按比例缩小
senses.example: The shop sells imitations of the museum's ancient figurines.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店出售博物馆古代小雕像的复制品。
senses.why: The copy now exists as a separate object beside the original, with its own price and its own label.
senses.whyCN: 复制品现在作为独立物件存在于原件旁边，有自己的价格和自己的标签。

senses.title: Counterfeit goods
senses.definition: a cheap copy made to be mistaken for an expensive original
senses.definitionCN: 廉价复制、用来冒充昂贵原件的赝品
senses.example: Customs officers found boxes of imitation handbags.
senses.exampleCN: 海关人员查获了几箱仿冒手提包。
senses.why: The copy now hides its own origin; it does not stand beside the original but tries to take its place.
senses.whyCN: 复制品这时藏起了自己的出身；它不是站在原件旁边，而是想取代原件。

senses.title: Imitation as learning
senses.definition: in psychology, copying as a way of acquiring a skill or behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中，通过复制来习得技能或行为的方式
senses.example: The study measured imitation in infants watching an adult use a tool.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究测量了婴儿观看成人使用工具时的模仿行为。
senses.why: Repetition is how a body learns: the learner copies first and understands later.
senses.whyCN: 重复是身体学习的方式：学习者先复制，之后再理解。

senses.title: Artistic mimesis
senses.definition: in art theory, the representation of nature or life by imitation
senses.definitionCN: 艺术理论中，通过模仿来再现自然或生活
senses.example: The debate over imitation in art goes back to the ancient Greeks.
senses.exampleCN: 关于艺术摹仿的争论可以追溯到古希腊。
senses.why: Art holds a mirror to the world; the copy is not a fake but a way of representing what is real.
senses.whyCN: 艺术给世界举了一面镜子；这里的复制不是造假，而是再现真实的一种方式。

senses.title: Social imitation
senses.definition: the copying of others' behaviour, fashion or habits across a group
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体里对他人行为、时尚或习惯的复制
senses.example: Fashion spreads through social imitation more than through advertising.
senses.exampleCN: 时尚更多靠社会性模仿传播，而不是靠广告。
senses.why: People copy in order to belong; the model is chosen because it looks like the group one wants to join.
senses.whyCN: 人们模仿是为了归属；选择这个样板，是因为它像自己想加入的那个群体。

senses.title: In imitation of; the proverb
senses.definition: used in the phrase in imitation of and in the saying that imitation is the sincerest form of flattery
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示「仿照」的固定说法，也见于谚语「模仿是最真诚的恭维」
senses.example: The hall was built in imitation of a Roman bath.
senses.exampleCN: 这座大厅是仿照罗马浴场建造的。
senses.why: The phrase turns copying into a method, and the proverb turns it into praise: to copy someone well is to say they are worth copying.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把复制变成一种方法，谚语则把它变成赞美：把一个人模仿得好，等于说这个人值得被模仿。

intro.en: Imitation came into English around 1400 from Old French imitacion, from Latin imitationem, the noun of action from imitari 'to copy, portray'. The word first named the act and only later the object.
intro.cn: imitation 在十五世纪初从古法语 imitacion 进入英语，源自拉丁语 imitationem，是 imitari「模仿、描摹」的动名词。这个词先指行为，后来才指物品。

items.en: Imitari meant 'to copy, portray, imitate'. Its past-participle stem imitat- supplies the base of the English noun and its relatives.
items.cn: imitari 意为「模仿、描摹、仿效」。它的过去分词词干提供了英语名词及其同族词的词基。

items.en: The action noun imitatio (genitive imitationis) meant 'a copying, imitation'. English took the accusative form imitationem through French.
items.cn: 动作名词 imitatio（属格 imitationis）意为「复制、模仿」。英语经法语借入的是它的宾格形式 imitationem。

items.en: Old French imitacion carried the Latin noun into medieval French, and from there into English around 1400.
items.cn: 古法语 imitacion 把这个拉丁名词带进中世纪法语，又大约在十五世纪初进入英语。

items.en: The first English sense was 'emulation; act of copying'; the meaning 'an artificial likeness' is recorded only from around 1600.
items.cn: 英语最早的义项是「争胜、复制的动作」；而「人造的相似物」这一意思直到约十六世纪末才有记录。

items.en: Modern English uses the noun for copies, counterfeits, artistic mimesis and social copying; the adjective imitation is recorded from the nineteenth century, as in imitation leather.
items.cn: 现代英语用这个名词指复制品、赝品、艺术摹仿和社会性模仿；形容词用法从十九世纪起有记录，如「人造革」这一说法。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of imitari is not settled. Some accounts connect it with imago 'image, likeness', while others reconstruct a PIE root *aim- 'to copy'; both are proposals, and neither can be demonstrated as the single source.
items.cn: 来源不确定：imitari 更深来源尚无定论。一些解释把它与 imago「图像、相似物」联系起来，另一些则重构原始印欧语词根 *aim-「复制」；两者都是假说，都无法被证明是唯一来源。

note.en: The first group holds words that look or sound close and are often mixed up with imitation; the second holds near neighbours that also name a copy, but with a different purpose.
note.cn: 第一组是与 imitation 形近或音近、常被混淆的词；第二组是同为「复制品」但目的不同的近义词。

entries.definition: The verb at the base of the family: to copy someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 这一词族的动词基础：复制某人或某物。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'copying or tending to copy'; it describes the tendency, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「模仿的、倾向于模仿的」形容词；它描写倾向，而不是行为本身。

entries.definition: A restriction, from Latin limes 'boundary'. It rhymes with imitation but comes from a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 限制，来自拉丁 limes「边界」。它与 imitation 押韵，但词根完全不同，两者并非同源。

entries.definition: A hint or indirect suggestion, from intimate 'to make known'. The shared ending is misleading.
entries.definitionCN: 暗示、间接提示，来自 intimate「使知道」。共同的词尾具有误导性，两者没有亲缘关系。

entries.definition: A general duplicate of an original; it carries no hint of deception or artistic theory.
entries.definitionCN: 原件的普通复制品；它不带欺骗或艺术理论的意味。

entries.definition: An exact copy, often made at the same scale and with official approval; it is more precise than imitation.
entries.definitionCN: 精确复制品，常按原尺寸并获正式许可；比 imitation 更精确。

entries.definition: A fake made to pass as genuine, especially money or goods; deception is built into the word.
entries.definitionCN: 冒充真品的假货，尤指钱币或商品；欺骗性写进了这个词本身。

entries.definition: The copying of another's appearance or behaviour, often for advantage; in biology it can help an animal survive.
entries.definitionCN: 复制他者的外表或行为，常为取得优势；在生物学中可帮助动物生存。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词语素、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: imit- (copy) + -ation (action noun): imitation is literally 'the act of copying'.
normal.cn: 复制词干加动作名词词尾：imitation 字面上就是「复制的动作」。

normal.en: Latin imitari 'to copy' and imitatio 'a copying' are the direct sources of the word.
normal.cn: 拉丁 imitari「复制」与 imitatio「复制行为」是这个词的直接来源。

normal.en: The family runs imitate, imitation, imitative, imitator, imitatively.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 imitate、imitation、imitative、imitator、imitatively。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the purpose: in imitation of, imitation leather, imitation goods, imitation learning.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出目的：仿照、人造革、仿冒商品、模仿学习。

normal.en: The saying that imitation is the sincerest form of flattery is a fixed proverb, not a separate root meaning.
normal.cn: 「模仿是最真诚的恭维」是一句固定谚语，并不是词根另长出的意思。

abstract.en: Picture a hand tracing the outline of a shadow on a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在墙上描出影子的轮廓。

abstract.en: Picture a copy that wants to be mistaken for the original.
abstract.cn: 想象一个希望被误认为原件的复制品。

abstract.en: Picture a child learning a knot by watching the same hands three times.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子看着同一双手打了三次结，才学会这个结。

examples.en: Young children learn language partly by imitation.
examples.cn: 幼儿部分通过模仿学习语言。

examples.en: The vase is a nineteenth-century imitation of a Greek original.
examples.cn: 这只花瓶是十九世纪对一件希腊原件的仿制品。

examples.en: His imitation of the manager's voice was painfully accurate.
examples.cn: 他对经理嗓音的模仿准确得让人尴尬。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊米泰申」—— 伊米对着镜子学泰申的动作，越学越像 → imitation 模仿；仿制品

root: 拉丁 imitari「模仿、复制」，经古法语 imitacion 于十五世纪初进入英语。imitari 更深来源不确定：与 imago「图像」的联系属假说，重构词根 *aim-「复制」也只是提议，均无法定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one copying gesture: look, repeat, and make a double. The double can be a performance, a replica, a fake, a learned skill, a work of art, a social habit, or a phrase that turns copying into praise.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都沿同一个复制动作展开：看、重复、做出一个「另一个」。这个「另一个」可以是一场表演、一件复制品、一件假货、一项学来的技能、一件艺术品、一种社会习惯，或一句把复制变成赞美的固定说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an eye takes a model, and the hand makes a second version.
core.cn: 核心意象：眼睛接收一个样板，手做出第二个版本。

branches.en: THE CORE: the act begins with a model outside the self and ends with a repeated action.
branches.cn: 核心：动作从一个自我之外的样板开始，以一次重复的行动结束。

branches.en: THE DOUBLE AS PERFORMANCE: the copy is aimed at a person's voice or manner and often played for laughter.
branches.cn: 作为表演的「另一个」：复制对象是一个人的嗓音或举止，常常是为了逗笑。

branches.en: TWO KINDS OF OBJECT: a replica stands openly beside the original, while a counterfeit tries to take its place.
branches.cn: 两类物件：复制品公开地站在原件旁边，赝品则想取代原件。

branches.en: COPYING AS GROWTH: imitation lets a body learn a skill and lets a group share a habit.
branches.cn: 作为成长的复制：模仿让身体学会技能，也让群体共享习惯。

branches.en: THE DOUBLE IN CULTURE AND LANGUAGE: mimesis holds a mirror to nature, while a fixed phrase turns copying into a method and a proverb turns it into praise.
branches.cn: 文化与语言里的「另一个」：摹仿给自然举镜子，固定短语把复制变成方法，谚语则把它变成赞美。

intro.en: Imitation is a Latin action noun: a copying stem plus a very common noun ending, and the family spreads through verb, adjective, person and adverb forms.
intro.cn: imitation 是拉丁动作名词：复制词干加一个极常见的名词词尾，词族再向动词、形容词、人物名词和副词扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is compact: a verb for copying, its action noun, and its past participle. English built the rest from the imitat- stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁这一族很紧凑：一个表示复制的动词、它的动作名词和过去分词。英语其余的形式都从这个过去分词词干长出来。

items.example: The stem carries the act of copying.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干承载着复制的动作。

items.meaning: the act or result of doing something
items.example: The ending turns the verb into a noun of action.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变成动作名词。

items.meaning: the act of copying; a copy
items.example: The museum sells imitations.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆出售复制品。

items.example: Children imitate what they hear.
items.exampleCN: 孩子会模仿听到的东西。

items.example: The style is highly imitative.
items.exampleCN: 这种风格模仿性很强。

items.example: He is a skilled imitator of voices.
items.exampleCN: 他是个擅长模仿嗓音的人。

items.example: The child imitatively repeated the gesture.
items.exampleCN: 孩子模仿着重复了那个动作。

items.example: Researchers rated the imitativeness of each child.
items.exampleCN: 研究者评估了每个孩子的模仿性。

items.meaningCN: 无法模仿的；独一无二的
items.example: She has an inimitable way of telling a story.
items.exampleCN: 她讲故事的方式无人能仿。

definition_zh: 可持续的；可长期维持的；（不耗尽资源而）能长期继续的；长期可行的
definition_en: able to be continued over the long term without destroying or exhausting the resources or conditions it depends on
core_image: 一只渔篓只取走水面一层鱼，留下大部分鱼群继续繁殖，旁边的日历翻过一年又一年
scene: 这里指「可持续的」。 The project aims for sustainable growth rather than a short-term boom.
sceneCN: 这里 sustainable 是「可持续增长」（第 3 个义项：增长不以透支未来为代价）；句意：该项目追求可持续增长，而不是短期繁荣。图中可辨识物件：渔篓、鱼群、逐年翻过的日历、缓缓上升的曲线、没有断裂的阶梯。

pos.zh: 可持续的；可长期维持的；（环境）不耗尽资源的；长期可行的

derivatives.zh: 可持续性（sustainable + -ity「性质」，语义由形容词偏移为抽象名词）
维持；支撑（源自古法语 sustenir = 拉丁 sustinere「自下托住」）
食物；生计（sustain + -ance「……之物」，由「支撑」偏移为「维持生命之物」）

senses.title: Kind to the environment
senses.titleCN: 环境上可持续的：不破坏、不耗尽自然
senses.definition: describing an activity or product that can continue without destroying or exhausting the natural environment it depends on
senses.definitionCN: 描述一种能够持续进行、而不破坏或耗尽所依赖的自然环境的活动或产品
senses.example: The factory switched to sustainable energy sources.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂改用可持续的能源。
senses.why: This is the modern headline sense: the word promises that a practice will not consume its own base. The Latin picture of holding up from below becomes the environment holding up the activity.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最显眼的义项：该词承诺一种做法不会消耗自身根基。拉丁语「自下托住」的画面变成环境托住这项活动。

senses.title: A rate or level that can be kept up
senses.titleCN: 可长期维持的速率或水平
senses.definition: describing a speed, level or pace that can be continued over time without falling or collapsing
senses.definitionCN: 描述一种可以长期保持、不致下滑或崩溃的速度、水平或节奏
senses.example: The team set a sustainable pace for the long climb.
senses.exampleCN: 团队为漫长的攀登设定了一个可持续的节奏。
senses.why: Here the word is applied to quantities: a pace is sustainable if the body or the budget can repeat it. The test is whether the rate outlasts the effort.
senses.whyCN: 这里该词用于数量：只要身体或预算能重复执行，节奏就是可持续的。检验标准是速率能否比努力更长久。

senses.title: Growth that does not overheat
senses.titleCN: 可持续增长：不过热、不透支的增长
senses.definition: describing economic or organizational growth that can continue without overheating, crashing or consuming its own future
senses.definitionCN: 描述能够持续进行、而不致过热、崩溃或消耗自身未来的经济或组织增长
senses.example: Analysts welcomed the shift toward sustainable growth.
senses.exampleCN: 分析师欢迎向可持续增长的转变。
senses.why: Economists use the word for expansion that stays within real limits of credit, labor and demand. A boom is fast; sustainable growth is fast enough to last.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家用该词指停留在信贷、劳动力与需求真实限度内的扩张。繁荣是快的；可持续增长则是快得能持久。

senses.title: Farming that protects the soil
senses.titleCN: 可持续农业：保护土壤与水源的耕作
senses.definition: describing agricultural methods that preserve soil, water and biodiversity while producing food over the long term
senses.definitionCN: 描述在长期产粮的同时保住土壤、水源与生物多样性的农业方法
senses.example: Sustainable agriculture rotates crops to protect the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 可持续农业通过轮作来保护土壤。
senses.why: In farming the word measures the ground itself: a method is sustainable if the field still produces in fifty years. The image of holding up from below becomes literal topsoil.
senses.whyCN: 在农业中，该词以土地本身为尺度：一片田地五十年后仍能产出，方法才算可持续。「自下托住」的意象变成了字面上的表土。

senses.title: Materials and buildings with a light footprint
senses.titleCN: 可持续材料与建筑：低环境代价的建造
senses.definition: describing materials, products or buildings that can be produced, used and maintained with low environmental cost over their life cycle
senses.definitionCN: 描述在整个生命周期内能以较低环境代价被生产、使用与维护的材料、产品或建筑
senses.example: The architects chose sustainable timber for the frame.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑师为框架选择了可持续木材。
senses.why: In construction and design the adjective certifies a whole life cycle, from harvest to disposal. It is the environmental sense applied to things rather than activities.
senses.whyCN: 在建筑与设计中，该形容词为从采伐到废弃的整个生命周期作担保。这是环境义项从活动延伸到物品。

senses.title: A business model that survives
senses.definition: describing a business model or income source that can continue earning enough to operate over the long term
senses.definitionCN: 描述能够长期持续赚到足够运营收入的商业模式或收入来源
senses.example: A subscription model proved more sustainable than one-off sales.
senses.exampleCN: 订阅模式被证明比一次性销售更可持续。
senses.why: In business English the word is about survival without constant rescue: revenue must cover costs year after year. The system keeps itself going.
senses.whyCN: 在商业英语中，该词指无需不断救援而能生存：收入必须年复一年地覆盖成本。系统自己维持自己。

senses.title: A lifestyle a person can maintain
senses.definition: describing a habit, diet or way of living that a person can continue without burning out or giving up
senses.definitionCN: 描述一个人能够长期坚持、不致耗尽精力或放弃的习惯、饮食或生活方式
senses.example: The diet is sustainable because it allows occasional treats.
senses.exampleCN: 这种饮食法允许偶尔犒劳自己，所以能够坚持。
senses.why: Health and productivity writers apply the word to willpower: a plan is sustainable if the person can repeat it next month. The scale is one life, not the planet.
senses.whyCN: 健康与效率类作者把该词用在意志力上：一个人下个月还能照做的计划才是可持续的。尺度是一个人的生活，而不是整个地球。

senses.title: A harvest that does not deplete the stock
senses.titleCN: 可持续产量：不耗尽资源的采收
senses.definition: describing a harvest, catch or extraction level that removes no more than the resource can replace
senses.definitionCN: 描述移除量不超过资源再生量的采收、捕捞或开采水平
senses.example: The quota was set at a sustainable yield.
senses.exampleCN: 配额被定在可持续产量的水平上。
senses.why: Fisheries and forestry use the word for the maximum that can be taken forever: take the interest, keep the capital. It is the oldest precise sense of the modern environmental meaning.
senses.whyCN: 渔业与林业用该词指可永远采走的最大量：只取利息，保住本金。这是现代环境义项中最古老而精确的用法。

intro.en: Sustainable is sustain plus the adjective ending -able; sustain came through Old French sustenir from Latin sustinere, made of sub- 'from below' and tenere 'to hold, keep'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: sustainable 是 sustain 加形容词词尾 -able；sustain 经古法语 sustenir 源自拉丁 sustinere，由 sub-「自下」与 tenere「握住、保持」组成。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin sustinere 'to hold up from below, support, endure' was built on sub- 'from below' and tenere 'to hold, keep'. It already covered both physical support and enduring hardship.
items.cn: 拉丁 sustinere「自下托住、支撑、承受」由 sub-「自下」与 tenere「握住、保持」构成；它既有物理支撑义，也有忍受苦难义。

items.en: English took sustain through Old French sustenir in the medieval period, with the meanings 'to keep in being, maintain, provide for'.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪经古法语 sustenir 借入 sustain，义为「使存续、维持、供养」。

items.en: Sustainable was formed on sustain with -able; in the seventeenth century it meant 'able to be supported or maintained', used of arguments, weights and provisions. Its first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: sustainable 由 sustain 加 -able 构成；十七世纪时义为「可被支撑或维持的」，用于论证、重物与给养。其最早书证年代存疑。

items.en: The environmental sense arose in the 1970s and 1980s, and the phrase sustainable development became a global policy term after the 1987 Brundtland report.
items.cn: 环境义项在二十世纪七八十年代兴起；sustainable development 一词在 1987 年《布伦特兰报告》后成为全球政策用语。

items.en: Economics and engineering fixed the modern range of the adjective: sustainable growth, sustainable yield, sustainable energy, sustainable materials.
items.cn: 经济学与工程学固定了该形容词的现代义域：可持续增长、可持续产量、可持续能源、可持续材料。

items.en: The exact first English citation of sustainable is uncertain. The deeper root of tenere is generally taken to be reconstructed Indo-European *ten- 'to stretch, hold', a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：sustainable 的英语最早书证年代不确定。tenere 的更深词根一般认为是重构的印欧语 *ten-「伸展、保持」，属重构形式，而非有记录的真实词形。

note.en: The first group separates the sustain family by part of speech; the second contrasts sustainable with near-synonyms, since sustainable stresses not exhausting resources and lasting over the long term.
note.cn: 第一组按词性区分 sustain 词族；第二组将 sustainable 与近义词对照，因为 sustainable 强调不耗尽资源、可长期维持。

entries.definition: Continuous over a period. Sustained describes effort that went on; sustainable asks whether it can go on without damage.
entries.definitionCN: 指持续的；sustained 描述确实持续下去的努力，sustainable 追问它能否无损害地继续。

entries.definition: The verb of keeping something going. Sustainable is the adjective formed on it with -able.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，指维持某物；sustainable 是它加 -able 构成的形容词。

entries.definition: The concrete means of staying alive. Sustainable describes the quality of a practice, not the food itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指维持生命的具体手段；sustainable 描述做法的性质，而非食物本身。

entries.definition: The abstract noun. Sustainable is the quality; sustainability is the name of the quality and of the movement.
entries.definitionCN: 抽象名词；sustainable 是性质，sustainability 是这一性质及其运动的名称。

entries.definition: Able to be kept in working order. Maintained implies constant input and care; sustainable implies the system can go on without exhausting itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指可保持良好运转；maintained 隐含需要不断投入与维护，sustainable 隐含系统能不耗尽自身而继续。

entries.definition: Able to work or succeed. Viable is about feasibility now; sustainable adds the demand that it last without damage.
entries.definitionCN: 指能行得通、能成功；viable 关乎眼下可行，sustainable 还要求无损害地长久延续。

entries.definition: Able to be replenished by natural processes. Renewable describes the source; sustainable describes the whole practice that respects the source.
entries.definitionCN: 指可被自然过程补充；renewable 描述资源本身，sustainable 描述尊重该资源的整个做法。

entries.definition: Resistant to wear. Durable is about physical toughness; sustainable is about not consuming what keeps the system alive.
entries.definitionCN: 指耐磨、结实；durable 关乎物理强度，sustainable 关乎不消耗维持系统存活的东西。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: sustain + -able: able to be held up, hence able to keep going.
normal.cn: sustain + -able：托得住，因而撑得久。

normal.en: The family runs sustain, sustainable, sustainability, sustained, sustenance, unsustainable.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 sustain、sustainable、sustainability、sustained、sustenance、unsustainable。

normal.en: Fixed phrases fix the range: sustainable development, sustainable growth, sustainable yield, sustainable energy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标定义域：可持续发展、可持续增长、可持续产量、可持续能源。

normal.en: Sustainable fishing takes no more than what regrows.
normal.cn: 可持续捕捞只取再生长的那部分。

normal.en: A sustainable pace is one you can repeat tomorrow.
normal.cn: 可持续的节奏是明天还能照做的节奏。

abstract.en: Picture a tree that yields fruit every year because the picker never strips it bare.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵每年都结果的树，因为采摘者从不把它摘光。

abstract.en: Picture a runner keeping a pace slow enough to finish the whole race.
abstract.cn: 想象一位跑者把节奏放慢到足以跑完全程。

abstract.en: Picture a well that stays full because no one pumps more than the rain returns.
abstract.cn: 想象一口总也不见底的井，因为没人抽得比雨水回补更多。

examples.en: The farm switched to sustainable practices that protect the topsoil.
examples.cn: 这家农场改用保护表土的可持续做法。

examples.en: Analysts doubted the project was financially sustainable without subsidies.
examples.cn: 分析师怀疑没有补贴，这个项目在财务上是否可持续。

examples.en: A sustainable workload keeps the whole team healthy year-round.
examples.cn: 可持续的工作量让整个团队全年保持健康。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sustain（维持）+ able（可……的）」——撑得住、耗不尽 → sustainable 可持续的

root: 拉丁 sustinere = sub-「自下」+ tenere「握住、保持」→ 古法语 sustenir → 英语 sustain + -able「可……的」。更深词根一般认为是印欧语 *ten-「伸展、保持」（重构形式）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one test — can it keep going? — applied to nature, rates, growth, farming, materials, business, habits and harvests.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共用同一道考题——能否一直运转？——分别施于自然、速率、增长、农业、材料、商业、习惯与收成。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something is held up from below so it can keep going without breaking.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物被从下方托住，得以持续运转而不垮。

branches.en: NATURAL RESOURCES: energy, farming and harvests do not deplete the base they draw on.
branches.cn: 自然资源：能源、农业与收成不耗尽其所依托的根基。

branches.en: RATES AND GROWTH: paces, levels and expansions can be kept up without collapse.
branches.cn: 速率与增长：节奏、水平与扩张可持续而不崩溃。

branches.en: MATERIALS AND BUILDINGS: products and structures are made and maintained at low environmental cost.
branches.cn: 材料与建筑：产品与结构以低环境代价制造与维护。

branches.en: BUSINESS SURVIVAL: a model earns enough to keep operating over the long term.
branches.cn: 商业生存：模式长期能赚到足以运营的收入。

branches.en: PERSONAL HABITS: a practice can be repeated without burning out.
branches.cn: 个人习惯：做法可反复执行而不致枯竭。

intro.en: Sustainable is sustain plus the adjective suffix -able: the Latin verb sustinere 'hold up from below' and the ending that says 'able to be'.
intro.cn: sustainable 是 sustain 加形容词词尾 -able：即拉丁动词 sustinere「自下托住」加「可……」的词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin element is tenere 'to hold, keep' with sub- 'from below'; -able reached English through French from Latin -abilis. The same family includes tenable, retain and maintain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁成分是 tenere「握住、保持」加 sub-「自下」；-able 经法语源自拉丁 -abilis。同一词族还有 tenable、retain、maintain。

items.meaning: able to be continued without exhausting the base
items.meaningCN: 可持续的；不耗尽根基而能继续的
items.example: They chose sustainable materials for the floors.
items.exampleCN: 他们为地板选择了可持续材料。

items.meaning: to hold up, keep in being
items.example: The region cannot sustain its growing population.
items.exampleCN: 该地区无法养活不断增长的人口。

items.example: Sustainability shaped the company's product line.
items.exampleCN: 可持续性影响了公司的产品线。

items.example: The team showed sustained effort all season.
items.exampleCN: 全队整个赛季都表现出持续的努力。

items.example: The refugees found sustenance in the mountain villages.
items.exampleCN: 难民在山村找到了食物与生计。

items.example: The boom proved unsustainable.
items.exampleCN: 这场繁荣被证明不可持续。

items.meaning: able to be held or defended
items.example: The theory is tenable only with new evidence.
items.exampleCN: 只有在新的证据下，这个理论才站得住脚。

items.structure: Latin manu tenere (to hold in hand) via Old French
items.example: Farmers maintain the terraces every spring.
items.exampleCN: 农民每年春天维护梯田。

definition_zh: 歪斜的（地）；出错的（地）；偏离正轨的（地）
definition_en: away from the expected position or course; crooked or amiss
core_image: 画框挂歪了一寸，怎么看着都不对劲
scene: 风吹过门廊，那顶草帽滑向了一边。 Everything went awry during the storm.
sceneCN: 这里 awry 指「出了岔子、乱了套」（第 2 个义项：事情偏离正轨）；句意：暴风雨中一切都乱了套。

pos.zh: 歪的；错的（常作表语）
歪斜地；错误地

derivatives.zh: 歪的；揶揄的（同根基础形容词）

senses.title: Crooked or twisted in position
senses.definition: turned or twisted to one side, off the straight or proper position
senses.definitionCN: 偏向一侧，离开端正的位置
senses.example: His tie sat awry after the windy walk.
senses.exampleCN: 顶着风走了一段，他的领带歪了。
senses.why: The root is wry, twisted: the body sees the crookedness first.
senses.whyCN: 词根是 wry「扭的」：眼睛最先看到的就是歪斜。

senses.title: Gone wrong in outcome
senses.definition: of plans or events, turned out badly or amiss
senses.definitionCN: 指计划或事态出了差错、未按预期发展
senses.example: The surprise party went awry when the guest of honor left early.
senses.exampleCN: 寿星早退，惊喜派对泡了汤。
senses.why: A crooked position becomes a crooked outcome by the usual metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 空间之「歪」循惯用隐喻转为结果之「错」。

senses.title: Off the intended course
senses.definition: drifting from the intended line or route
senses.definitionCN: 偏离预定路线或方向
senses.example: The arrow flew awry in the crosswind.
senses.exampleCN: 横风让箭偏离了靶心。
senses.why: The straight path bends; motion shows the twist.
senses.whyCN: 直线被扭弯，运动把「扭」显现出来。

senses.title: Tilted or askew in expression
senses.definition: of a smile or look, twisted, as a wry or sardonic expression
senses.definitionCN: 形容微笑或神情歪扭，含嘲弄意味
senses.example: She gave an awry grin at the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听了消息，她嘴角一歪，似笑非笑。
senses.why: The face can twist as well as things can.
senses.whyCN: 面孔也能像物件一样「扭」。

senses.title: Disordered in arrangement
senses.definition: of a group of things, not aligned or squared up
senses.definitionCN: 指一批物件没有对齐、排正
senses.example: The books stood awry on the sagging shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 书架塌陷，书东倒西歪。
senses.why: One twist disturbs the row; alignment is its opposite.
senses.whyCN: 一处歪扭便搅乱整排；awry 正是「对齐」的反面。

senses.title: Morally off course
senses.definition: of conduct, turned aside from what is right
senses.definitionCN: 指行为偏离正道
senses.example: The reform went awry when its funds found other pockets.
senses.exampleCN: 款项流入私囊，改革便走上了歧路。
senses.why: The straight-and-narrow is literally a line; leaving it is the same twist.
senses.whyCN: 「正道」本就是一条线，离开即是同样的「扭」。

senses.title: Failure announced in hindsight
senses.definition: in narrative use, marking the moment things begin to fail
senses.definitionCN: 叙事用法，标记事态开始失控的时刻
senses.example: Everything had gone awry by the second act.
senses.exampleCN: 到第二幕，一切已然失控。
senses.why: Storytellers mark the twist with this one word.
senses.whyCN: 讲故事的人用这一个词标记转折。

senses.title: Body parts or clothing out of true
senses.definition: of hats, glasses, or limbs, sitting at the wrong angle
senses.definitionCN: 指帽子、眼镜或肢体角度不正
senses.example: Her spectacles rode awry across her nose.
senses.exampleCN: 她的眼镜歪斜地架在鼻梁上。
senses.why: The oldest English sense kept to the crooked and the worn.
senses.whyCN: 最早的英语义就停留在「歪戴、扭放」上。

intro.en: Awry comes from a-, on, plus wry, twisted, from Old English wrih, twisted, from the verb wrihan, to cover or twist; the compound formed in Middle English.
intro.cn: awry 由 a-（处于）+ wry（扭的）构成；wry 出自古英语 wrih「扭的」，动词原形 wrihan 意为「覆盖、扭」。复合词形成于中古英语。

items.en: The twist-root is reconstructed as wreik-, to twist or bind.
items.cn: 「扭」词根被重构为 wreik-「扭、缠」。

items.en: wrihan meant to cover or twist; its participle wrih meant twisted.
items.cn: 古英语 wrihan 意为覆盖、扭，分词 wrih 意为扭的。

items.en: The adjective wry survived for crooked, both of things and faces.
items.cn: 中古英语形容词 wry 保留下来，指物件与面孔的歪扭。

items.en: The compound a-wry arose, on or into a twisted state.
items.cn: 复合词 a-wry 出现，义为「处于扭歪状态」。

items.en: Shakespeare's era fixed go awry for plans failing.
items.cn: 莎士比亚时代，go awry 定型为「计划失败」的固定说法。

items.en: Today go awry dominates; the literal crooked sense lingers in descriptions.
items.cn: 如今 go awry 占主导；字面「歪斜」义仍见于描写文字。

note.en: Group one gathers the twist family and sound-alikes; group two gathers words of crookedness and failure.
note.cn: 第一组收「扭」词族及音近词；第二组收歪斜与失败义场的词。

entries.definition: the base adjective: a wry smile twists sideways.
entries.definitionCN: 基础形容词：wry smile 是歪向一边的苦笑。

entries.definition: for a short time; one letter off and nothing twisted about it.
entries.definitionCN: 片刻；与 awry 一字之差，毫无歪扭之意，词源不同。

entries.definition: to twist the body; the same twist-root made into motion.
entries.definitionCN: 身体扭动；同一「扭」词根化作动作。

entries.definition: crooked in position; the closest spatial twin.
entries.definitionCN: 位置歪斜；空间义上最接近的孪生词。

entries.definition: wrong or out of order; the closest outcome twin.
entries.definitionCN: 不对劲、出错；结果义上最接近的孪生词。

entries.definition: with a sideways, suspicious glance.
entries.definitionCN: 斜眼而视，含怀疑。

entries.definition: utterly upside down and disordered.
entries.definitionCN: 完全颠倒、乱作一团。

entries.definition: gone wildly out of control, informal.
entries.definitionCN: 失控乱套，口语用法。

normalIntro.en: Read a-wry as on-wry: something landed on its twist.
normalIntro.cn: 把 a-wry 读作 on-wry：某物落在了「扭」的状态上。

normal.en: a- meaning on or into plus wry, twisted.
normal.cn: a- 表「处于、进入」+ wry「扭的」。

normal.en: go awry is the collocation exams reward.
normal.cn: go awry 是考试偏爱的固定搭配。

normal.en: Rhyme memory: awry rhymes with a-cry when plans fail.
normal.cn: 押韵记忆：计划失败，awry 与 cry 押韵。

normal.en: wry smile, writhe, and awry share the old twist-root.
normal.cn: wry smile、writhe、awry 共享古老的「扭」词根。

normal.en: Adjective and adverb look identical; context tells them apart.
normal.cn: 形容词与副词同形，靠语境区分。

abstract.en: See the frame tilt one stubborn degree.
abstract.cn: 看那画框固执地歪了一度。

abstract.en: Awry is the sound of a plan snapping at its weakest joint.
abstract.cn: awry 是计划在最脆弱处断裂的声音。

abstract.en: Feel the wind take your hat sideways.
abstract.cn: 感觉风把你的帽子掀向一边。

examples.en: Careful plans went awry when the ferry was cancelled.
examples.cn: 渡轮停航，缜密的计划随之落空。

examples.en: His glasses sat awry and gave him a scholar's charm.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something straight that has taken a twist and stayed there.
core.cn: 核心意象：原本笔直之物被扭了一下，再没回去。

branches.en: THE POSITION SIDE: ties, books, glasses out of true.

definition_zh: 纪律的；惩戒的；学科的；规训的
definition_en: relating to rules and punishment, or to a branch of study and its methods
core_image: 一张桌子两边：一边放着行为守则与处罚条例，一边放着学科书目与方法手册
scene: 学院走廊里，墙上并排挂着两块牌子，一块写守则与处罚，一块写本领域的研究方法。 Two notices hang side by side in the corridor: one lists conduct and penalties, the other the methods of the field, and both fall under disciplinary rules.
sceneCN: 这里指第 1 个义项。这里 disciplinary 是「纪律惩戒的；学科的」（第 1、2 个义项：规则处罚与学科归属）；句意：走廊里并排挂着两块牌子，一块写守则与处罚，一块写本领域的方法，都归在纪律与学科之下。图中可辨识物件：走廊、两块牌子、守则文本、学科书目。

pos.zh: 纪律的；惩戒的；学科的；规训的

senses.title: Relating to rules and punishment
senses.definition: concerned with the enforcement of rules and the punishment of those who break them
senses.definitionCN: 与规则的执行及对违规者的处罚有关的
senses.example: The committee opened a disciplinary inquiry into the complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会就该投诉启动了纪律调查。
senses.why: Latin disciplina meant 'instruction' before it meant 'punishment'. Disciplinary keeps the older frame: rules exist to train, and penalties are the last instrument of that training.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 disciplina 先指“教导”，后指“惩罚”。disciplinary 保留了较早的框架：规则是为了训练，处罚只是这种训练的最后手段。

senses.title: Belonging to a field of study
senses.definition: relating to a branch of knowledge, its methods and its standards of evidence
senses.definitionCN: 与某一知识分支、其方法及证据标准有关的
senses.example: The paper crosses disciplinary boundaries between biology and economics.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文跨越了生物学与经济学之间的学科边界。
senses.why: A discipline is first a body of instruction. A field of study is exactly that: a body of things taught and methods passed on. The academic sense is older than it looks.
senses.whyCN: discipline 首先是一套教导。一个研究领域正是如此：一套被教的东西与传下去的方法。这个学术义比看上去更古老。

senses.title: Formal proceedings against a member
senses.titleCN: 对成员的正式纪律程序
senses.definition: describing an official process by which a professional body investigates and may penalize a member
senses.definitionCN: 描述专业团体调查并可能处罚成员的正式程序
senses.example: The nurse faced a disciplinary hearing over the error.
senses.exampleCN: 这名护士因该失误面临纪律听证。
senses.why: Here the adjective marks a procedure, not a mood. Disciplinary hearing is a fixed phrase because the hearing exists only to apply the rules of the profession.
senses.whyCN: 这里形容词标记的是一套程序，而不是一种气氛。disciplinary hearing 是固定搭配，因为这种听证只为执行行业规则而存在。

senses.title: Training that produces self-control
senses.definition: relating to the training of habits, obedience or self-control
senses.definitionCN: 与习惯、服从或自制的训练有关的
senses.example: Sport offers disciplinary training in patience.
senses.exampleCN: 运动提供了耐心的纪律训练。
senses.why: The root discere means 'to learn'. Disciplinary training is not primarily about catching offenders; it is about making a behaviour reliable through repetition.
senses.whyCN: 词根 discere 意为“学习”。纪律训练主要不是抓违规者，而是通过重复让某种行为变得可靠。

senses.title: Self-imposed ascetic practice
senses.definition: relating to strict self-regulation, especially in religious or ascetic practice
senses.definitionCN: 与严格自我约束有关的，尤指宗教或苦修实践
senses.example: The monastery kept a disciplinary silence after compline.
senses.exampleCN: 修道院在晚祷后保持纪律性的静默。
senses.why: Religious orders used disciplina for the rule that shaped a life. The disciplinary silence is not a punishment for anyone; it is the rule itself acting on the body.
senses.whyCN: 修会用 disciplina 指塑造生活的会规。纪律性的静默不是对谁的惩罚；它就是会规本身作用在身体上。

senses.title: Governing by surveillance and correction
senses.definition: in social theory, describing power that shapes behaviour through observation, normalization and correction
senses.definitionCN: 社会理论中描述通过观察、规范化与纠正来塑造行为的权力
senses.example: Foucault described the disciplinary power of schools and prisons.
senses.exampleCN: 福柯描述了学校与监狱的规训权力。
senses.why: This sense stresses that rules do not only punish after the fact; they produce docile bodies by constant watching. The adjective shifts from 'of rules' to 'of a mode of power'.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项强调规则不只事后惩罚；它们通过持续观看生产驯顺的身体。形容词从“规则的”转向“一种权力模式的”。

senses.title: A board that applies the rules
senses.definition: describing a body, such as a board or tribunal, whose function is to apply professional or institutional rules
senses.definitionCN: 描述以执行专业或机构规则为职能的机构，如委员会或裁判庭
senses.example: The disciplinary board meets on the first Monday of each month.
senses.exampleCN: 纪律委员会每月第一个星期一开会。
senses.why: The adjective attaches to institutions rather than to acts. A disciplinary board is defined by its function, not by the severity of its decisions.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词附着在机构上，而不是行为上。纪律委员会由其职能定义，而不是由其决定的严厉程度定义。

senses.title: Methods specific to a field
senses.definition: describing the techniques, vocabulary and standards that a particular academic field treats as proper
senses.definitionCN: 描述某一学术领域视为正当的技术、词汇与标准
senses.example: Peer review is a disciplinary norm, not a universal one.
senses.exampleCN: 同行评议是一种学科规范，而非普世规范。
senses.why: Each field trains its members to see some evidence as decisive and other evidence as irrelevant. What counts as proof is itself disciplinary.
senses.whyCN: 每个领域都训练其成员把某些证据看作决定性的，把另一些看作无关的。什么算作证明，本身就是学科性的。

intro.en: Disciplinary is discipline plus -ary. Discipline comes from Latin disciplina, 'instruction, knowledge, a rule of life', from discipulus 'pupil', from discere 'to learn'. The adjective is a 16th-century formation and carries both the teaching and the punishing branches.
intro.cn: disciplinary 是 discipline 加 -ary。discipline 来自拉丁 disciplina“教导、知识、生活规则”，源于 discipulus“学生”，再上溯 discere“学习”。形容词是 16 世纪构造，同时承载“教导”与“惩罚”两支。

items.en: The root *dek- meant 'to take, to accept'. Latin discere 'to learn' comes from it, and so does docere 'to teach', which supplies doctor and document.
items.cn: 词根 *dek- 意为“拿取、接受”。拉丁 discere“学习”由此而来，docere“教导”也同出此源，后者给出 doctor 与 document。

items.en: Discere meant 'to learn'. Discipulus, 'pupil', is generally taken as discere plus a suffix; some handbooks link the ending to capere 'to grasp'. The exact formation is marked here as source uncertain.
items.cn: discere 意为“学习”。discipulus“学生”一般认为由 discere 加后缀构成；部分手册把词尾联系到 capere“抓取”。确切构词在此标注为「来源不确定」。

items.en: Disciplina covered instruction, a branch of knowledge, and the rule by which a pupil lives. Roman writers used it for military training as well, which prepared the later sense of enforced order.
items.cn: disciplina 涵盖教导、知识分支以及学生所遵循的规则。罗马作家也用它指军事训练，为后来“强制秩序”的义项铺路。

items.en: Old French discipline entered English as discipline with the senses 'instruction' and 'rule'. The punitive sense grows in the 16th century as institutions formalize penalties.
items.cn: 古法语 discipline 进入英语作 discipline，带“教导”与“规则”义。随着机构把处罚制度化，惩罚义在 16 世纪生长起来。

items.en: The adjective disciplinary is formed to mean 'of or belonging to discipline'. Early uses concern church and school order rather than academic fields.
items.cn: 形容词 disciplinary 构成，意为“属于 discipline 的”。早期用法关于教会与学校秩序，而非学术领域。

items.en: As universities organized into departments, disciplinary came to mean 'belonging to a field of study', and interdisciplinary followed. In the 20th century social theory gave it the sense of a mode of power.
items.cn: 随着大学按系科组织，disciplinary 开始表示“属于某一研究领域”，interdisciplinary 随之出现。20 世纪的社会理论又赋予它“一种权力模式”的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the noun, the person noun and the adjective of state. The meaning group contrasts rule-enforcement with academic and corrective terms.
note.cn: 形近组区分名词、指人名词与状态形容词；词义组把“执行规则”与学术、纠正类词区分开。

entries.definition: a field of study, a system of rules, or the act of training and punishing. All senses of the adjective come from it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究领域、规则体系，或训练与处罚行为。形容词的所有义项都来自它。

entries.definition: a person who insists on strict rules. It names a person, while disciplinary describes rules or procedures.
entries.definitionCN: 坚持严格规则的人。它指人，而 disciplinary 描述规则或程序。

entries.definition: trained to obey and control oneself. It describes a person's habit, not an institution's function.
entries.definitionCN: 受过训练、能服从与自控的。它描述个人习惯，而非机构职能。

entries.definition: intended as punishment. It is narrower than disciplinary, which also covers instruction and academic fields.
entries.definitionCN: 以惩罚为目的的。它比 disciplinary 窄，后者还涵盖教导与学科。

entries.definition: intended to correct a fault. A corrective measure aims at repair, while a disciplinary one aims at order.
entries.definitionCN: 意在纠正错误的。纠正措施目标是修复，纪律措施目标是秩序。

entries.definition: relating to study and scholarship. It overlaps with sense 02 but says nothing about rules or punishment.
entries.definitionCN: 与学习和学术有关的。它与第 2 义项重叠，但不涉及规则或处罚。

entries.definition: relating to official rules and their administration. It stresses formal regulation more than training.
entries.definitionCN: 与官方规则及其执行有关的。它比训练更强调正式规章。

entries.definition: relating to the methods of a field. It is close to sense 08 but focuses on procedure rather than standards.
entries.definitionCN: 与某一领域的方法有关的。它接近第 8 义项，但聚焦于程序而非标准。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the word into the learning root and the adjective suffix, then place the two main branches side by side: rules and fields.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词拆成“学习”词根与形容词后缀，再把两大分支并排放好：规则与学科。

normal.en: See discere, 'to learn', behind discipline: rules began as lessons.
normal.cn: 看见 discipline 背后的 discere“学习”：规则最初是课程。

normal.en: Picture the two noticeboards: penalties on one, reading lists on the other, both labelled disciplinary.
normal.cn: 想象那两块告示牌：一边是处罚，一边是书单，都写着 disciplinary。

normal.en: For a professional, disciplinary hearing is a procedure, not an insult.
normal.cn: 对专业人士来说，纪律听证是一套程序，不是侮辱。

normal.en: For academia, remember interdisciplinary: fields have borders, so they can be crossed.
normal.cn: 学术方面记住 interdisciplinary：学科有边界，所以能被跨越。

normal.en: Keep the old monastic image: silence kept as a rule, not as a punishment.
normal.cn: 记住古老的修院意象：静默是作为会规而守，不是作为惩罚。

abstract.en: Hold one axis with two ends: training at one end, punishment at the other, and most uses sit between.
abstract.cn: 抓住一根轴的两端：一端是训练，一端是惩罚，多数用法位于中间。

abstract.en: Notice that a discipline is both a thing you learn and a thing that constrains you.
abstract.cn: 注意 discipline 既是你要学的东西，也是约束你的东西。

abstract.en: Ask of every use: is the rule shaping a person, or sorting knowledge?
abstract.cn: 对每个用法都问：这条规则在塑造人，还是在整理知识？

examples.en: The company took disciplinary action against two employees.
examples.cn: 公司对两名员工采取了纪律处分。

examples.en: Her work is admired across disciplinary lines.
examples.cn: 她的研究跨越学科界限而受到赞赏。

examples.en: The journal applies strict disciplinary standards to submissions.
examples.cn: 该刊对投稿采用严格的学科标准。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“地斯普林那里”：地里的斯普林（discipline）在那边立着牌子，一边写纪律，一边写学科——disciplinary 就是纪律的、学科的。

root: 拉丁语 discere“学习”，派生 discipulus“学生”（构词细节存疑），再派生 disciplina“教导、知识、生活规则”；经古法语 discipline 进入英语，加形容词后缀 -ary 构成 disciplinary。同根 docere“教导”给出 doctor、document、docile。

sensesIntro.en: Disciplinary holds two branches that grew from one trunk. The trunk is disciplina, a body of instruction; one branch became the rules a learner must obey, the other became the field a learner studies. From the first come hearings, penalties and the theory of disciplinary power; from the second come boundaries, methods and interdisciplinary work. The adjective is always about a frame that shapes people or knowledge.
sensesIntro.cn: disciplinary 的两大分支长在同一根主干上。主干是 disciplina，一套教导；一支长成学习者必须遵守的规则，另一支长成学习者所研究的领域。前者给出听证、处罚与规训权力理论；后者给出学科边界、方法与跨学科工作。这个形容词始终关于一个塑造人或知识的框架。

core.en: A frame of instruction: rules that train, and fields that organize knowledge.
core.cn: 一套教导框架：训练人的规则，以及整理知识的学科。

branches.en: ENFORCEMENT: rules, hearings and the boards that apply them.
branches.cn: 执行：规则、听证与执行规则的机构。

branches.en: SCHOLARSHIP: fields, their boundaries, methods and standards.
branches.cn: 学术：领域、边界、方法与标准。

branches.en: TRAINING: habit made reliable by repetition.
branches.cn: 训练：通过重复使习惯变得可靠。

branches.en: ASCETIC RULE: self-imposed order shaping a life.
branches.cn: 苦修会规：塑造生活的自我约束。

branches.en: THEORY: power that shapes behaviour by watching it.
branches.cn: 理论：通过观看塑造行为的权力。

intro.en: Disciplinary is a noun plus -ary. The items show the discere family, the person suffix -arian, and the productive prefix inter- that turns a discipline into a crossing.
intro.cn: disciplinary 是名词加 -ary。下列条目展示 discere 词族、指人后缀 -arian，以及把学科变成“跨越”的高产前缀 inter-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries pair discere with docere, the two halves of teaching. One is what the pupil does, the other what the teacher does.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目把 discere 与 docere 放在一起，这是教学的两半：一个是学生做的，一个是教师做的。

items.meaning: relating to rules, punishment or a field of study
items.meaningCN: 与规则、处罚或学科有关的
items.example: The matter went to a disciplinary panel.
items.exampleCN: 此事交由纪律小组处理。

items.meaning: training; a field of study; a system of rules
items.example: History is an old discipline.
items.exampleCN: 历史学是一门古老的学科。

items.meaning: a person who insists on strict rules
items.example: The headmaster was a strict disciplinarian.
items.exampleCN: 校长是一位严格纪律的执行者。

items.meaning: trained to obey and control oneself
items.example: She kept a disciplined study routine.
items.exampleCN: 她保持有纪律的学习作息。

items.example: The centre runs interdisciplinary research.
items.exampleCN: 该中心开展跨学科研究。

items.meaning: drawing on several fields side by side
items.example: The clinic uses a multidisciplinary team.
items.exampleCN: 该诊所使用多学科团队。

items.meaning: a follower who learns from a teacher
items.example: He was a disciple of the old master.
items.exampleCN: 他是那位老大师的弟子。

items.example: The animal was remarkably docile.
items.exampleCN: 这只动物异常温顺。

items.meaning: a teacher; a holder of the highest degree
items.example: She earned her doctorate in physics.
items.exampleCN: 她获得了物理学博士学位。

definition_zh: 群体遗传学；种群遗传学（研究种群内与种群间等位基因频率变化规律的遗传学分支）
definition_en: the branch of genetics that studies how allele and genotype frequencies change within and between populations over time
core_image: 深夜实验室里，几十代果蝇的翅脉标本铺满长桌，研究员把每一代的性状比例换算成频率曲线
scene: 深夜的实验室里，研究员把几十代果蝇的翅脉记录摊在长桌上，想从整个群体的角度看清基因比例怎样一代代改变。 Population genetics turns those breeding records into a map of shifting allele frequencies.
sceneCN: 这里指向这门学科本身（第 1 个义项：研究种群内遗传变异与等位基因频率变化的遗传学分支）；句意为群体遗传学把这些繁育记录变成一幅等位基因频率不断变动的地图。图中可辨识物件：培养瓶、翅脉标本、频率曲线、台灯。

pos.zh: 名词：不可数，指学科名称；作主语时谓语用单数

collocations.zh: 群体遗传学的研究路径
把群体遗传学用于保护实践

derivatives.zh: 由学科名加表示「从业者」的词尾构成，义为「群体遗传学家」
由学科名转作定语形容词，义为「群体遗传层面的」
由 population 与 genomics 组合而成，义为「种群基因组学」，研究全基因组尺度的群体变异
同一学科框架下的核心概念，义为「种群结构」，指群体内与群体间的遗传分化格局
同一框架下的概念，义为「种群瓶颈」，指群体规模骤然缩小导致遗传多样性下降

senses.title: The discipline itself
senses.definition: the branch of genetics that studies the frequencies of alleles and genotypes in groups of interbreeding organisms
senses.definitionCN: 研究互交群体中各类等位基因与基因型出现频率的遗传学分支
senses.example: Population genetics explains why some variants are common in one region and rare in another.
senses.exampleCN: 群体遗传学解释了为什么某些变异在一个地区常见、在另一个地区罕见。
senses.why: The name simply joins the object of study, the population, to the tool, genetics; the discipline exists because inheritance has to be counted across many individuals, not just traced in one family.
senses.whyCN: 名称只是把研究对象「群体」与工具「遗传学」拼在一起；这门学科之所以成立，是因为遗传必须在上千个体中计数，而不能只在一个家系里追踪。

senses.title: Allele frequency as the central measure
senses.titleCN: 以等位基因频率为核心量
senses.definition: the proportion of each allele at a locus within a population, the quantity the field tracks over generations
senses.definitionCN: 某一基因座上每种等位基因在群体中所占的比例，也是本学科跨世代追踪的核心量
senses.example: Population genetics detected a shift in allele frequency across two seasons, which showed that selection was acting.
senses.exampleCN: 等位基因频率在两个季节间发生偏移，说明选择压力正在起作用。
senses.why: Individuals carry genotypes, but only frequencies can be summed over a group; making the frequency the unit of analysis is what turns heredity into a measurable population process.
senses.whyCN: 个体携带的是基因型，但只有频率能在群体层面相加；把频率当作分析单位，才使遗传成为可测量的群体过程。

senses.title: Mathematical modelling tradition
senses.definition: the tradition of building equations for selection, drift, mutation and migration, founded by Fisher, Haldane and Wright
senses.definitionCN: 为选择、漂变、突变与迁移建立方程的传统，由费希尔、霍尔丹与赖特奠基
senses.example: A simple population genetics model showed that even weak selection could fix an allele in a few hundred generations.
senses.exampleCN: 一个简单模型显示，即使很弱的选择压力也能在数百代内使某个等位基因固定下来。
senses.why: Field counts alone cannot separate several forces acting at once; equations let researchers ask what would happen if only one force were at work.
senses.whyCN: 野外的计数无法同时拆开几种力量的作用；方程让人可以追问「若只有一种力量在起作用会怎样」。

senses.title: Division of labour with molecular genetics
senses.definition: the subfield that works with frequencies in groups rather than with the molecular machinery of a single genome
senses.definitionCN: 处理群体中的频率、而非单个基因组的分子机制的子领域
senses.example: Molecular genetics read the sequence, while population genetics asked how often that sequence appears.
senses.exampleCN: 分子遗传学读取序列，群体遗传学则追问这段序列出现的频率有多高。
senses.why: The same data can be read at two scales: the molecule explains mechanism, the population explains distribution, and the field defines itself by the second question.
senses.whyCN: 同一批数据可以在两个尺度上读：分子层面解释机制，群体层面解释分布，本学科正是以第二个问题界定自己。

senses.title: Conservation and ecology
senses.titleCN: 保护生物学与生态学应用
senses.definition: the use of frequency models to estimate genetic diversity, inbreeding and viability in threatened species
senses.definitionCN: 用频率模型估计受威胁物种的遗传多样性、近交程度与存续能力
senses.example: Conservation managers used population genetics to decide which herds could be safely mixed.
senses.exampleCN: 保护管理者用群体遗传学判断哪些兽群可以安全地混群。
senses.why: Small isolated groups lose variants fast; counting those variants is the only way to tell whether a reserve is holding a viable gene pool.
senses.whyCN: 小而隔离的群体丢失变异很快；只有把这些变异数清楚，才能判断保护区是否守住了可存续的基因库。

senses.title: Plant and animal breeding
senses.definition: the application of frequency and selection models to predict genetic gain in breeding programmes
senses.definitionCN: 把频率与选择模型用于预测育种计划中的遗传增益
senses.example: Breeders rely on population genetics to predict how fast a trait will improve.
senses.exampleCN: 育种者依靠群体遗传学预测某个性状改良得有多快。
senses.why: Breeding is selection made deliberate; the same equations that describe natural selection can forecast the response of a herd or a crop.
senses.whyCN: 育种是把选择变成有意为之；描述自然选择的同一套方程，可以预测畜群或作物的改良反应。

senses.title: Medical and epidemiological use
senses.definition: the study of variant frequencies across human groups to interpret disease risk and ancestry
senses.definitionCN: 研究不同人群中的变异频率，用以解释疾病风险与祖源
senses.example: Population genetics showed that the protective variant is far more common in one continent.
senses.exampleCN: 群体遗传学显示，这种具有保护作用的变异在某个大陆要常见得多。
senses.why: A risk variant may look important in one clinic and be common everywhere; only a frequency comparison across groups can tell whether it is truly rare.
senses.whyCN: 某个风险变异在一家诊所里可能显得重要，却可能到处都常见；只有跨群体比较频率，才能判断它是否真的罕见。

senses.title: A teaching subject and research toolkit
senses.definition: a standard course and a set of sampling and statistical methods taught across biology degrees
senses.definitionCN: 一门标准课程，也是一套在生物学各学位中教授的采样与统计方法
senses.example: The seminar introduced population genetics through sampling exercises and frequency tables.
senses.exampleCN: 研讨课通过采样练习与频率表来介绍群体遗传学。
senses.why: The field is defined as much by its methods as by its findings, so it is taught as a toolkit before it is taught as a body of results.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科既由发现界定，也由方法界定，因此教学上先教工具、再教结论。

senses.title: Relation to population genomics
senses.titleCN: 与种群基因组学的关系
senses.definition: the classical frequency framework that population genomics extends to thousands of loci at once
senses.definitionCN: 经典频率框架，而种群基因组学把它扩展到同时分析成千上万个位点
senses.example: Population genetics supplied the theory that population genomics later scaled up to whole genomes.
senses.exampleCN: 群体遗传学提供了理论，种群基因组学后来把它扩展到全基因组。
senses.why: More markers do not change the questions; they sharpen the estimates, so the newer field inherits its logic from the older one.
senses.whyCN: 更多标记并不改变问题，只是让估计更精细；新领域因此继承了旧领域的逻辑。

intro.en: The phrase is built from an English noun of Latin origin, a Greek-derived technical term coined in the early twentieth century, and the plural marker of the discipline name. Each part is transparent, but the exact moment when the two words were first printed together is not recorded.
intro.cn: 这个短语由拉丁语来源的英语名词、二十世纪初以希腊语词根造出的术语以及学科名的复数词尾构成。各部分含义清楚，但两个词最初印在一起的准确时刻并无记录。

items.en: Populus meant a people or a community; populatio, from populari, to lay waste or to populate, gave English the noun population, first used of inhabitants and later of any interbreeding group.
items.cn: 这个词指人民或共同体的成员；由表示「使有人居住」的动词派生的名词进入英语后先指居民，后来才指任何互交繁育的群体。

items.en: Genesis meant origin or coming into being; from it came genetikos, concerned with generation, the root behind the modern vocabulary of heredity.
items.cn: 这个词意为起源、生成；由它派生的形容词表示「与生育、发生有关的」，成为现代遗传词汇的词根。

items.en: William Bateson coined genetics for the study of heredity and variation, deliberately choosing a Greek root rather than an existing Latin one.
items.cn: 贝特森为研究遗传与变异的学问造出这个术语，特意选用希腊词根而非现成的拉丁词根。

items.en: Fisher, Haldane and Wright showed that selection, drift and migration could be written as frequency equations, and the phrase population genetics came into use for that programme.
items.cn: 费希尔、霍尔丹与赖特证明选择、漂变与迁移都能写成频率方程，这个短语随之成为该研究纲领的名称。

items.en: From the 1990s the same framework was applied to thousands of markers at once, and population genomics was named as its large-scale successor.
items.cn: 自一九九零年代起，同一框架被用于同时分析成千上万个标记，并以其大规模后继者的名义命名了新领域。

items.en: The compound itself appears in print in the second quarter of the twentieth century; the precise first attestation is uncertain, while the origin of each component is not in doubt.
items.cn: 这一复合词在二十世纪第二个二十五年间见于印刷品；其确切首见年代不确定，但各成分的来源并无争议。

note.en: The first group shares wording or the same technical root; the second group names neighbouring branches that ask related but distinct questions.
note.cn: 第一组共享字面或同一个术语词根；第二组是相邻分支，问题相关但各不相同。

entries.definition: The study of variation across thousands of loci in a population, an extension of the classical framework.
entries.definitionCN: 研究群体中成千上万个位点的变异，是经典框架的扩展。

entries.definition: The study of how populations grow, interact and are limited by their environment.
entries.definitionCN: 研究种群如何增长、相互作用并受环境限制。

entries.definition: The broad study of heredity and variation.
entries.definitionCN: 研究遗传与变异的广义学科。

entries.definition: The total stock of alleles carried by a population.
entries.definitionCN: 一个群体所携带的全部等位基因总和。

entries.definition: The pattern of genetic differences among subpopulations of one species.
entries.definitionCN: 同一物种各亚群体之间遗传差异的格局。

entries.definition: Genetics applied to the causes of evolutionary change, of which population genetics is the quantitative core.
entries.definitionCN: 把遗传学用于解释演化变化的原因，群体遗传学是其定量核心。

entries.definition: The study of genetic variation in natural populations with an emphasis on adaptation to habitat.
entries.definitionCN: 研究自然群体中的遗传变异，侧重对栖息地的适应。

entries.definition: The genetics of continuously varying traits, using statistical rather than single-locus models.
entries.definitionCN: 研究连续变异性状的遗传学，用统计模型而非单位点模型。

entries.definition: The applied field that uses population principles to protect endangered species.
entries.definitionCN: 运用群体原理保护濒危物种的应用领域。

entries.definition: The wider study of populations, including ecology, genetics and demography.
entries.definitionCN: 更宽泛的群体研究，涵盖生态、遗传与人口统计。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations chain the object of study, the central measure, and the applied uses; the abstract ones reduce the field to the arithmetic of inheritance.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想串起研究对象、核心量与各项应用；抽象联想把整门学科化简为遗传的算术。

normal.en: Population is the object: a group of interbreeding individuals, not a single family.
normal.cn: 群体是研究对象：一群互交繁育的个体，而不是一个家系。

normal.en: Genetics is the tool: the same laws of inheritance, now counted instead of traced.
normal.cn: 遗传学是工具：同样的遗传规律，从追踪改为计数。

normal.en: Allele frequency is the measure that makes the group visible to statistics.
normal.cn: 等位基因频率是让群体变得可统计的那个量。

normal.en: The equations of Fisher, Haldane and Wright are the field's native language.
normal.cn: 费希尔、霍尔丹与赖特的方程是这门学科的母语。

normal.en: Conservation, breeding and medicine are the three places the equations are put to work.
normal.cn: 保护、育种与医学是这些方程投入实际工作的三个场所。

abstract.en: A population is an abacus: every individual is a bead, and the field counts which beads are alike.
abstract.cn: 群体是一把算盘：每个个体都是一颗珠子，学科数的是哪些珠子相同。

abstract.en: Inheritance stops being a family tree and becomes a ledger of proportions.
abstract.cn: 遗传不再是家谱，而变成一本比例账簿。

abstract.en: The field asks not who your ancestors were but how often your variant occurs.
abstract.cn: 这门学科问的不是你的祖先是谁，而是你的变异出现得有多频繁。

examples.en: Population genetics predicts that small isolated groups lose variation quickly.
examples.cn: 群体遗传学预测，小而隔离的群体很快会丢失变异。

examples.en: She applied population genetics to decide how to mix the two captive herds.
examples.cn: 她运用群体遗传学来决定如何把两个圈养兽群混群。

examples.en: A course in population genetics usually begins with allele frequency tables.
examples.cn: 群体遗传学课程通常从等位基因频率表讲起。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「泡普雷申 基因题克斯」——把一大群人（population）的基因当成一道统计题（genetics）：群体遗传学

root: 第一个成分来自拉丁语 populus「人民」，经表示「使有人居住」的动词派生出英语「群体、人口」；第二个成分由希腊语 genesis「起源、生成」派生的形容词经德语进入英语，一九零五年由贝特森定名为遗传学。整个短语的确切首见年代不确定，但两个成分的来源清楚。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses divide into four layers: the discipline's definition, its two core instruments, its neighbours, and its applications.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项分四层：学科定义、两件核心工具、与相邻学科的分工，以及各项应用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bench of fruit-fly records, every generation reduced to a table of proportions.
core.cn: 核心意象：一桌果蝇记录，每一代都被化约成一张比例表。

branches.en: THE DEFINITION: the field is named for its object and its tool, and its first sense is simply that pairing.
branches.cn: 定义本身：学科以研究对象与工具命名，第一个义项就是这一配对。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENTS: frequency is the measure, equations are the language, and together they turn heredity into a population process.
branches.cn: 两件工具：频率是量，方程是语言，合起来把遗传变成群体过程。

branches.en: THE BOUNDARIES: molecular genetics reads mechanism, population genomics reads scale, and the classical field sits between them.
branches.cn: 学科边界：分子遗传学读机制，种群基因组学读规模，经典学科居于两者之间。

branches.en: THE APPLICATIONS: conservation, breeding and medicine each borrow the frequency model for a practical decision.
branches.cn: 三类应用：保护、育种与医学各自借用频率模型做实际决策。

branches.en: THE CLASSROOM: the field is also taught as a toolkit of sampling and tables before it is taught as results.
branches.cn: 课堂形态：这门学科在讲结论之前，先作为采样与制表的工具被教授。

intro.en: The term is a compound of an English noun with Latin ancestry and a Greek-derived technical word; its parts say object plus instrument, nothing more.
intro.cn: 这个术语由一个有拉丁渊源英语名词与一个希腊词根术语复合而成；各部件只说明「对象加工具」。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the word for a people and the noun of inhabiting; Greek supplies the root for origin and generation, which English turned into the name of a science.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「人民」与「居住」的名词；希腊语提供了「起源、生成」的词根，英语据此造出学科名。

items.example: The word named the body of citizens before it named any breeding group.
items.exampleCN: 这个词先指公民整体，后来才指任何繁育群体。

items.example: It gave English the noun population.
items.exampleCN: 它给英语提供了「群体、人口」这一名词。

items.example: It turns the verb of inhabiting into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 它把表示居住的动词变成状态名词。

items.example: The root names the beginning of a new organism or form.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指新个体或新形态的开端。

items.example: It is the direct source of the English adjective genetic.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语形容词的直接来源。

items.example: Johannsen shortened the Greek root into a word for the unit itself.
items.exampleCN: 约翰森把希腊词根缩短，造出指遗传单位的词。

items.example: It turns the adjective into the name of a discipline.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成学科名称。

items.example: In biology the word narrows from inhabitants to a breeding unit.
items.exampleCN: 在生物学中，这个词从「居民」窄化为「繁育单位」。

items.meaning: the study of heredity and variation
items.meaningCN: 研究遗传与变异的学科
items.example: The name was coined in 1905 and covers all scales of inheritance.
items.exampleCN: 该名称造于一九零五年，涵盖各尺度的遗传研究。

derivatives.zh: 由学科名加表示「从业者」的词尾构成，义为「群体遗传学家」
由学科名转作定语形容词，义为「群体遗传层面的」
由 population 与 genomics 组合而成，义为「种群基因组学」，研究全基因组尺度的群体变异
同一学科框架下的核心概念，义为「种群结构」，指群体内与群体间的遗传分化格局

definition_en: to make beer by fermenting; to make tea or coffee by steeping; also to be developing, as in a storm brewing

senses.title: To make beer by fermenting
senses.definition: to make beer by soaking and fermenting grain
senses.definitionCN: 通过浸泡与发酵谷物来制作啤酒
senses.example: They brew their own beer in the garage.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在车库里自酿啤酒。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the brewing of ale.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是酿造麦芽酒。

senses.title: To make tea or coffee
senses.definition: to make a hot drink by steeping leaves or grounds in water
senses.definitionCN: 用热水浸泡茶叶或咖啡粉制成热饮
senses.example: She brewed a strong pot of tea.
senses.exampleCN: 她泡了一壶浓茶。

senses.whyCN: 同样的浸泡过程从谷物移到了叶片。

senses.title: To be developing
senses.definition: to be forming or gathering, especially something unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 正在形成或积聚，尤指不好的事
senses.example: Trouble had been brewing for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 麻烦已经酝酿了好几周。
senses.why: A slow fermentation becomes an image for slow trouble.
senses.whyCN: 缓慢的发酵成了慢慢变坏的麻烦的意象。
