definition_zh: 自由贸易；无关税或少关税的贸易；主张开放市场的主张
definition_en: trade between countries carried on without tariffs, quotas or other government restrictions
core_image: 一道海关关卡被完全打开，货物直接穿过，栏杆上挂着一块写着零的牌子
scene: 经济论坛的讲台上，一位学者指着世界地图说，若各国取消关税，货物就能像在本国一样流动。 The lecture argued that free trade raises output in every participating country.
sceneCN: 这里指「不受关税与配额限制的贸易」，对应第 1 个义项：货物在国与国之间自由进出、不设壁垒；句意为这场讲座主张自由贸易会提高所有参与国的产出。画面要点：讲台、世界地图、被抬起的栏杆、零关税标牌。

pos.zh: 自由贸易（不可数，作定语时写作 free-trade）

collocations.zh: 自由贸易与保护主义之争

derivatives.zh: 自由贸易的（free trade 转化为定语形式，语义从「制度」转为「属于该制度的」）
自由（free 加名词后缀，指不受约束的状态）
自由地（free 加副词后缀，指以不受限制的方式）
更自由的（free 的比较级，指限制更少）
贸易；交易（短语的后半，源自古英语与低地德语中表示「路径、往来」的词）

senses.title: Trade without tariffs or quotas
senses.titleCN: 无关税与配额限制的贸易
senses.definition: the exchange of goods between countries without tariffs, quotas or other barriers
senses.definitionCN: 国家之间不设关税、配额或其他壁垒的货物交换
senses.example: The lecture argued that free trade raises output in every participating country.
senses.exampleCN: 这场讲座主张自由贸易会提高所有参与国的产出。
senses.why: Free means not held back, and trade means exchange, so the phrase is exchange that no border charge or limit obstructs.
senses.whyCN: free 意为不受束缚，trade 意为交换，因此这个短语就是没有边境收费或限制阻碍的交换。

senses.title: The policy doctrine advocating it
senses.definition: the political and economic doctrine that barriers to trade should be removed
senses.definitionCN: 认为应当取消贸易壁垒的政治与经济主张
senses.example: Free trade was the party's answer to rising prices.
senses.exampleCN: 自由贸易是该党对物价上涨的回答。
senses.why: Once an idea is argued for, its name becomes a label for the camp that holds it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某种想法被反复论证，它的名称就成为主张者的旗帜。

senses.title: The scope of free trade agreements
senses.titleCN: 自由贸易协定所覆盖的范围
senses.definition: the arrangements in which a group of countries lowers barriers among themselves
senses.definitionCN: 若干国家在彼此之间降低壁垒的安排
senses.example: The free trade area removed duties on most manufactured goods.
senses.exampleCN: 这个自由贸易区取消了大多数制成品的关税。
senses.why: Regional arrangements borrow the name because they practise the same absence of barriers, though only inside the group.
senses.whyCN: 区域安排借用这个名称，因为它们实践同样的无壁垒状态，尽管只在集团内部。

senses.title: Free trade in one sector
senses.titleCN: 某一行业内的自由贸易
senses.definition: the removal of barriers in a particular industry, such as services or agriculture
senses.definitionCN: 在某一行业（如服务或农业）取消壁垒
senses.example: Free trade in services remains limited by licensing rules.
senses.exampleCN: 服务自由贸易仍受许可规则限制。
senses.why: Negotiations proceed sector by sector, so the phrase is often narrowed by a subject word.
senses.whyCN: 谈判按行业推进，因此这个短语常被主题词收窄。

senses.title: Free trade contrasted with fair trade
senses.titleCN: 与公平贸易相对的自由贸易
senses.definition: the trade model that stresses openness, as opposed to one that stresses standards and fairness
senses.definitionCN: 强调开放、与强调标准与公平的模式相对的贸易模式
senses.example: Critics want fair trade, not merely free trade.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者要的是公平贸易，而不只是自由贸易。
senses.why: Two slogans compete for the same ground, so the phrase is often defined by what it is set against.
senses.whyCN: 两个口号争夺同一块阵地，因此这个短语常用它的对立面来定义。

senses.title: The economic theory behind it
senses.definition: the theory that specialization and exchange raise total welfare through comparative advantage
senses.definitionCN: 认为分工与交换通过比较优势提高总福利的理论
senses.example: Free trade rests on the theory of comparative advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 自由贸易建立在比较优势理论之上。
senses.why: The phrase names not only a practice but the reasoning that justifies it, so it appears beside theory and models.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语不只指做法，也指为它辩护的推理，因此常与理论和模型并置。

senses.title: The claimed benefits and costs
senses.definition: the gains and losses attributed to open trade, such as lower prices and displaced workers
senses.definitionCN: 归于开放贸易的得失，如更低价格与失业的工人
senses.example: The debate weighed the benefits of free trade against local job losses.
senses.exampleCN: 辩论权衡了自由贸易的好处与本地失业。
senses.why: A doctrine is judged by outcomes, so the phrase becomes a shorthand for a bundle of predicted effects.
senses.whyCN: 主张要按结果评判，因此这个短语成为一束预期效果的简称。

senses.title: Any unrestricted exchange
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何不受限制的交流
senses.definition: the free movement of goods, ideas or people without artificial obstruction
senses.definitionCN: 货物、观念或人不被人为阻碍地自由流动
senses.example: Some writers speak of free trade in ideas as well as in goods.
senses.exampleCN: 有些作者谈到的不只是货物的自由贸易，还有观念的自由流通。
senses.why: The abstract sense drops tariffs and keeps only openness, so the phrase can describe any unblocked flow.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义去掉关税，只保留开放，因此这个短语可以描述任何不被堵塞的流动。

intro.en: Free trade joins free, a native English word for not being held, with trade, a Germanic word for path and exchange. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: free trade 把英语本族表示「不受束缚」的 free，与源自日耳曼语、表示「路径与往来」的 trade 组合起来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Freo meant not in bondage, and it described persons who were not slaves or serfs.
items.cn: freo 意为不受奴役，形容并非奴隶或农奴的人。

items.en: Trade came into English from Middle Low German or Dutch, where it meant a track or course, and English widened it to commerce.
items.cn: trade 经中古低地德语或荷兰语进入英语，原指路径或行程，英语把它扩展到商业。

items.en: Economists began to argue that exchange should be freed from duties, and free trade named that absence of restraint.
items.cn: 18 世纪经济学家开始主张让交换摆脱关税，free trade 用来指这种无束缚状态。

items.en: With the repeal of the corn laws and the rise of industrial exports, free trade became a political creed, not only a description.
items.cn: 随着谷物法废除与工业出口兴起，自由贸易成为一种政治信条，而不只是描述。

items.en: Twentieth-century treaties turned the slogan into detailed rules for tariffs, services and dispute settlement.
items.cn: 20 世纪的条约把这个口号变成关于关税、服务与争端解决的细致规则。

note.en: The first group shares the freedom root but has moved into other senses; the second group names rival or neighbouring trade doctrines.
note.cn: 第一组共享「自由」词根但语义已转移；第二组是对立或相邻的贸易主张。

entries.definition: Not held or restricted; alone it can describe a seat, a person or a service, with no reference to trade.
entries.definitionCN: 不受束缚或限制；单独使用时可以形容座位、人或服务，与贸易无关。

entries.definition: The state of being free; it is a condition, while free trade is a policy about exchange.
entries.definitionCN: 自由的状态；它是一种境况，而自由贸易是关于交换的政策。

entries.definition: Without restraint; it describes how an action is done, not what is traded.
entries.definitionCN: 不受限制地；它描述动作方式，不描述交易内容。

entries.definition: A person who is not a slave or serf; the word is historical and has no commercial sense.
entries.definitionCN: 非奴隶或农奴的人；这个词属历史用法，没有商业含义。

entries.definition: The process of reducing barriers; free trade is the end state or the doctrine, liberalization is the path.
entries.definitionCN: 降低壁垒的过程；自由贸易是终点或主张，自由化是路径。

entries.definition: Trade with few restrictions; it is less doctrinaire than free trade and often used by officials.
entries.definitionCN: 限制很少的贸易；它比自由贸易少一些教条色彩，官员常用。

entries.definition: The doctrine of minimal government interference in the economy; free trade is its application to external commerce.
entries.definitionCN: 政府尽量少干预经济的学说；自由贸易是它在对外贸易上的应用。

entries.definition: Trade governed by standards of wages, environment and producer treatment; it may accept tariffs to protect those standards.
entries.definitionCN: 受工资、环境与生产者待遇标准约束的贸易；它可能接受关税以保护这些标准。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real native root for free, the real trade word and real policy phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的本族「自由」词根、真实的贸易词与真实政策搭配。

normal.en: Free means no restraint and trade means exchange, so the phrase is exchange without border charges.
normal.cn: free 意为无束缚，trade 意为交换，短语就是没有边境收费的交换。

normal.en: Free is a native English word, while trade came through the Low Countries, so the phrase mixes two layers.
normal.cn: free 是英语本族词，trade 经低地国家传入，短语混合了两个层次。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the uses: free trade area, free trade agreement, free trade policy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示用法：自由贸易区、自由贸易协定、自由贸易政策。

normal.en: The standard opposite is protectionism, which puts barriers back.
normal.cn: 标准反义说法是保护主义，它把壁垒重新立起来。

normal.en: Free trade is a doctrine as well as a practice, so it takes verbs like advocate and defend.
normal.cn: 自由贸易既是做法也是主张，因此可带「倡导」「捍卫」这类动词。

abstract.en: Picture a checkpoint with the barrier raised and no ledger open on the desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一处关卡，栏杆抬起，桌上没有打开的账本。

abstract.en: Picture two markets joined by a road with no toll booth anywhere along it.
abstract.cn: 想象两个市场被一条路连起，路上没有一处收费站。

abstract.en: Picture ideas crossing a border as easily as grain, with nothing inspected.
abstract.cn: 想象观念像谷物一样越过边界，没有东西被查验。

examples.en: The party campaigned on free trade and lower prices.
examples.cn: 该党以自由贸易和更低物价为竞选主张。

examples.en: Free trade in agriculture was the hardest chapter to negotiate.
examples.cn: 农业自由贸易是最难谈的一章。

examples.en: Economists disagree about how fast free trade should be introduced.
examples.cn: 经济学家对自由贸易应以多快速度推行存在分歧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「自由地买卖」——free 是不受限制，trade 是买卖，货不受关卡阻挡就是自由贸易

root: free 源自古英语 freo「不受奴役」，属日耳曼语层；trade 源自古英语与中古低地德语中表示「路径、往来」的词。合指不受关税与配额限制的贸易。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a practice to a creed: trade without barriers, the doctrine, the regional arrangement, a single sector, the contrast with fair trade, the theory, the claimed effects and finally any unblocked flow.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从做法走向信条：无壁垒的贸易、其主张、区域安排、单一行业、与公平贸易的对照、其理论、其所宣称的效果，最后是任何不被堵塞的流动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised border barrier with no ledger open beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：抬起的边境栏杆，旁边没有打开的账本。

branches.en: BASE ABSENCE: exchange proceeds without tariffs or quotas.
branches.cn: 基础的无：交换在没有关税与配额的情况下进行。

branches.en: DOCTRINE AND THEORY: the practice becomes a creed with a reasoning behind it.
branches.cn: 主张与理论：做法变成信条，并带有其推理。

branches.en: SCOPE: the absence of barriers applies to a region or to one sector.
branches.cn: 范围：无壁垒状态适用于一个区域或一个行业。

branches.en: DEBATE: the phrase is defined against fair trade and judged by its effects.
branches.cn: 争论：这个短语在与公平贸易的对照中被定义，并按效果被评判。

branches.en: METAPHOR: any flow can be called free when nothing blocks it.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何流动在没有阻碍时都可以被称为自由。

intro.en: Free trade is a phrase of two free words, a native adjective and a Germanic noun of exchange.
intro.cn: free trade 由两个自由词构成，一个是英语本族形容词，一个是日耳曼来源的交换名词。

latinIntro.en: Neither half is Latin: free is native English and trade came through the Low Countries.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都不来自拉丁语：free 是英语本族词，trade 经低地国家传入。

definition_zh: 参数；参量；（可调的）指标；界限；限定因素
definition_en: a measurable quantity that defines a system or model and can be set or varied; also a limit that bounds what is possible
core_image: 一块写满公式的白板旁边，立着几根可调的刻度尺，每一根都决定曲线往哪边弯
scene: 实验室的白板上写着一个模型公式，旁边列着三个可调旋钮。 Each knob is a parameter of the model, and turning it changes the shape of the whole curve.
sceneCN: 这里 parameter 是「模型中的可调参量」（第 1 个义项：决定模型形状的量）；句意：每个旋钮都是模型的一个参数，拧动它就会改变整条曲线的形状。图中可辨识物件：白板公式、三个旋钮、刻度盘、曲线图、记号笔。

pos.zh: （数学）参数；参变量
（统计）总体参数
（计算机）参数；实参
（常用复数）界限；范围
限定因素；决定条件

senses.title: A value that shapes a model
senses.definition: in mathematics, a quantity that is fixed for one case but can vary between cases, and whose value determines the form of an equation or curve
senses.definitionCN: 数学中在单个情形里固定、但可在不同情形间变化的量，其取值决定方程或曲线的形态
senses.example: Changing the parameter a turns the circle into an ellipse.
senses.exampleCN: 改变参数 a，圆就变成了椭圆。
senses.why: Greek para- means beside and metron means measure: a parameter is a measure set beside the main variables. It does not move during one calculation, yet it decides the shape of the whole result.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 para- 是“在旁边”，metron 是“度量”：参数就是摆在主要变量旁边的一把尺。它在一次计算中不动，却决定整个结果的形状。

senses.title: The population parameter in statistics
senses.definition: in statistics, a true numerical characteristic of a whole population, usually unknown and estimated from a sample
senses.definitionCN: 统计学中整个总体的真实数值特征，通常未知，需由样本估计
senses.example: The population mean is a parameter, while the sample mean is a statistic.
senses.exampleCN: 总体均值是参数，样本均值是统计量。
senses.why: Statistics splits the unseen whole from the visible part. The parameter belongs to the whole and is therefore fixed but unknown; the statistic belongs to the sample and is calculated. The word keeps its sense of a measure that stands beside the data.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把看不见的总体与看得见的部分分开。参数属于总体，因而固定却未知；统计量属于样本，是被算出来的。这个词仍保留“摆在数据旁边的度量”之意。

senses.title: An argument passed to a function
senses.definition: in computing, a value supplied to a function, routine, or command that changes what it does
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中传给函数、例程或命令的值，用以改变其行为
senses.example: The function takes two parameters: a file name and a size.
senses.exampleCN: 这个函数接收两个参数：文件名和大小。
senses.why: A function is a small machine with settings. The values you hand it are measures set beside the operation, deciding which case it handles; programming simply inherited the mathematical word.
senses.whyCN: 函数是一台带设定的小机器。你交给它的值就是摆在操作旁边的度量，决定它处理哪一种情形；编程只是继承了数学里的这个词。

senses.title: A design or operating parameter
senses.definition: in engineering and design, a measurable specification that a product or process must meet
senses.definitionCN: 工程与设计中产品或过程必须满足的可测规格
senses.example: The bridge was built to withstand wind parameters far above the legal minimum.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥按远高于法定最低值的风力参数建造。
senses.why: An engineer cannot test every future wind. Instead the design is fixed to numbers that stand for the conditions, and those numbers are the parameters. The measure now controls the object rather than describing it.
senses.whyCN: 工程师无法测试未来每一种风。于是把设计固定在代表这些条件的数字上，这些数字就是参数。度量在这里不是描述对象，而是控制对象。

senses.title: The limits within which you may act
senses.definition: usually in the plural, the limits or boundaries that define what is possible or acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 通常用复数，指界定何为可能或可接受的界限
senses.example: We must work within the parameters of the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 我们必须在预算范围内工作。
senses.why: A parameter fixes a value, and a set of fixed values marks out a space of allowed cases. English speakers turned that space into a boundary, so working within parameters means staying inside the range the numbers permit.
senses.whyCN: 一个参数固定一个值，一组固定值就划出一片允许的情形空间。英语使用者把这片空间理解为边界，因此“在参数之内工作”就是待在这些数字允许的范围内。

senses.title: A limiting factor
senses.definition: a factor that limits or determines the character of a situation or outcome
senses.definitionCN: 限制或决定某一情形、结果性质的因素
senses.example: Cost is the main parameter of the project.
senses.exampleCN: 成本是这个项目的主要限定因素。
senses.why: This sense pushes the word from a number to a factor that behaves like a number: it sets the conditions others must fit. Some usage guides object that limit would be clearer, but the extension follows the same logic of a value that governs a range.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项把词从“一个数字”推到“像数字那样起作用的因素”：它设定别人必须迁就的条件。有些用法指南认为用 limit 更清楚，但这一扩展仍沿着“一个值支配一片范围”的逻辑。

senses.title: A measured physical quantity
senses.definition: in science, a measurable quantity such as temperature or pressure that characterizes a system
senses.definitionCN: 科学中表征系统的可测量，如温度或压力
senses.example: Temperature and salinity are the key parameters of the seawater model.
senses.exampleCN: 温度和盐度是海水模型的关键参数。
senses.why: Here the word comes close to its Greek parts again: a measure taken beside the system, entered into the model. The quantity is not the system itself but a number that stands for one aspect of it.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词又贴近了它的希腊成分：在系统旁边取得的一个度量，被输入模型。这个量不是系统本身，而是代表系统某一侧面的数字。

senses.title: A switch in universal grammar
senses.titleCN: 普遍语法中的一个参数
senses.definition: in linguistics, one of a small set of grammatical options that a language fixes, such as whether it drops subjects
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中一门语言所固定的少数语法选项之一，如是否允许省略主语
senses.example: The pro-drop parameter distinguishes Spanish from English.
senses.exampleCN: 省略主语参数把西班牙语与英语区分开来。
senses.why: In Chomskyan theory the universal grammar is a system with a few switches, and each switch is a parameter. The metaphor is exact: a small setting beside the main system, fixed to one value, which explains a whole family of surface differences.
senses.whyCN: 在乔姆斯基的理论里，普遍语法是一套带几个开关的系统，每个开关就是一个参数。这个比喻很精确：主系统旁边的一个小设定，固定为某个值，就能解释一整族表层差异。

intro.en: Parameter is a scientific coinage from two Greek parts. Its mathematical sense is old; the statistical, computing, and 'limits' senses are modern, and the last one is often criticised as an extension.
intro.cn: parameter 是由两个希腊成分构成的科学造词。其数学义较老；统计、计算与“界限”三义都是现代新增，最后一义常被批评为扩展过度。

items.en: Parameter appears in geometry, in the treatment of conic sections, meaning a fixed line or length used to describe a curve. It is formed in Modern Latin from Greek parts.
items.cn: parameter 于 17 世纪 50 年代出现在几何学中，用于讨论圆锥曲线，指描述曲线时使用的一条定线或定长。它是在近代拉丁语中用希腊成分构成的。

items.en: The parts are para- 'beside, subsidiary' and metron 'measure'. Metron goes back to PIE *me- 'to measure', the same family as meter, metre, and measure.
items.cn: 两个成分是 para-“在旁边、辅助”与 metron“度量”。metron 上溯原始印欧语 *me-“测量”，与 meter、metre、measure 同族。

items.en: The word spreads through mathematics as the general name for a quantity that is constant within a problem but can be varied between problems.
items.cn: 这个词在数学中扩散开来，泛指在单个问题内保持不变、但在不同问题之间可以变化的量。

items.en: Statistics adopts the term for a true characteristic of a population, as opposed to a statistic computed from a sample. The distinction becomes standard in sampling theory.
items.cn: 统计学采用这个术语，指总体的真实特征，与由样本算出的统计量相对。这一区分在抽样理论中成为标准。

items.en: The 'limits' sense spreads in general usage, probably helped by the sound of perimeter. Usage guides often call it imprecise, since a parameter is a value rather than a boundary, but the sense is now widespread in business and policy writing.
items.cn: “界限”义在一般用法中扩散，可能受到 perimeter 读音的影响。用法指南常说它不精确，因为参数是取值而不是边界；但在商业与政策写作中，这一义项如今已很常见。

note.en: The first group is the -meter family, which shares metron but differs in prefix; the second compares words for values, factors, and limits.
note.cn: 第一组是 -meter 词族，共享 metron 但前缀不同；第二组比较表示“取值、因素与界限”的词。

entries.definition: the distance around a closed shape. Its prefix is peri- 'around', and its sound has probably influenced the 'limits' sense of parameter.
entries.definitionCN: 封闭图形一周的长度。其前缀是 peri-“环绕”，它的读音很可能影响了 parameter 的“界限”义。

entries.definition: an instrument that measures air pressure. The second element is the same metron, the first is baros 'weight'.
entries.definitionCN: 测量气压的仪器。后半是同一个 metron，前半是 baros“重量”。

entries.definition: a straight line through the centre of a circle. Its dia- means across, so it is a measure across, not beside.
entries.definitionCN: 穿过圆心的直线。它的 dia- 意为“穿过”，所以是“横量”，而不是“旁量”。

entries.definition: an instrument for measuring temperature. Same metron, different prefix: heat
entries.definitionCN: 测量温度的仪器。同一个 metron，不同前缀：热。

entries.definition: a quantity that can change within a problem. A parameter is held fixed within one case, which is the standard contrast in modelling.
entries.definitionCN: 在一个问题内可以变化的量。参数在单个情形里保持固定，这是建模中的标准对照。

entries.definition: one of the elements that contributes to a result. It is causal and often qualitative, while parameter is measurable and settable.
entries.definitionCN: 促成结果的要素之一。它偏因果、常为定性，而 parameter 可测量、可设定。

entries.definition: the point beyond which something stops. It is the plain word for a boundary and is often recommended over parameter in the 'limits' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物停止的那条线。它是表示边界的最普通词，在“界限”义上常被建议用来替代 parameter。

entries.definition: a detailed requirement that a product must meet. It is a stated requirement, while a parameter is a quantity used to define or control the system.
entries.definitionCN: 产品必须满足的详细要求。它是被写明的规格，而 parameter 是用来定义或控制系统的一个量。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the two Greek parts, then three abstract images about settings that govern a range.
normalIntro.cn: 先用五个围绕两个希腊成分的挂钩，再用三个关于“设定支配范围”的抽象画面。

normal.en: para- beside, meter measure: a parameter is a measuring stick standing beside the equation.
normal.cn: para- 在旁边，meter 度量：参数就是立在方程旁边的一把量尺。

normal.en: Picture a sound desk: each slider is a parameter. Move one, and the whole sound changes.
normal.cn: 想象一张调音台：每个推子就是一个参数。推动一个，整个声音都变。

normal.en: A function call like draw(x, y, size) passes parameters; the brackets are where the settings go.
normal.cn: 像 draw(x, y, size) 这样的函数调用传的就是参数；括号就是放设定的地方。

normal.en: Statisticians pair them: parameter belongs to the population, statistic belongs to the sample. Whole versus part.
normal.cn: 统计学家把它们配对：参数属于总体，统计量属于样本。整体对部分。

normal.en: Beware perimeter: it sounds like parameter and means the line around a shape. Around is not beside.
normal.cn: 当心 perimeter：读音像 parameter，意思却是图形一周的线。around 不是 beside。

abstract.en: A parameter is a small decision that decides a large shape: one number fixed in advance, and a whole family of curves follows.
abstract.cn: 参数是一个决定大形状的小决定：一个数字事先定好，一整族曲线随之而来。

abstract.en: Parameters are the handles a system gives you. What you cannot reach is not a parameter but a constraint.
abstract.cn: 参数是系统交给你的把手。你够不到的东西不是参数，而是约束。

abstract.en: Naming a limit a parameter flatters it: it makes a wall sound like a dial.
abstract.cn: 把界限叫作参数是在给它贴金：让一堵墙听起来像一个旋钮。

examples.en: The model has three parameters, and each must be estimated from the data.
examples.cn: 这个模型有三个参数，每一个都必须由数据估计。

examples.en: You can adjust the display parameters in the settings menu.
examples.cn: 你可以在设置菜单里调整显示参数。

examples.en: The committee has to decide whether the plan falls within the parameters of the grant.
examples.cn: 委员会必须判断该计划是否落在资助范围内。

dict_mnemonic.note: para- 记成“在旁边”，meter 记成“量”：摆在主变量旁边、用来定形状的那个量，就是参数。
dict_mnemonic.text: para（在旁边）+ metron（度量）→ 旁边的量度 → 参数、参量；被引申为“界限”

root: 希腊 para-（在旁边、辅助）+ metron（度量，原始印欧语 *me-）→ 近代拉丁 parameter → 英语 parameter。

sensesIntro.en: The senses begin with a value set beside an equation, move to the unseen value of a population, to the value handed to a function, to the number a design must meet, then to the range those numbers allow, to a limiting factor, to a measured physical quantity, and finally to a switch in universal grammar.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从“摆在方程旁边的取值”开始，转到总体的未知值、传给函数的值、设计必须满足的数字，再由这些数字划出的范围，转到限定因素、可测物理量，最后落到普遍语法里的一个开关。

core.en: A row of adjustable scales standing beside one equation, each bending the curve
core.cn: 立在一条方程旁边的一排可调刻度，每一格都让曲线换形

branches.en: The model and the whole: a value that shapes an equation, and the true value of a population.
branches.cn: 模型与总体：决定方程形状的取值，以及总体的真实值。

branches.en: Inputs to systems: a value passed to a function, and a physical quantity fed into a model.
branches.cn: 系统的输入：传给函数的值，以及输入模型的物理量。

branches.en: Specification: the measurable numbers a design must meet.
branches.cn: 规格：一项设计必须满足的、可测量的数字。

branches.en: The disputed extension: a boundary treated as a factor, and a factor treated as a setting.
branches.cn: 有争议的扩展：把边界当作因素，又把因素当作设定。

branches.en: A switch in universal grammar: one of the few options a language fixes.
branches.cn: 普遍语法中的一个开关：一门语言所固定的少数选项之一。

intro.en: Parameter's family is technical and regular: the adjective, the adverb, the verb of setting parameters, and the participle. The prefix para- and the root metron are shared with a large measuring family.
intro.cn: parameter 的词族技术性强而规则：形容词、副词、表示“设定参数”的动词及其分词。前缀 para- 与词根 metron 与一个庞大的“测量”词族共享。

latinIntro.en: Modern Latin parameter was coined from Greek parts, and Latin metrum (from Greek metron) is the source of English metre and meter. The Greek compound, not a Latin root, is the true origin.
latinIntro.cn: 近代拉丁语 parameter 是用希腊成分新造的；拉丁语 metrum（来自希腊语 metron）则是英语 metre 与 meter 的来源。真正的源头是希腊复合词，而不是拉丁词根。

items.meaning: a fixed or settable quantity that defines a system
items.meaningCN: 定义系统的固定或可设定量
items.example: The parameter controls the slope of the line.
items.exampleCN: 这个参数控制直线的斜率。

items.meaning: expressed by or relating to parameters
items.example: The software builds parametric models.
items.exampleCN: 该软件构建参数化模型。

items.example: The curve is defined parametrically.
items.exampleCN: 这条曲线是用参数方式定义的。

items.meaning: to express or control something by parameters
items.meaningCN: 参数化；用参数表示或控制
items.example: They parameterized the model by grain size.
items.exampleCN: 他们按颗粒大小对模型进行参数化。

items.meaning: the act or result of expressing something in parameters
items.example: A good parameterization reduces the error.
items.exampleCN: 良好的参数化能降低误差。

items.meaning: set up so that values can be supplied
items.meaningCN: 已参数化的；可传入取值的
items.example: The parameterized query avoids injection.
items.exampleCN: 参数化查询可避免注入攻击。

items.example: Parallel, paramedic, parameter.
items.exampleCN: 平行的、急救员、参数。

items.example: Metron is the second half of parameter.
items.exampleCN: metron 是 parameter 的后半部分。

items.meaning: the measured line around a shape
items.meaningCN: 绕图形一周量出的线；周长
items.example: The perimeter of the square is four times one side.
items.exampleCN: 正方形的周长是一边长的四倍。

latinEntries.structure: Modern Latin coinage from Greek parts
latinEntries.meaning: a line or measure used to describe a curve
latinEntries.meaningCN: 用来描述曲线的一条定线或度量
latinEntries.example: Parameter entered English from the Latin of geometry.
latinEntries.exampleCN: parameter 经几何学的拉丁语进入英语。
拉丁语 metrum 给出英语 metre。

definition_zh: 宪法的；章程的；体质的；保健散步
definition_en: relating to a constitution (the body of laws governing a state) or to a person's physical constitution; also a daily walk taken for health
core_image: 国家的骨架与个人的骨架：一套支撑整体的基本规则
scene: 这里指「宪法的」。 The court struck down the law because it violated a constitutional right to free speech.
sceneCN: 这里 constitutional 是「宪法上的」（第 1 个义项：与国家宪法相关的）；句意：法院驳回了这部法律，因为它侵犯了宪法规定的言论自由权。图中可辨识物件：法庭、宪法文本、天平、法槌。

pos.zh: 宪法的；章程的；体质的
保健散步

senses.title: Relating to a nation's constitution
senses.titleCN: 宪法的；与国家宪法相关的
senses.definition: connected with or permitted by the set of basic laws by which a country is governed
senses.definitionCN: 与治理国家的基本法律体系相关或被其允许的
senses.example: The new law was challenged on constitutional grounds.
senses.exampleCN: 这部新法律以违宪为由受到质疑。
senses.why: Latin constituere means 'to set up, establish'. The constitution is what sets up the state; constitutional describes what belongs to that founding framework.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 constituere 意为「建立、设立」。宪法是设立国家的东西；constitutional 描述的是属于这一立国框架的事物。

senses.title: Allowed or required by a constitution
senses.definition: permitted or required by the constitution of a country or organization
senses.definitionCN: 被国家或组织的宪法所允许或要求的
senses.example: Free elections are a constitutional requirement in most democracies.
senses.exampleCN: 自由选举是大多数民主国家的宪法要求。
senses.why: The suffix -al turns the noun constitution into an adjective meaning 'of or belonging to the constitution'.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 把名词 constitution 变成形容词，意为「属于宪法的」。

senses.title: Relating to a person's physical makeup
senses.definition: relating to the structure or condition of a person's body or mind
senses.definitionCN: 与一个人身心的结构或状况相关的
senses.example: He has a strong constitutional resistance to colds.
senses.exampleCN: 他体质强健，不易感冒。
senses.why: Constitution can also mean the natural make-up of the body. Constitutional here describes qualities that come from that inbuilt structure.
senses.whyCN: constitution 也可指身体的自然构成。此处 constitutional 描述的是来自这种内在结构的特质。

senses.title: Relating to the make-up of something
senses.definition: relating to the composition or essential structure of something
senses.definitionCN: 与某物的组成或本质结构相关的
senses.example: There are constitutional weaknesses in the design of the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥的设计存在结构性弱点。
senses.why: The same root idea of 'what something is built from' applies to objects, not just people or states.
senses.whyCN: 「某物由什么构成」这一根义同样适用于物体，而不仅限于人或国家。

senses.title: A walk taken regularly for health
senses.definition: a walk taken regularly to keep or improve one's health
senses.definitionCN: 为保持或增进健康而定期进行的散步
senses.example: Grandpa takes his constitutional in the park every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 爷爷每天早上在公园作保健散步。
senses.why: A constitutional walk is one taken to benefit one's bodily constitution — the word shortens 'constitutional walk'.
senses.whyCN: 保健散步是为了有益于身体 constitution（体质）而进行的散步——这个词是 constitutional walk 的省略。

senses.title: Inherent in the basic structure
senses.definition: forming part of the essential nature or character of something
senses.definitionCN: 构成某物本质或特征的一部分的
senses.example: Courtesy is constitutional to his character.
senses.exampleCN: 礼貌是他性格中固有的特质。
senses.why: If a quality is constitutional, it is built into the fundamental make-up, like a clause written into a constitution.
senses.whyCN: 如果一种特质是 constitutional 的，它就被写入了基本构成，就像写进宪法的条款一样。

senses.title: Of or relating to constitutional law
senses.definition: belonging to the field of law that deals with constitutions
senses.definitionCN: 属于处理宪法的法律领域的
senses.example: She is a leading scholar of constitutional history.
senses.exampleCN: 她是宪法史领域的顶尖学者。
senses.why: This is the specialized sense used by legal scholars, narrowing the adjective to the study of constitutions.
senses.whyCN: 这是法律学者使用的专业义项，把这个形容词限定在宪法研究范围内。

senses.title: Beneficial to bodily health
senses.definition: tending to improve or preserve physical health
senses.definitionCN: 倾向于改善或保持身体健康的
senses.example: Sea air was once thought to be highly constitutional.
senses.exampleCN: 海风曾被认为极有益于健康。
senses.why: Something constitutional in this sense supports the body's constitution, much as a walk does.
senses.whyCN: 此义下的 constitutional 事物支持身体的体质，就像散步一样。

intro.en: Constitutional is an English adjective formed on the noun constitution, which comes from Latin constitutio. The chain is Latin verb → noun → adjective, with the English suffix -al.
intro.cn: constitutional 是在名词 constitution 上构成的英语形容词，constitution 来自拉丁 constitutio。链条是拉丁动词→名词→形容词，英语后缀是 -al。

items.en: constituere meant 'to set up, establish, appoint'. It is con- 'together' + statuere 'to place, set', from stare 'to stand'. The image is of placing things together so that a structure stands.
items.cn: constituere 意为「建立、设立、任命」。由 con-「一起」+ statuere「放置、设立」构成，statuere 来自 stare「站立」。画面是把东西放在一起，使一个结构站立起来。

items.en: The past participle constitutus gave the stem constitut-, used to build nouns. The sense shifts from the act of setting up to the result: what has been established.
items.cn: 过去分词 constitutus 提供了词干 constitut-，用于构成名词。意义从「设立的动作」转向「设立的结果」：已经建立的东西。

items.en: constitutio meant 'establishment, arrangement, decree, temperament'. It covered both political arrangements (a decree) and the natural arrangement of the body (temperament).
items.cn: constitutio 意为「建立、安排、法令、气质」。它既涵盖政治上的安排（法令），也涵盖身体的自然安排（气质）。

items.en: Old French constitution kept the political and physical senses. English borrowed it in the 14th century, at first for both law and bodily make-up.
items.cn: 古法语 constitution 保留了政治和身体两层意义。英语在 14 世纪借入，最初既指法律也指身体构成。

items.en: Around 1700, English added the suffix -al to make constitutional. At first it meant 'relating to the bodily constitution'; the political sense grew stronger after the American and French revolutions.
items.cn: 约 1700 年，英语加上后缀 -al 构成 constitutional。最初意为「与身体体质相关的」；政治意义在美国革命和法国革命之后逐渐增强。

items.en: Today constitutional is most common in law and politics, but the old bodily sense survives in the phrase 'a constitutional' (a health walk) and in references to physical constitution.
items.cn: 如今 constitutional 最常用于法律和政治，但旧的身体义在「a constitutional（保健散步）」和提及身体素质时仍然保留。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root stare/statue; the second contains words close in political or bodily meaning.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁词根 stare/statue；第二组是政治或身体意义相近的词。

entries.definition: the system of laws by which a country is governed; also a person's bodily make-up
entries.definitionCN: 国家治理的法律体系；也指人的身体构成

entries.definition: relating to an institution (an established organization or custom); from instituere 'to establish'
entries.definitionCN: 与机构（已建立的组织或习俗）相关的；来自 instituere「建立」

entries.definition: a voting member of a district; forming part of a whole. From constituere, -ent suffix
entries.definitionCN: 选区的投票成员；构成整体的一部分。来自 constituere，后缀 -ent

entries.definition: relating to the law in general; broader than constitutional, which specifically concerns the constitution
entries.definitionCN: 与一般法律相关的；比 constitutional 更广，constitutional 特指宪法

entries.definition: relating to the essential structure of something; close to the 'bodily make-up' sense of constitutional
entries.definitionCN: 与某物的本质结构相关的；接近 constitutional 的「身体构成」义

entries.definition: forming a necessary base or core; a constitutional right is one kind of fundamental right
entries.definitionCN: 构成必要基础或核心的；宪法权利是基本权利的一种

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes and real word relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分和真实同族词。

normal.en: con- 'together' + statuere 'to set up': the constitution sets up the state, and constitutional describes what that setup contains.
normal.cn: con-「一起」+ statuere「设立」：宪法设立国家，constitutional 描述这个设立所包含的东西。

normal.en: constitution is the noun (the document or the body); -al turns it into the adjective.
normal.cn: constitution 是名词（文件或身体）；-al 把它变成形容词。

normal.en: Constitutional walks were literally walks to improve one's constitution — the word shortens the phrase.
normal.cn: 保健散步字面就是改善体质的散步——这个词是短语的省略。

normal.en: in- flips the meaning: unconstitutional is what the constitution does not allow.
normal.cn: in- 翻转意义：unconstitutional 是宪法不允许的。

normal.en: institutional is the -al adjective of institution, just as constitutional is the -al adjective of constitution.
normal.cn: institutional 是 institution 的 -al 形容词，正如 constitutional 是 constitution 的 -al 形容词。

abstract.en: Think of a nation as a building: the constitution is the steel frame, and constitutional rights are the beams that cannot be removed.
abstract.cn: 把国家想象成一栋建筑：宪法是钢架，宪法权利是不能拆除的横梁。

abstract.en: Think of a person's health as their inner architecture; a constitutional walk gently exercises that structure.
abstract.cn: 把人的健康想象成内在的建筑结构；保健散步温和地锻炼这个结构。

abstract.en: Think of the word as 'constitution + all': everything belonging to the constitution is constitutional.
abstract.cn: 把这个词想成「constitution + all」：属于宪法的一切都是 constitutional。

examples.en: The court ruled that the new tax law violated a constitutional guarantee of equal treatment.
examples.cn: 法院裁定新税法违反了宪法保障的平等对待原则。

examples.en: She takes a thirty-minute constitutional along the river every evening.
examples.cn: 她每天傍晚沿河作三十分钟的保健散步。

examples.en: A constitutional weakness in the immune system makes him prone to infections.
examples.cn: 免疫系统的结构性弱点使他容易感染。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「康斯提图神」——康（con）壮的体质由神（stitution）设立 → constitutional 宪法的、体质的

root: 拉丁 constituere「建立、设立」（con-「一起」+ statuere「放置」，statuere 来自 stare「站立」）；constitution 名词 + -al 形容词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one idea of 'what a thing is built on': the state is built on its constitution, the body on its constitution, and an object on its structural make-up.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享「事物建立在什么之上」这一观念：国家建立在宪法之上，身体建立在体质之上，物体建立在其结构构成之上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a frame or skeleton that holds a whole together.
core.cn: 核心意象：把整体撑住的框架或骨架。

branches.en: POLITICAL FRAMEWORK: the constitution and its study form the legal skeleton of a state.
branches.cn: 政治框架：宪法及其研究构成国家的法律骨架。

branches.en: PERMISSION BY THE FOUNDING TEXT: what the constitution allows is constitutional.
branches.cn: 立国文本的许可：宪法允许的就是合宪的。

branches.en: INNER BUILD OF A PERSON: the body's constitution gives natural strengths and weaknesses.
branches.cn: 人的内在构成：身体的体质带来天生的强弱。

branches.en: STRUCTURE OF A THING: constitutional weaknesses are built into the design; constitutional air supports health.
branches.cn: 事物的结构：结构性弱点内建于设计；有益健康的空气支持体质。

branches.en: WALK FOR THE BODY: a constitutional is a walk meant to serve the body's constitution.
branches.cn: 为身体而走：保健散步是为服务身体体质而进行的散步。

intro.en: Constitutional is built on the noun constitution with the productive adjective suffix -al. The deeper parts (con-, statuere) are fossilized inside the base.
intro.cn: constitutional 是在名词 constitution 上加能产的形容词后缀 -al 构成。更深层的部分（con-、statuere）已凝固在词基内部。

latinIntro.en: Latin statuere 'to set up' and its parent stare 'to stand' produced a huge family: state, statue, status, station, institute, constitute, destitute. The root appears as stat-, stit-, or stan-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 statuere「设立」及其母体 stare「站立」产生了庞大词族：state、statue、status、station、institute、constitute、destitute。词根以 stat-、stit- 或 stan- 形式出现。

items.meaning: the act or result of establishing; a body of fundamental laws; bodily make-up
items.meaningCN: 宪法；体质；建立（-tion 构成行为或结果名词）
items.example: The constitution guarantees freedom of religion.
items.exampleCN: 宪法保障宗教信仰自由。

items.meaning: of or belonging to a constitution
items.meaningCN: 宪法的；体质的（-al 形容词后缀）
items.example: The amendment is a constitutional right.
items.exampleCN: 这项修正案是一项宪法权利。

items.example: The court declared the law unconstitutional.
items.exampleCN: 法院宣布该法律违宪。

items.meaningCN: 合宪性（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: Lawyers debated the constitutionality of the measure.
items.exampleCN: 律师们辩论该措施的合宪性。

items.meaning: a voting member; forming part of a whole
items.meaningCN: 选民；组成的（-ent 形容词/名词后缀）
items.example: Each constituent has the right to vote.
items.exampleCN: 每位选民都有投票权。

items.meaning: to make up or form something
items.example: Twelve people constitute a jury.
items.exampleCN: 十二个人组成一个陪审团。

items.example: The university is an old institution.
items.exampleCN: 这所大学是一个古老的机构。

items.example: A statue of the founder stands in the square.
items.exampleCN: 广场上矗立着创始人的雕像。

items.meaning: the legal or social position of a person
items.example: The status of the agreement is still unclear.
items.exampleCN: 该协议的地位仍不清楚。

definition_zh: 羊皮纸；写在羊皮纸上的文件；仿羊皮纸；羊皮纸色的
definition_en: animal skin prepared for writing; a document written on it; a modern paper imitating it
core_image: 修复台上放着一张半透明的动物皮纸，边缘磨得发亮，纤维在灯下隐约可见
scene: 修复台上摊着一页边缘卷曲的旧文书。 The oldest deed in the archive survives on a sheet of parchment.
sceneCN: 这里 parchment 指「经过处理的动物皮书写材料」（第 1 个义项：可书写的羊皮纸）；句意为档案馆里最古老的契约留存在一张羊皮纸上。

pos.zh: 羊皮纸；羊皮纸文件；仿羊皮纸
羊皮纸的；羊皮纸色的

derivatives.zh: parchment + -ize（动词后缀）→ 使呈羊皮纸状
parchment + -like（类似后缀）→ 像羊皮纸的
parchment + -er（从业者后缀）→ 制作羊皮纸的人
拉丁 vitulinum「小牛的」→ 小牛皮纸：更精细的皮纸
拉丁 pergamena + -eous（形容词后缀）→ 羊皮纸质的

senses.title: Animal skin prepared for writing
senses.titleCN: 经过处理可供书写的动物皮
senses.definition: the skin of a sheep, goat or calf, cleaned and stretched to receive writing
senses.definitionCN: 经清洗、拉伸、刮薄后可供书写的羊、山羊或小牛皮
senses.example: The oldest deed in the archive survives on a sheet of parchment.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆里最古老的契约留存在一张羊皮纸上。
senses.why: the word came from the Latin name for the material of Pergamon, so the substance itself is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自帕加马材料之名的拉丁语，因此材料本身是第一义。

senses.title: A document written on parchment
senses.definition: a document or legal instrument written on prepared animal skin
senses.definitionCN: 写在处理过的动物皮上的文件或法律文书
senses.example: The land grant is a parchment with three wax seals.
senses.exampleCN: 这份土地授予书是一张盖有三枚火漆印的羊皮纸文件。
senses.why: a material name commonly stands for the object made from it, as paper does for a sheet.
senses.whyCN: 材料名常转指用它做成的东西，就像 paper 也指一张纸。

senses.title: An old scroll or document
senses.definition: an old document, especially one rolled or folded and kept as an heirloom
senses.definitionCN: 古老的文件，尤指卷起或折起、被当作传家宝保存的
senses.example: The family kept the parchment rolled in a tin box.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人把那份羊皮纸文书卷起来放在铁盒里。
senses.why: because the material lasted, old records were often made of it, so age and material merged in the sense.
senses.whyCN: 由于这种材料耐久，旧记录常用它制成，年代与材料在词义中合流。

senses.title: Modern paper imitating parchment
senses.definition: stiff paper treated to look like animal skin, used for certificates, crafts or baking
senses.definitionCN: 经处理使其像动物皮的光滑硬纸，用于证书、手工或烘焙
senses.example: The invitation was printed on cream parchment.
senses.exampleCN: 邀请函印在米色仿羊皮纸上。
senses.why: industry copied the look of the old material and kept its name, a familiar pattern in paper names.
senses.whyCN: 工业复制了旧材料的外观并沿用其名，这在纸张名称中是常见模式。

senses.title: A ceremonial diploma
senses.definition: a formal diploma or award printed on parchment-like paper
senses.definitionCN: 印在仿羊皮纸上的正式文凭或奖状
senses.example: The university handed each graduate a parchment at the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 大学在典礼上给每位毕业生发了一张羊皮纸质地的文凭。
senses.why: ceremonies value the look of age, so a modern certificate borrows the old material's dignity.
senses.whyCN: 典礼看重年代感，因此现代证书借用了旧材料的庄重。

senses.title: A pale yellow papery texture
senses.definition: a colour and surface like old animal skin, pale yellow and slightly translucent
senses.definitionCN: 像旧动物皮一样的颜色与表面：浅黄、略带半透明
senses.example: The lampshade cast a parchment glow over the room.
senses.exampleCN: 灯罩在房间里投下一层羊皮纸般的柔光。
senses.why: the material's colour became an adjective for any surface with that warm, papery look.
senses.whyCN: 这种材料的颜色变成了形容词，用于任何带那种暖色纸感的事物。

senses.title: A drumhead material
senses.definition: a skin or synthetic sheet stretched over a drum
senses.definitionCN: 蒙在鼓上的皮膜或合成膜
senses.example: The drummer replaced the parchment before the recording.
senses.exampleCN: 鼓手在录音前换了鼓面。
senses.why: animal skin stretched tight is also what makes a drum speak, a physical reuse of the same material.
senses.whyCN: 绷紧的动物皮也正是让鼓发声的东西，是同一材料的实体再利用。

senses.title: Split sheepskin for bookbinding
senses.definition: a thin split of sheepskin used to cover books and bind documents
senses.definitionCN: 覆书或装订文件用的薄层羊皮
senses.example: The binder chose parchment for the spine because it wears well.
senses.exampleCN: 装订师选了羊皮纸做书脊，因为它耐磨。
senses.why: bookbinding kept the strongest form of the material, so the trade name survives in the craft.
senses.whyCN: 书籍装订保留了这种材料最结实的形态，行业名称因此在手艺中留存。

intro.en: Parchment came into English through Old French parchemin from Latin pergamena charta, 'paper of Pergamon'. The city's name supplies the word, and the story of its invention is a report we inherit rather than a proven fact.
intro.cn: parchment 经古法语 parchemin 来自拉丁 pergamena charta「帕加马的纸」。这个词由城市名而来，而关于它如何被发明的说法是继承下来的记述，并非已证事实。

items.en: Pergamenos was the adjective for Pergamon, a city in Asia Minor famous for its library.
items.cn: Pergamenos 是小亚细亚城市帕加马的形容词，该城以图书馆闻名。

items.en: Latin pergamena charta meant 'Pergamene paper', the writing material associated with the city.
items.cn: 拉丁 pergamena charta 意为「帕加马的纸」，指与这座城市相关的书写材料。

items.en: Old French shortened the phrase into parchemin, the form English encountered.
items.cn: 古法语把短语缩成 parchemin，英语遇到的就是这个形式。

items.en: English borrowed the word for the prepared skin and soon for documents written on it.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入这个词，先指处理过的皮，很快也指写在其上的文件。

items.en: It is generally thought that Pergamon developed the material when Egypt restricted papyrus exports, but the story rests on an ancient report and is not independently proven.
items.cn: 一般认为，帕加马在埃及限制纸草出口时发展出这种材料；但此说依据的是一则古代记述，未经独立证实。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the earliest English use is dated differently across dictionaries, though the Old French and Latin chain is solid.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：各词典给出的英语首见年代不一，但古法语与拉丁链条可靠。

note.en: Group one holds materials and book forms easily confused with parchment; group two holds general words for old written records.
note.cn: 第一组是容易与 parchment 混淆的材料与书籍形态；第二组是泛指古老文字记录的词。

entries.definition: A smoother, finer skin, usually calf, used for luxury books; parchment is the broader and coarser term.
entries.definitionCN: 更光滑精细的皮，通常取自小牛，用于精装书；parchment 是更宽、更粗的一类。

entries.definition: A parchment or other sheet scraped clean and written on again; it is a use of parchment, not the material.
entries.definitionCN: 被刮净后再次书写的羊皮纸或其他纸页；它是羊皮纸的用法，而非材料本身。

entries.definition: A document rolled for storage; it may be parchment, paper or other material.
entries.definitionCN: 为保存而卷起的文件；材料可能是羊皮纸、纸或其他。

entries.definition: A book of bound leaves; parchment may be its pages, but the codex is the binding form.
entries.definitionCN: 装订成册的书；羊皮纸可作书页，但册页本说的是装订形态。

entries.definition: The modern writing sheet made from wood or rag fibre; parchment is animal skin or its imitation.
entries.definitionCN: 用木浆或破布纤维制成的现代书写纸；parchment 是动物皮或其仿制品。

entries.definition: Any written record; parchment names the material or an old formal record.
entries.definitionCN: 任何书面记录；parchment 指材料或古老正式文书。

entries.definition: A formal legal document, often historically written on parchment; the legal act is the point.
entries.definitionCN: 正式法律文书，历史上常写在羊皮纸上；重点在法律行为。

entries.definition: The skin of a sheep as a material or as a diploma slang; parchment is the prepared writing surface.
entries.definitionCN: 羊皮原料或文凭的口语说法；parchment 是加工后的书写表面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the city name, the Old French form and the real craft materials.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：城市名、古法语形式与真实的手工艺材料。

normal.en: Pergamon is the city hidden inside the word.
normal.cn: 帕加马就是藏在词里的那座城市。

normal.en: Old French parchemin is the direct parent of the English form.
normal.cn: 古法语 parchemin 是英语形式的直接来源。

normal.en: Parchment is skin; vellum is the finer calfskin version.
normal.cn: parchment 是皮纸；vellum 是更精细的小牛皮纸。

normal.en: A palimpsest is a parchment scraped and used twice.
normal.cn: 重写本是被刮净后二次使用的羊皮纸。

normal.en: Modern parchment paper copies the look for baking and certificates.
normal.cn: 现代仿羊皮纸为烘焙与证书复制了这种外观。

abstract.en: Parchment is an animal's back turned into a page of law.
abstract.cn: 羊皮纸是把动物的背变成一页法律。

abstract.en: It is a surface that remembers the knife that thinned it.
abstract.cn: 它是一个记得那把削薄它的刀的表面。

abstract.en: Old deeds feel heavy because the material once carried a living body.
abstract.cn: 旧契约显得沉重，因为材料曾承载过一个活着的身体。

examples.en: The scribe copied the charter onto a fresh sheet of parchment.
examples.cn: 抄写员把特许状抄到一张新的羊皮纸上。

examples.en: Bake the cookies on parchment paper so they do not stick.
examples.cn: 把饼干放在烘焙纸上烤，以免粘住。

examples.en: The parchment was so old that the ink had faded to brown.
examples.cn: 那羊皮纸太旧了，墨迹已褪成褐色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pergam（帕加马）+ ent」——帕加马城发明的书写皮纸 → 羊皮纸

root: 拉丁 pergamena charta「帕加马的纸」→ 古法语 parchemin → 英语 parchment；城市名源自希腊 Pergamon。发明经过为古代记述，一般认为可信但未独立证实。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one material: prepared skin, the document written on it, an old record, its modern imitation, a diploma, its colour, a drumhead and a binding.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一种材料展开：处理过的皮、写在其上的文件、古老记录、现代仿制品、文凭、颜色、鼓面与装订。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin, pale animal skin stretched tight, waiting for ink and outlasting the hand that wrote.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张绷紧的浅色薄兽皮，等着墨迹，也比写字的手活得更久。

branches.en: STRETCHED SKIN: a writing sheet and a drumhead are the same animal surface pulled tight for two purposes.
branches.cn: 绷紧的皮：书写纸与鼓面是同一张兽皮为两种用途绷紧。

branches.en: MATERIAL BECOMES RECORD: the document and the old scroll are the skin carrying memory.
branches.cn: 材料成为记录：文件与古老卷轴都是承载记忆的皮。

branches.en: MODERN COPY: imitation paper and a diploma borrow the old look for new ceremonies.
branches.cn: 现代复制：仿制纸与文凭为新仪式借用旧外观。

branches.en: COLOUR MEMORY: the pale tone keeps the material visible in lampshades and rooms.
branches.cn: 颜色记忆：浅黄色调让材料在灯罩与房间里继续可见。

branches.en: CRAFT USE: split sheepskin survives as a bookbinding material.
branches.cn: 手艺用途：劈层羊皮作为装订材料留存。

intro.en: Parchment is a place name turned material name, and its family includes both craft terms and ordinary paper words.
intro.cn: parchment 是由地名变成的材料名，其词族既含手工艺词，也含普通纸张词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pergamena charta carries the Greek city adjective; English took the shortened French form, not the full Latin phrase.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pergamena charta 承载希腊城市形容词；英语取的是缩短后的法语形式，而非完整拉丁短语。

items.example: The city name sits inside the material word.
items.exampleCN: 城市名藏在材料词里。

items.example: The adjective renamed the writing skin.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词重新命名了书写用皮。

items.example: The Latin phrase literally said Pergamene paper.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁短语字面就是「帕加马的纸」。

items.example: French shortened the phrase for everyday use.
items.exampleCN: 法语把短语缩短以供日常使用。

items.example: The deed was written on parchment.
items.exampleCN: 契约写在羊皮纸上。

items.example: Vellum is smoother than parchment.
items.exampleCN: 小牛皮纸比羊皮纸更光滑。

items.example: The palimpsest hides an older text beneath.
items.exampleCN: 重写本下面藏着更早的文本。

items.example: The process parchmentizes the surface.
items.exampleCN: 这道工序让表面呈羊皮纸状。

latinEntries.structure: pergamena, -ae (f., first declension; adjective used as noun, from Greek)

derivatives.zh: parchment + -ize（动词后缀）→ 使呈羊皮纸状
parchment + -like（类似后缀）→ 像羊皮纸的
parchment + -er（从业者后缀）→ 羊皮纸制作者
拉丁 vitulinum「小牛的」→ 精细小牛皮纸
pergamena + -eous（形容词后缀）→ 羊皮纸质的

definition_zh: 提供信息的；增长见识的；有教益的；内容充实的
definition_en: giving useful facts or knowledge; instructive and rich in content
core_image: 一张折叠地图上密密标着水系、海拔和村名——看的人什么都没做，脑子里的地图却变厚了
scene: 这里指「提供信息的」。 The lecture was surprisingly informative: every slide carried a map and a number.
sceneCN: 这里 informative 是「提供有用信息的」（第 1 个义项：给出有用事实或细节的）；句意：这场讲座出乎意料地有信息量，每张幻灯片都带着地图和数字。图中可辨识物件：投影幕、幻灯片、笔记本。

pos.zh: 提供信息的；增长见识的；有教益的

senses.title: Giving useful facts
senses.titleCN: 提供有用信息的：看完能多知道几件事
senses.definition: giving facts or details that are useful to the reader or listener
senses.definitionCN: 向读者或听者提供有用事实或细节的
senses.example: The pamphlet is short but very informative.
senses.exampleCN: 这本小册子很短，但信息量很大。
senses.why: Informative is inform plus -ive 'having the nature of'. To inform is to give a shape to a mind; an informative text is one that actually presses that shape in.
senses.whyCN: informative 是 inform 加 -ive「具有某种性质的」。inform 是给头脑塑形；一篇 informative 的文字，就是确实把形状压进去的文字。

senses.title: Teaching and instructive
senses.titleCN: 有教益的：不只是知道，还学到
senses.definition: giving knowledge in a way that teaches or improves the reader
senses.definitionCN: 以能教导或提升读者的方式给予知识的
senses.example: The documentary was an informative account of the migration.
senses.exampleCN: 这部纪录片是对这场迁徙的有教益的记述。
senses.why: The oldest sense of informare is 'to instruct, form the mind'. The adjective keeps that educational tone: what is informative leaves the mind better shaped than before.
senses.whyCN: informare 最古老的意义是「教导、塑造头脑」。这个形容词保留着教育语调：informative 的东西让头脑比先前塑得更好。

senses.title: Dense with content
senses.titleCN: 内容充实的：每一页都装得下东西
senses.definition: containing a large amount of information in relation to its length
senses.definitionCN: 相对于篇幅而言含有大量信息的
senses.example: It is the most informative chapter in the book.
senses.exampleCN: 这是全书内容最充实的一章。
senses.why: A page is informative in proportion to how much shape it puts into the reader's mind per line. Density is the modern measure of the old shaping act.
senses.whyCN: 一页文字有多 informative，取决于每一行能给读者的头脑压进多少形状。密度是那个古老塑形动作的现代量度。

senses.title: Well-researched and detailed
senses.titleCN: 资料翔实的：细节经过查证
senses.definition: based on thorough research and full of verified detail
senses.definitionCN: 基于充分研究、充满经核实细节的
senses.example: The report is informative about costs and timelines.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告在成本和工期方面资料翔实。
senses.why: Research supplies verified particulars. The word then describes the shaping as thorough rather than merely plentiful: the details fit together.
senses.whyCN: 研究提供经核实的细节。此时这个词描述的是塑形之彻底，而不只是数量之多：细节彼此咬合。

senses.title: Revealing and illuminating
senses.titleCN: 能说明问题的：把原本看不见的照亮
senses.definition: helping one understand a situation by revealing something previously unclear
senses.definitionCN: 通过揭示先前不清楚之处来帮助理解局势的
senses.example: The comparison is informative about how the two systems differ.
senses.exampleCN: 这项比较能说明两个体系如何不同。
senses.why: Something revealing opens a closed shape: the new facts rearrange the reader's picture, so the information is felt as light rather than volume.
senses.whyCN: 能揭示事物的东西会打开一个封闭的形状：新事实重新排列读者心中的图景，于是信息被感受为光，而不是体积。

senses.title: Clear in conveying data
senses.titleCN: 标示清楚的：图表和标签一眼能读懂
senses.definition: of a label, chart, or sign, presenting data clearly enough to be understood
senses.definitionCN: 指标签、图表或标志清楚呈现数据、足以被理解的
senses.example: The map uses informative colours instead of decoration.
senses.exampleCN: 这张地图用的是说明性的颜色，而不是装饰。
senses.why: On a chart or label, informativeness is literal: the form must be legible before it can shape understanding. A beautiful label that cannot be read is not informative.
senses.whyCN: 在图表或标签上，信息性是字面意义上的：形式必须先可读，才能塑形理解。一个漂亮却读不懂的标签并不 informative。

senses.title: An educational experience
senses.titleCN: 有教益的经历：走一趟，人变了
senses.definition: of an experience, teaching one something lasting
senses.definitionCN: 指一段经历，使人学到持久的东西
senses.example: A week in the clinic proved more informative than any textbook.
senses.exampleCN: 在诊所的一周比任何教科书都更有教益。
senses.why: An experience informs when it leaves a durable shape in memory. The adjective shifts from the source to its effect on a person.
senses.whyCN: 一段经历能 inform，是因为它在记忆里留下持久的形状。这个形容词从信息源转向了对人的效果。

senses.title: Conveying meaning without words
senses.titleCN: 传达信息的：一个眼神也带着消息
senses.definition: of a look, gesture, or expression, communicating something to an observer
senses.definitionCN: 指眼神、手势或表情向观察者传达某种信息的
senses.example: She shot him an informative glance across the table.
senses.exampleCN: 她在桌子那头向他投去一个意味深长的眼神。
senses.why: A glance can inform without words: the face takes a form the other reads. The adjective extends to any sign that carries meaning.
senses.whyCN: 一个眼神不用言语也能 inform：面部取得一种被对方读取的形状。这个形容词于是扩展到任何承载意义的信号。

senses.title: Telling in statistics
senses.titleCN: 有说明力的：数字一摆，判断就变
senses.definition: of figures or results, revealing a pattern that changes one's judgment
senses.definitionCN: 指数字或结果揭示出改变判断的模式
senses.example: The dropout rates are especially informative.
senses.exampleCN: 辍学率尤其能说明问题。
senses.why: Statistics are called informative when they change a judgment, not merely when they are numerous. The old measure of effect survives inside the modern quantitative use.
senses.whyCN: 统计数字被称为 informative，是因为它们改变了判断，而不只是数量多。古老的「效果」量度保存在现代定量用法里。

intro.en: Informative is inform plus the adjective suffix -ive, from Latin -ivus 'having the nature of'. It shares the base forma with information, but it describes the source that gives shape rather than the shape received.
intro.cn: informative 是 inform 加形容词后缀 -ive，后者来自拉丁 -ivus「具有某种性质的」。它与 information 共享词基 forma，但描述的是塑形的来源，而不是被接收的形状。

items.en: forma 'shape, mould' is the base. The family always keeps the idea of an outline imposed on something plastic, whether clay or a mind.
items.cn: 词基是 forma「形状、模子」。这个词族始终保留「把轮廓加在可塑之物上」的观念，无论那东西是黏土还是头脑。

items.en: in- 'into' plus formare 'to shape' gives 'to mould, to form the mind, to instruct'. The teaching sense is the one that produced informative.
items.cn: in-「向内」加 formare「塑形」得到「塑造、塑造头脑、教导」。产生 informative 的正是这个教导义。

items.en: Latin -ivus means 'having the nature of, tending to'. English -ive is its borrowed form, visible in instructive, active, and creative.
items.cn: 拉丁 -ivus 意为「具有某种性质的、倾向于」。英语 -ive 是它的借入形式，在 instructive、active、creative 中都能看到。

items.en: English built informative on inform with -ive. The word is recorded from the seventeenth century, first close to 'formative', then settling into 'giving information'.
items.cn: 英语用 inform 加 -ive 构成 informative。这个词自 17 世纪有记录，最初接近「有塑形作用的」，后来稳定为「提供信息的」。

items.en: As information shifted toward 'facts', informative shifted with it: from 'shaping the mind' to 'supplying facts that shape the mind'. The educational trace remains in the 'instructive' sense.
items.cn: 随着 information 转向「事实」，informative 也跟着转：从「塑造头脑」转为「提供能塑造头脑的事实」。教育痕迹仍留在「有教益」这一义项里。

items.en: Modern usage separates informative from informed: a book is informative, while a reader is informed. The first describes the source, the second the person who received the shape.
items.cn: 现代用法把 informative 与 informed 分开：书是 informative，读者是 informed。前者描述来源，后者描述接受了形状的人。

note.en: The first group is built on inform and forma, except informal, which uses a different in- meaning 'not'. The second group contains words that also praise what teaches or reveals, but from other roots.
note.cn: 第一组建立在 inform 与 forma 上，只有 informal 例外，它用的是另一个表示「不」的 in-。第二组是同样用来称赞「有教益、能揭示」之物、但词根不同的词。

entries.definition: to tell someone facts; literally to give the mind a shape. Informative is its -ive adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 告知某人事实；字面是给头脑塑形。informative 是它的 -ive 形容词。

entries.definition: facts or knowledge communicated. It names the content; informative names the quality of the source.
entries.definitionCN: 被传递的事实或知识。它指内容本身，informative 指来源的性质。

entries.definition: having facts; knowledgeable. A person is informed, but a book is informative; the pair divides receiver from source.
entries.definitionCN: 知情的；有知识的。人是 informed，书是 informative；这对词把接收者与来源分开。

entries.definition: relaxed, unofficial. It is in- 'not' plus formalis, not the in- 'into' of informare; the shared letters hide two different prefixes.
entries.definitionCN: 非正式的；放松的。它是 in-「不」加 formalis，不是 informare 的 in-「向内」；相同的字母掩盖了两个不同的前缀。

entries.definition: giving instruction or a lesson. It stresses the moral or practical lesson; informative stresses the supply of facts.
entries.definitionCN: 有指导意义的。它强调道德或实践上的教训，informative 强调事实的供给。

entries.definition: intended to teach or improve. It points to a purpose, while informative points to the amount of knowledge actually delivered.
entries.definitionCN: 有教育目的的。它指向目的，informative 指向实际传递的知识量。

entries.definition: making something hidden known. It stresses disclosure; informative can also mean merely full of detail.
entries.definitionCN: 揭示隐藏之事的。它强调披露，informative 也可以只表示细节丰富。

entries.definition: helping one understand by casting light on a subject. It is closer to the 'revealing' sense of informative than to its 'fact-filled' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 使理解变清楚的。它更接近 informative 的「揭示」义，而不是「充满事实」义。

normalIntro.en: The family is one shaping act seen from three sides: the mould (forma), the act of pressing it in (inform), and the quality of a thing that presses it in well (informative).
normalIntro.cn: 这个词族是从三个方向看同一个塑形动作：模子（forma）、把形状压进去的动作（inform），以及一块能把它压进去的好材料（informative）。

normal.en: inform + -ive: informative = having the nature of informing, that is, of shaping the mind with facts.
normal.cn: inform + -ive：informative = 具有 inform 性质的，也就是能用事实给头脑塑形。

normal.en: The base is forma 'shape', so an informative talk is one that leaves a shape behind, not one that merely makes noise.
normal.cn: 词基是 forma「形状」，所以 informative 的讲座是留下形状的讲座，而不只是发出声音。

normal.en: informative describes the source; informed describes the person. A book informs, and the reader becomes informed.
normal.cn: informative 描述来源，informed 描述人。书在 inform，读者则变得 informed。

normal.en: If you can say 'I learned something', the thing was informative; if you can only say 'I heard a lot', it was merely long.
normal.cn: 如果你能说「我学到了东西」，那东西就是 informative；如果你只能说「我听了许多」，那只是冗长。

normal.en: informal looks like a sibling but carries in- 'not'; it belongs to formal, not to forma.
normal.cn: informal 看着像兄弟，却带着 in-「不」；它属于 formal，不属于 forma。

abstract.en: Think of a mind as soft clay and a good lecture as a mould: informative is the mould's property, not the clay's.
abstract.cn: 把头脑想成软泥，把好讲座想成模子：informative 是模子的性质，不是泥的性质。

abstract.en: Think of a map that adds a contour line each time you look: every added line is a fact, and the map is informative because it becomes more navigable.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，每次看都多出一条等高线：每条新增的线就是一个事实，地图之所以 informative，是因为它变得更好用。

abstract.en: Think of a window opened in a dark room: informative is not the amount of glass but the amount of light that gets through.
abstract.cn: 想象在暗室里打开一扇窗：informative 不在于玻璃多少，而在于透进来多少光。

examples.en: The museum's audio guide is brief but remarkably informative.
examples.cn: 博物馆的语音导览简短，却极有信息量。

examples.en: We had an informative meeting with the engineers about the delays.
examples.cn: 我们和工程师就延误问题开了一次很有收获的会。

examples.en: The chart is informative because it compares costs per kilometre, not just totals.
examples.cn: 这张图之所以能说明问题，是因为它比较的是每公里成本，而不只是总额。

dict_mnemonic.note: 拆词联想 · 词源辅助
dict_mnemonic.text: in（向内）+ form（形状）+ ative（具有某种性质的）——能把形状压进你脑子里的东西，就是「提供信息的、有教益的」；同族 information 指压进去的那个形状。

root: inform「告知、塑形」（拉丁 informare ← in-「向内」+ forma「形状」）+ -ive（拉丁 -ivus「具有某种性质的」）；与 information 同源，词基同为 forma。informative 描述来源，informed 描述接收者。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all measure one thing: how much shape a source presses into a mind. A text, a chart, a class, a glance, or a statistic can each carry that shaping force.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都在衡量同一件事：一个来源能把多少形状压进头脑。一段文字、一张图表、一堂课、一个眼神或一组统计，都能携带这种塑形之力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a source that leaves the receiver's mind better shaped than before.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个让接收者头脑比先前塑得更好的来源。

branches.en: FACT AND DENSITY: useful facts supplied, and the amount of them packed into a given space.
branches.cn: 事实与密度：提供有用事实，以及在给定篇幅里装进多少事实。

branches.en: TEACHING: a text that instructs, and an experience that leaves a lasting lesson.
branches.cn: 教导：教导人的文字，以及留下持久教益的经历。

branches.en: THOROUGHNESS AND CLARITY: verified detail, and a form legible enough to be read.
branches.cn: 翔实与清楚：经核实的细节，以及清楚到足以被读懂的形式。

branches.en: REVELATION: a comparison or a set of figures that rearranges one's judgment.
branches.cn: 揭示：重新排列判断的比较或一组数字。

branches.en: THE WORDLESS SIGN: a look or gesture that carries a message.
branches.cn: 无言的信号：一个携带消息的眼神或手势。

intro.en: Informative is inform plus -ive. The suffix is productive and Latin in origin; the base goes back through French to Latin informare, itself in- plus forma. The word therefore has two suffixes in its history: -ation in information and -ive in informative.
intro.cn: informative 是 inform 加 -ive。这个后缀能产，源自拉丁；词基经法语上溯拉丁 informare，而 informare 本身是 in- 加 forma。因此这个词的历史里有两个后缀：information 里的 -ation 与 informative 里的 -ive。

latinIntro.en: Latin forma 'shape' and informare 'to shape, instruct' supply the base. The suffix -ivus 'having the nature of' yields English -ive, also seen in active, passive, and creative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 forma「形状」与 informare「塑形、教导」提供词基。后缀 -ivus「具有某种性质的」产生英语 -ive，也见于 active、passive、creative。

items.meaning: to give the mind a shape; to tell
items.example: The nurse informed him of the test results.
items.exampleCN: 护士把检验结果告诉了他。

items.meaning: what is communicated; the shaping of a mind
items.meaningCN: 被传递的内容；对头脑的塑形
items.example: The website offers information on local clinics.
items.exampleCN: 这个网站提供本地诊所的信息。

items.meaning: having the nature of informing; giving facts
items.meaningCN: 具有告知性质的；提供事实的
items.example: The briefing was clear and informative.
items.exampleCN: 这次简报清楚而富有信息。

items.meaningCN: 已获得事实的；有见识的
items.example: The decision was made by an informed committee.
items.exampleCN: 这个决定由一个知情的委员会作出。

items.example: The report is informatively illustrated.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告的插图很有说明性。

items.example: They tested the informativeness of different labels.
items.exampleCN: 他们测试了不同标签的信息量。

items.example: The researcher interviewed three informants.
items.exampleCN: 研究者采访了三位信息提供者。

items.example: Uninformed rumours spread quickly online.
items.exampleCN: 缺乏根据的谣言在网上迅速传播。

items.meaning: not formal; a different prefix from inform
items.meaningCN: 非正式的（in- 意为「不」，与 inform 的前缀不同）
items.example: They held an informal meeting in the corridor.
items.exampleCN: 他们在走廊里开了一次非正式会议。

latinEntries.meaning: having the nature of, tending to
latinEntries.meaningCN: 具有某种性质的；倾向于

definition_zh: 可靠地；稳定地；有把握地；可信地；不出差错地
definition_en: in a way that can be trusted to give accurate, consistent, or dependable results
core_image: 校准台上摆着一排相同的砝码，每次称量，指针都停在同一格刻度上。
scene: 实验室主管让学生把同一份样品连测三次，三次读数几乎分毫不差，她这才同意把数据写进报告。 The instrument reliably gave the same reading three times, so the results could be trusted in the report.
sceneCN: 这里 reliably 是“稳定可靠地得出结果”（第 1 个义项）；句意：三次读数一致，结果可信，可以写进报告。

pos.zh: 可靠地；稳定地；有把握地

senses.title: Results you can trust
senses.titleCN: 可靠地：结果经得起信任
senses.definition: in a way that produces results a person can trust without checking every step
senses.definitionCN: 以让人无须逐步核查也能信任其结果的方式
senses.example: The sensor reliably reports the temperature to within half a degree.
senses.exampleCN: 这个传感器能可靠地把温度报告到半度以内。
senses.why: The suffix -ly turns the adjective reliable into a manner; reliable itself comes from rely, to bind fast, so the manner described is one that does not slip.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ly 把形容词 reliable 变成方式副词；reliable 出自 rely“牢牢绑住”，因此这种做事方式不会松脱走样。

senses.title: The same every time
senses.titleCN: 稳定重现：每次都是同一个结果
senses.definition: in a way that repeats the same outcome under the same conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在相同条件下重复得出同一结果的方式
senses.example: The recipe reliably produces the same crumb every time she bakes it.
senses.exampleCN: 她每次烘烤，这个配方都稳定地做出同样的组织。
senses.why: Repetition is the practical test of reliability: if the outcome moves about, the method cannot be trusted, however good a single trial looks.
senses.whyCN: 重复是可靠性的实际检验：结果若飘忽不定，方法就不可信，单次试验再漂亮也没有用。

senses.title: Machines that do not fail
senses.titleCN: 不出差错地：设备与服务靠得住
senses.definition: with a low rate of failure, especially of machines, systems, or services
senses.definitionCN: 故障率很低，尤指机器、系统或服务
senses.example: The backup generator has run reliably through three winter storms.
senses.exampleCN: 这台备用发电机经历了三场冬季风暴，一直运行可靠。
senses.why: When the subject is a machine, reliability is counted in hours of service rather than in truth; -ly still marks the manner of working.
senses.whyCN: 主语是机器时，可靠性以服务时长而不是以真假来衡量；-ly 标记的仍是运行的方式。

senses.title: A source worth believing
senses.titleCN: 有把握地：消息来源可信
senses.definition: in a way that shows the speaker has sound grounds for what is said
senses.definitionCN: 表现出说话者对所言有可靠依据的方式
senses.example: She is reliably informed that the talks will resume next month.
senses.exampleCN: 据她可靠的消息，会谈将于下月恢复。
senses.why: The phrase reliably informed moves the word from things to testimony: reliability now belongs to the channel that supplies the news.
senses.whyCN: reliably informed 把词从“事物”移到“证言”：这里的可靠性属于提供消息的那个渠道。

senses.title: Measured with little error
senses.definition: with a small margin of error when a value is measured or estimated
senses.definitionCN: 测量或估计数值时误差很小
senses.example: Satellite data can reliably estimate the area of open water.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星数据能可靠地估算开阔水域的面积。
senses.why: Accuracy is closeness to a true value; reliability is getting that closeness again and again. The adverb often carries both at once.
senses.whyCN: 准确讲的是与真值接近，可靠讲的是能否一次次保持这种接近；这个副词常常两者兼有。

senses.title: Predictable in advance
senses.titleCN: 可预期地：事先就能算准
senses.definition: in a way that allows an outcome to be forecast before it happens
senses.definitionCN: 使结果能在发生之前就被预测的方式
senses.example: Demand for electricity reliably peaks on the hottest afternoons.
senses.exampleCN: 用电需求可靠地在最热的下午达到高峰。
senses.why: A pattern that can be counted on becomes a planning tool; predictability is reliability seen from the future looking back.
senses.whyCN: 能被指望的规律就成了规划工具；可预测性是从未来往回看的可靠性。

senses.title: Holding up over time
senses.definition: continuing to work well over a long period without sudden loss of quality
senses.definitionCN: 长时间持续良好运转，质量不突然下滑
senses.example: The bridge has carried traffic reliably for over eighty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥已可靠地承载交通八十余年。
senses.why: Durability adds a time axis: a thing may work well today yet be unreliable if it fails soon, so the adverb claims endurance.
senses.whyCN: 耐久性加上了时间轴：某物今天好用，若不久就坏仍不可靠；这个副词主张的是持久。

senses.title: Safely assumed in reasoning
senses.titleCN: 可信地：推理中可当前提
senses.definition: used to say that something may be taken as true in an argument
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示在某论证中可以把某事当作真的
senses.example: We can reliably assume that any sample drawn this way is unbiased.
senses.exampleCN: 我们可以可信地假定，这样抽取的样本没有偏差。
senses.why: In logic the adverb licenses an inference rather than describing an action; reliability means the premise will not betray the conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 在逻辑里这个副词是给推理发放许可，而不是描述动作；可靠意味着前提不会让结论落空。

intro.en: Reliably is rely plus -able plus -ly. The Latin source is religare, to bind fast, whose participle gave the idea of something tied so that it cannot slip.
intro.cn: reliably 由 rely 加 -able 再加 -ly 构成。其拉丁来源是 religare“牢牢绑住”，其分词义带来“绑紧而不松脱”的观念。

items.en: Ligare meant to tie or bind. A thing bound fast stays where it is put, and this physical image later supplies the moral idea of trust.
items.cn: ligare 意为“系、绑”。绑紧的东西会留在原处，这个具体形象后来提供了“信任”这一抽象含义。

items.en: Religare strengthened the image to binding fast or tying back. Roman writers used it for obligations that hold a person to a duty.
items.cn: religare 把形象加强为“绑牢、系回”。罗马作家用它指把人系在义务上的约束。

items.en: Old French relier meant to fasten together or connect, and it carried both the physical and the binding-obligation senses.
items.cn: 古法语 relier 意为“把……系在一起、连接”，兼有物理捆绑与义务约束两层意思。

items.en: English rely first meant to gather or assemble, then to depend on a person or thing, since what is fastened to you is what you lean on.
items.cn: 英语 rely 最初指“聚集、集合”，后指“依靠人或物”，因为系在你身上的东西正是你所倚靠的。

items.en: The Latin suffix -abilis marked what can be done or what deserves to be done; added to rely it yields reliable, worthy of being depended on.
items.cn: 拉丁后缀 -abilis 标记“可以……的、值得……的”；加在 rely 上得到 reliable“值得依靠的”。

items.en: The Old English adverb ending -lice became -ly. It converts the adjective into the manner of doing something, hence reliably, in a dependable manner.
items.cn: 古英语副词词尾 -lice 演变为 -ly，把形容词转成做事的方式，于是 reliably 就是“以可依靠的方式”。

note.en: The first group is the rely family, which shares one root; the second compares adverbs of dependability, accuracy, and consistency.
note.cn: 第一组是 rely 词族，共享同一词根；第二组比较表示可靠、准确、稳定的几个副词。

entries.definition: to depend on someone or something for support or truth. It names the act of leaning on a source.
entries.definitionCN: 依靠某人或某物以获得支持或真相；命名的是倚靠这一动作。

entries.definition: deserving to be depended on. It judges a person, machine, or result, not a manner.
entries.definitionCN: 值得依靠的；评判的是人、机器或结果，而不是做事方式。

entries.definition: the quality of being dependable, often measured by failure rate or repeatability.
entries.definitionCN: 可靠的性质，常用故障率或可重复性来衡量。

entries.definition: the state of depending on something. It stresses dependence, not the quality of the depended-on thing.
entries.definitionCN: 依赖的状态；强调依赖关系，而不是被依赖物的品质。

entries.definition: in a way that can be counted on, with emphasis on personal or contractual trust.
entries.definitionCN: 可以被指望地；强调人身上的信任或契约上的信守。

entries.definition: in the same way on different occasions, with emphasis on uniformity rather than on truth.
entries.definitionCN: 在不同场合以同样的方式；强调一致性，而不是正确性。

entries.definition: without error, with emphasis on closeness to a true value rather than on repeatability.
entries.definitionCN: 没有错误地；强调与真值的接近，而不是可重复性。

entries.definition: at a regular, unbroken rate. It describes rhythm and continuity rather than trustworthiness.
entries.definitionCN: 以规则、不间断的速度；描述节奏与连续性，而非可信程度。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: rely, -able, -ly. Nothing is added that the word does not contain.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：rely、-able、-ly，不额外添加词里没有的东西。

normal.en: Rely plus able plus ly: able to be relied on, and doing things that way.
normal.cn: 依靠加“能够”再加副词尾：能够被依靠，并且以那种方式做事。

normal.en: A rope tied fast does not slide; that picture is the whole of reliability.
normal.cn: 绑紧的绳子不会滑；这幅画面就是“可靠”的全部内容。

normal.en: Three identical readings are what let a scientist say the method works reliably.
normal.cn: 三次读数一样，科学家才敢说这个方法稳定可靠。

normal.en: In an engineering report, reliably means the part never dropped out of service.
normal.cn: 在工程报告里，可靠就意味着这个零件从未掉过链子。

normal.en: Saying reliably informed puts a guarantee on the messenger as well as the message.
normal.cn: 说“据可靠消息”，等于把消息和传话人一起打了包票。

abstract.en: Reliability is not one success but the willingness to be checked again tomorrow.
abstract.cn: 可靠不是一次成功，而是明天仍敢让别人复查。

abstract.en: Handing a task to a machine moves trust from character to calibration.
abstract.cn: 把任务交给机器，就是把信任从人品转移到刻度。

abstract.en: To call something predictable is to squeeze the future into a number that can be recomputed.
abstract.cn: 说某事可预期，就是把未来压缩成一行可以复算的数。

examples.en: The old pump reliably starts on the first try, even in freezing weather.
examples.cn: 这台旧水泵即使在严寒中也能可靠地一次启动。

examples.en: Studies reliably show that spaced review beats a single long cram.
examples.cn: 研究一致表明，间隔复习胜过一次性长时间突击。

examples.en: A witness who is reliably informed may still repeat a rumour, so the source needs checking.
examples.cn: 消息来源可靠的人也可能转述谣言，因此来源仍需核查。

dict_mnemonic.text: 依赖（rely）加“能够”、加副词尾——能够被依赖地做事，就是可靠地。

root: 由 rely（信赖、依靠，源自拉丁语 religare“牢牢绑住”）加 -able（值得……的）与 -ly（副词后缀）构成，本义为“以牢靠可信、可被依靠的方式”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of reliably, all circling one idea: what is done this way will not let you down. The thing that holds may be a result, a machine, a source, a measurement, a forecast, a habit, or a premise.
sensesIntro.cn: reliably 的八个义项都围绕一个观念：以这种方式做出的事不会让你落空。靠得住的对象可以是结果、机器、消息来源、测量、预测、习惯，也可以是推理前提。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of identical weights on a calibration bench, the needle stopping at the same mark every time.
core.cn: 核心意象：校准台上一排相同的砝码，指针每次都停在同一格刻度。

chain: RELIABLE ABLE TO BE DEPENDED ON

branches.en: TRUST IN THE RESULT AND IN THE SOURCE: a trustworthy reading and a trustworthy messenger both remove the need for checking.
branches.cn: 信任结果与信任来源：可信的读数和可信的传话人，都免去了逐项核查。

branches.en: REPEATABILITY AND ACCURACY: the same value time after time, and a value close to the true one.
branches.cn: 可重复与精确：一次次得到同一个值，并且这个值贴近真值。

branches.en: ENDURANCE OF THINGS: a machine that does not fail today and a bridge that does not fail for decades.
branches.cn: 事物的耐久：今天不出故障的机器，与几十年不出问题的桥。

branches.en: RELIABILITY SEEN FROM THE FUTURE: a pattern stable enough to plan around.
branches.cn: 从未来看可靠性：稳定到足以据此做计划的规律。

branches.en: RELIABILITY IN ARGUMENT: a premise that will not betray the conclusion drawn from it.
branches.cn: 论证中的可靠性：不会让由它推出的结论落空的前提。

intro.en: Reliably is built from rely plus the adjective suffix -able and the adverb suffix -ly; the family later adds -ability for the abstract quality and un- for the opposite.
intro.cn: reliably 由 rely 加形容词后缀 -able 与副词后缀 -ly 构成；词族后来又用 -ability 表示抽象性质，用 un- 表示相反。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is ligare, to bind, strengthened in religare. The suffix -abilis belongs to Latin adjective formation, while -ly is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 ligare“绑”，在 religare 中加强。后缀 -abilis 属拉丁形容词构词，而 -ly 是英语本族词尾。

items.example: The Latin verb survives mainly inside compounds such as oblige and religion.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词主要残存在 oblige（使负有义务）、religion（宗教）等复合词里。

items.meaning: to bind fast, to tie back
items.example: Roman law spoke of obligations that religare a person to a promise.
items.exampleCN: 罗马法谈到把人系在承诺上的义务，就用这个动词。

items.meaning: to depend on for support or truth
items.example: Readers rely on the glossary when the text turns technical.
items.exampleCN: 文本变得专业时，读者会依靠术语表。

items.example: The clinic needs a reliable supply of clean water.
items.exampleCN: 诊所需要可靠的洁净水供应。

items.example: Engineers test reliability by running the unit for thousands of hours.
items.exampleCN: 工程师通过让设备运行数千小时来测试可靠性。

items.example: The village's reliance on one well made every drought a crisis.
items.exampleCN: 全村依赖一口井，使每次干旱都成了危机。

items.example: The ferry reliably crosses the strait twice a day.
items.exampleCN: 渡轮每天可靠地穿越海峡两次。

items.meaning: not able to be depended on
items.example: An unreliable narrator makes the reader doubt every fact.
items.exampleCN: 不可靠的叙述者让读者怀疑每一个事实。

items.meaning: able to act without depending on others
items.example: The course aims to make students self-reliant in research.
items.exampleCN: 这门课旨在让学生在研究中能够自立。

definition_en: a dishonest person, a mischievous child spoken of with affection, or an old word for one of the rabble
core_image: 一个孩子嘴角还沾着果酱，却笑着摇头说不是自己
scene: 那孩子偷吃了果酱，被问起时还笑着摇头否认。 The child had eaten the jam and, when asked, shook his head with the smile of a rascal.

senses.title: A dishonest person
senses.definition: a person who lies or cheats to get what he wants
senses.definitionCN: 为得到想要的东西而撒谎或行骗的人
senses.example: The landlord was a rascal who raised the rents twice a year.
senses.exampleCN: 那房东是个无赖，一年涨两次租。
senses.why: This is the plain, cold sense; no affection softens it.
senses.whyCN: 这是最直白、最冷的一层，没有任何亲昵来软化它。

senses.title: A mischievous child
senses.definition: a child whose small tricks are forgiven because they are funny
senses.definitionCN: 因为小把戏好笑而被原谅的孩子

senses.exampleCN: 那孩子偷吃了果酱，还像个小淘气一样摇头否认。
senses.why: Tone decides this sense: the same fault is reported with a smile, and blame turns into fondness.
senses.whyCN: 语气决定了这一层：同样的过错被带笑地说出来，责备就变成了疼爱。

senses.title: (Archaic) a low-born person

senses.example: In old comedy the rascal is usually a quick-tongued servant.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧喜剧里，这种下等人通常是嘴快的仆人。

senses.whyCN: 十四世纪的那层意思解释了这个词的来历：rascaille 最初指一群人，而不是一个人。

branches.en: One word, two tones: blame or affection.
branches.cn: 同一个词，两种语气：责备或疼爱。

branches.en: The archaic crowd word behind the modern insult.
branches.cn: 现代骂名背后那个古老的群体词。

branches.en: From a whole rabble to one smiling face.
branches.cn: 从一整群乌合之众到一张笑脸。

intro.en: The rasc- family is thin but lively: rascal, rascally and rascality all describe small dishonesty with a grin.
intro.cn: rasc 词族不厚却活泼：rascal、rascally、rascality 都描述带笑的小不诚实。

latinIntro.en: Latin rasus, 'scraped bare', gave French rascaille, the rabble; English softened the crowd word into one person.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rasus（刮得精光）给出法语 rascaille（乌合之众）；英语把这个群体词软化成一个人。

items.example: A little rascal.
items.exampleCN: 一个小淘气。

items.example: Two smiling rascals.

items.example: A rascally trick.
items.exampleCN: 一个无赖伎俩。

items.example: A piece of rascality.

items.exampleCN: 一个剃光的头。

items.example: The rascaille of the town.
items.exampleCN: 城里的乌合之众。
