definition_zh: 重新武装；重整军备；重新装备
definition_en: to equip an army or a country with weapons again, especially after disarmament
core_image: 仓库的门重新打开，木箱里取出的枪还裹着油纸
scene: 停战才过五年，边境的工厂又开始连夜造炮。 Within five years of the truce the border factories were rearming.
sceneCN: 这里 rearm 指重整军备（第 1 个义项：重新武装军队）；句意为停战才过五年，边境的工厂又开始连夜造炮。

pos.zh: 重新武装；重整军备；重新装备

senses.title: To arm again
senses.definition: to supply a country or a force with weapons again, especially after disarmament or defeat
senses.definitionCN: 在解除武装或战败之后，再次向国家或部队供应武器
senses.example: The country began to rearm quietly after the defeat.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家在战败之后悄悄开始重整军备。
senses.why: The re- is the whole point: the weapons had been given up, and now they come back.
senses.whyCN: re- 是这个词的全部要害：武器已经交出去了，现在又回来。

senses.title: To equip with new weapons
senses.definition: to replace a force's old equipment with a newer generation of weapons
senses.definitionCN: 用更新一代的武器替换一支部队的旧装备
senses.example: The brigade rearmed with longer-range artillery.
senses.exampleCN: 这个旅换装了射程更远的火炮。
senses.why: Here the emphasis is on upgrading rather than restoring; the force was armed, but not with these.
senses.whyCN: 这一层重在升级而非恢复：部队本来有武器，只是不是这一批。

intro.en: Rearm joins the Latin prefix re-, 'again', to arm, from Latin arma, 'weapons or gear'.
intro.cn: rearm 把拉丁语前缀 re-（再次）加到 arm 上，arm 源自拉丁语 arma（武器、装备）。

items.en: Arma meant weapons and military equipment.
items.cn: arma 指武器与军事装备。

items.en: English arm meant to fit out for war.
items.cn: 英语 arm 意为为战争配备。

items.en: Disarm named the opposite act.
items.cn: disarm 命名相反的动作。

items.en: Rearm became urgent language after the Great War.
items.cn: 一战之后，rearm 成为紧迫的用语。

items.en: Today it also describes rebuilding any capacity.
items.cn: 今天它也描述重建任何能力。

note.en: The look-alike group is the arm- family; the near-meaning group separates remilitarize, mobilize, equip and refit.
note.cn: 形近组是 arm 词族；近义组把「重新军事化」「动员」「装备」「改装」分开。

entries.definition: to supply with weapons.
entries.definitionCN: 提供武器。

entries.definition: carrying weapons.
entries.definitionCN: 携带武器的。

entries.definition: to take weapons away.
entries.definitionCN: 解除武装。

entries.definition: the process of rearming.
entries.definitionCN: 重整军备的过程。

entries.definition: to restore military control.
entries.definitionCN: 恢复军事控制。

entries.definition: to prepare forces for action.
entries.definitionCN: 使部队准备行动。

entries.definition: to supply with needed items.
entries.definitionCN: 提供所需装备。

entries.definition: to repair and re-equip.
entries.definitionCN: 修理并重新装备。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a storehouse opened again and rifles still greased in paper.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「仓库再次打开，步枪还裹着油纸」的画面。

normal.en: Rearm is re plus arm: the weapons come back.
normal.cn: rearm 是 re 加 arm：武器回来了。

normal.en: Picture a crate opened after years, the oil paper still on the metal.
normal.cn: 想象多年之后打开一只木箱，金属上的油纸还在。

normal.en: Say ree-ARM; the stress falls on the short second syllable.
normal.cn: 读 ree-ARM，重音落在短的第二音节。

normal.en: The word always implies an earlier disarm.
normal.cn: 这个词总暗含一次更早的解除武装。

normal.en: Ask who pays for the rearming, and who is told it is temporary.
normal.cn: 问谁为重整军备付账，谁又被告诉这只是暂时的。

abstract.en: To rearm is to treat peace as an interval rather than an end.
abstract.cn: 重整军备是把和平当作间歇，而不是终点。

abstract.en: Weapons restored are not the same weapons: the second arming changes the first.
abstract.cn: 恢复的武器已不是原来的武器：第二次武装改变了第一次。

abstract.en: The word is neutral in grammar and accusing in history.
abstract.cn: 这个词在语法上中性，在历史里却带着指控。

examples.en: The country began to rearm quietly after the defeat.
examples.cn: 这个国家在战败之后悄悄开始重整军备。

examples.en: The brigade rearmed with longer-range artillery.
examples.cn: 这个旅换装了射程更远的火炮。

examples.en: Rearming absorbed the budget that had been promised to schools.
examples.cn: 重整军备吞掉了原本承诺给学校的预算。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（再次）+ arm（武装）→ 再把武器发下去。

root: 拉丁语 arma（武器）+ re-（再次）

sensesIntro.en: Rearm has two senses: bringing weapons back after they were given up, and fitting a force out with newer ones.
sensesIntro.cn: rearm 有两层：交出武器之后把它拿回来，以及给部队换上更新的一代。

core.en: A CRATE OPENED AGAIN
core.cn: 再次被打开的军械箱

branches.en: A treaty, then factories restarting.
branches.cn: 一份条约，然后工厂重新开工。

branches.en: Old guns replaced by longer-range ones.
branches.cn: 旧炮换成射程更远的炮。

branches.en: Peace treated as an interval.
branches.cn: 被当作间歇的和平。

branches.en: An upgrade rather than a restoration.
branches.cn: 升级而不是恢复。

branches.en: Arming again, and arming better.
branches.cn: 重新武装，以及武装得更好。

intro.en: The arm- family runs both ways: arm and rearm add weapons, disarm removes them, and armament names the whole apparatus.
intro.cn: arm 词族可以两头走：arm 与 rearm 增加武器，disarm 拿走武器，armament 命名整套装置。

latinIntro.en: Latin arma gives arm, armament and disarm through French forms; re- is the Latin prefix of repetition.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 arma 经法语形式给出 arm、armament、disarm；re- 是表示重复的拉丁语前缀。

items.example: Rearm the guard.
items.exampleCN: 重新武装卫队。

items.example: They rearmed at once.
items.exampleCN: 他们立刻重新武装。

items.example: A rearming state.
items.exampleCN: 一个正在重整军备的国家。

items.example: Costly rearmament.
items.exampleCN: 代价高昂的重整军备。

items.example: Arm the troops.
items.exampleCN: 武装部队。

items.example: An armed patrol.
items.exampleCN: 一支武装巡逻队。

items.example: Disarm the militia.
items.exampleCN: 解除民兵武装。

items.example: Heavy armament.
items.exampleCN: 重型军备。

definition_zh: 分子；分数线上方的数；除法中的被除数；比率中的前项
definition_en: the number above the line in a fraction, or the quantity that is divided by another
core_image: 一张纸上写着分数，横线上方的数字被红笔描了一道
scene: 纸上写着一个分数，横线上方的数字被红笔描了一道。 In the fraction, the numerator tells how many parts are counted.
sceneCN: 这里 numerator 指「分数中写在横线上方的数，表示取了多少份」（第 1 个义项：分数的分子）；句意为在这个分数里，分子说明数了几份。图中可辨识物件：纸、分数横线、红笔、上下两个数字。

pos.zh: 分子；被除数；比的前项

derivatives.zh: 数字；数字的（同出拉丁 numerus）
数字的；数值的（同出拉丁 numerus）
计算；识数的（同出拉丁 numerare）
列举；清点（同出拉丁 enumerare）

senses.title: The number above the fraction bar
senses.definition: the number in a fraction that shows how many equal parts are taken
senses.definitionCN: 分数中说明取了多少个等份的那个数
senses.example: In the fraction, the numerator tells how many parts are counted.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个分数里，分子说明数了几份。
senses.why: numerator is Latin for 'counter': the top number counts the parts that the fraction is talking about.
senses.whyCN: numerator 在拉丁语里是「数数者」：上面那个数负责清点这个分数所说的份数。

senses.title: The dividend in a division
senses.definition: the quantity that is divided by another quantity
senses.definitionCN: 被另一个量所除的那个量
senses.example: In the written division, the numerator sits inside the bracket.
senses.exampleCN: 在竖式除法里，被除数写在除号里面。
senses.why: a fraction is a division written down, so the top number plays exactly the role of the dividend.
senses.whyCN: 分数就是写下来的除法，因此上面那个数扮演的正是被除数的角色。

senses.title: The first term of a ratio
senses.definition: the first quantity named when two amounts are compared as a ratio
senses.definitionCN: 两个量作比时先说出的那个量
senses.example: In the ratio, the numerator is the part being compared to the whole.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个比里，前项是被拿去与整体比较的那一部分。
senses.why: a ratio is a fraction in words, so the first term takes the place of the top number.
senses.whyCN: 比就是用文字说出的分数，因此前项占据的就是上面那个数的位置。

senses.title: The count in a rate
senses.titleCN: 比率中实际计数的部分
senses.definition: the number of events counted in the top part of a rate or proportion
senses.definitionCN: 比率或比例中，上半部分实际数出的事件数
senses.example: The numerator of the infection rate is the number of new cases.
senses.exampleCN: 感染率的分子是新病例的数目。
senses.why: in public health a rate is written as events over population, and the events are literally the counted numerator.
senses.whyCN: 在公共卫生里，率写成「事件数除以人口数」，事件数就是被数出来的分子。

senses.title: The numerator polynomial
senses.titleCN: 代数分式的分子多项式
senses.definition: the polynomial written above the line in an algebraic fraction
senses.definitionCN: 代数分式中写在横线上方的那个多项式
senses.example: Factor the numerator polynomial before simplifying the expression.
senses.exampleCN: 化简表达式之前，先把分子多项式因式分解。
senses.why: algebraic fractions copy ordinary fractions exactly, so the top polynomial keeps the name of the top number.
senses.whyCN: 代数分式完全照搬普通分数，因此上面那个多项式沿用上面那个数的名字。

senses.title: A common numerator
senses.definition: a numerator shared by two or more fractions after they are adjusted for comparison
senses.definitionCN: 两个或更多分数在调整以便比较后所共有的分子
senses.example: Rewriting both fractions with a common numerator made the larger one obvious.
senses.exampleCN: 把两个分数都改写成相同的分子后，较大的那个就一目了然了。
senses.why: just as fractions can share a denominator, they can be rewritten to share a numerator, and the counting role gives the name.
senses.whyCN: 正如分数可以有公分母，它们也能改写成共同的分子，命名依据仍是「数份」这个角色。

senses.title: The numerator of a percentage
senses.definition: the amount placed over one hundred when a proportion is written as a percentage
senses.definitionCN: 把比例写成百分数时，放在一百上面的那个量
senses.example: In the percentage, the numerator is the share and the denominator is one hundred.
senses.exampleCN: 在百分数里，分子是所占的份额，分母是一百。
senses.why: a percentage is a fraction with one hundred underneath, so the share above the line is still the numerator.
senses.whyCN: 百分数就是分母为一百的分数，因此横线上方的份额仍然是分子。

senses.title: An older word for a counter
senses.definition: an older use for a person who numbers or counts things
senses.definitionCN: 较旧的用法，指给事物编号或清点事物的人
senses.example: The old ledger lists the numerator who checked each crate.
senses.exampleCN: 旧账本上记着负责清点每个木箱的人。
senses.why: the Latin agent noun meant 'one who counts', and the mathematical use grew out of that literal counting person.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁施动名词本意是「数数的人」，数学用法正是从那个字面意义上的清点者长出来的。

intro.en: Numerator is Latin numerator 'a counter', from numerare 'to count', from numerus 'number'. The mathematical use came through French numérateur in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: numerator 是拉丁 numerator「数数者」，出自 numerare「计数」，再上溯到 numerus「数」。数学用法在十六世纪经法语 numérateur 而来。

items.en: Numerus meant 'number'. It is the source of numeral, numerical, enumerate and numerous in English.
items.cn: numerus 意为「数」。它是英语 numeral、numerical、enumerate 与 numerous 的来源。

items.en: Numerare meant 'to count, to number', a verb built directly on the noun.
items.cn: numerare 意为「计数、编号」，是直接由这个名词构成的动词。

items.en: The agent noun numerator named one who counts, a teller or reckoner; the ending -tor marks the person who does the action.
items.cn: 施动名词 numerator 指数数的人，即点算员；词尾 -tor 标记执行动作的人。

items.en: French formed the mathematical term numérateur for the top number of a fraction, since that number counts the parts taken.
items.cn: 法语构成数学术语 numérateur，指分数上方那个数，因为那个数负责清点取走的份数。

items.en: English adopted numerator in the sixteenth century together with the printed notation of fractions.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪随印刷的分数写法一起接受了 numerator。

items.en: The first English citation for the mathematical sense is approximate; numerus and numerare are securely attested Latin words.
items.cn: 数学义在英语中的最早书证为约数；numerus 与 numerare 则是有可靠记录的拉丁词。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin word for number and is easily mixed up; the second group names the other parts of a division or ratio.
note.cn: 第一组共享那个表示「数」的拉丁词，容易混淆；第二组是除法或比里的其他部分。

entries.definition: A written sign for a number; it names the mark, not the top part of a fraction.
entries.definitionCN: 指表示数的书写符号；命名的是记号，不是分数的上半部分。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning expressed in numbers; it describes data, not a fraction position.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「用数字表示的」，描述数据，不指分数的位置。

entries.definition: Adjective meaning able to handle numbers, or a verb meaning to count; neither is the fraction term.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词意为「会算数的」，动词意为「计数」；两者都不是分数术语。

entries.definition: To list one by one, from enumerare 'to count out'; it is a verb of listing, not a part of a fraction.
entries.definitionCN: 指逐项列出，出自 enumerare「数出来」；是列举的动词，不是分数的部分。

entries.definition: The bottom number, built on nomen 'name'; it names the size of the parts while the numerator counts them.
entries.definitionCN: 下面那个数，建立在 nomen「名字」上；它命名每份的大小，而分子负责数份数。

entries.definition: The quantity being divided; in a fraction it is the number above the bar.
entries.definitionCN: 指被除的量；在分数里就是横线上方的数。

entries.definition: The first term of a ratio, matching the numerator's position in a fraction.
entries.definitionCN: 指比的前项，对应分子在分数里的位置。

entries.definition: The number reached by counting; a numerator is that count written above a fraction bar.
entries.definitionCN: 指清点得到的数目；分子就是写成分数横线上方的那个清点结果。

entries.definition: The everyday phrase for the numerator used in early teaching.
entries.definitionCN: 早期教学里对分子的日常说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin verb, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁动词、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: numerus 'number' plus -ator 'one who': the counter, the number that counts the parts.
normal.cn: numerus「数」加 -ator「做……的人」：数数者，负责清点份数的那个数。

normal.en: The family runs numerator, numeral, numerical, numerate and enumerate, all from numerus.
normal.cn: 同族词有 numerator、numeral、numerical、numerate 与 enumerate，都出自 numerus。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: numerator and denominator, common numerator, numerator polynomial.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：分子与分母、公分子、分子多项式。

normal.en: The numerator sits on top and counts; the denominator sits below and names.
normal.cn: 分子在上面负责数，分母在下面负责命名。

normal.en: A percentage is just a fraction with one hundred below, so its top is still a numerator.
normal.cn: 百分数就是分母为一百的分数，所以它的上方仍然是分子。

abstract.en: Picture a hand picking up three slices from a loaf cut into eight.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从切成八片的面包里拿起三片。

abstract.en: Picture a tally keeper standing at the door, marking every person who enters.
abstract.cn: 想象一个记数人站在门口，给每个进来的人画一道。

abstract.en: Picture the number on top of a fraction as a small flag marking how much is claimed.
abstract.cn: 想象分数上面的数是面小旗，标出「要了多少」。

examples.en: When the numerator and denominator share a factor, both can be divided by it.
examples.cn: 分子与分母有公因子时，两边都能被它除。

examples.en: The numerator of the rate counts only confirmed cases.
examples.cn: 这个比率的分子只统计确诊病例。

examples.en: Write the numerator above the bar and the denominator below it.
examples.cn: 把分子写在横线上方，分母写在下方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「数在上」——负责点数的那一行写在上头 → 分子

root: 拉丁 numerus「数」→ numerare「计数」→ numerator「数数者」→ 法语 numérateur（分数上方的数）→ 英语 numerator。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all keep one role: the number that counts what is being taken. It counts slices of a fraction, items in a dividend, the first term of a ratio, cases in a rate, terms of a polynomial and parts of a percentage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个角色：负责清点「取走多少」的那个数。它数分数的份数、被除数里的个数、比的前项、比率中的病例、多项式的项，以及百分数里的份额。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the number written above the fraction bar, marked with red ink.
core.cn: 核心意象：写在分数横线上方的数，被红笔描过。

branches.en: THE COUNTING POSITION: the top number of a fraction, and the shared top number used for comparison.
branches.cn: 计数的位置：分数的上方数，以及用于比较的公分子。

branches.en: THE SAME ROLE ELSEWHERE: the dividend of a division and the first term of a ratio.
branches.cn: 同一角色在别处：除法的被除数与比的前项。

branches.en: COUNTING WHAT HAPPENED: cases in a rate and the share written over one hundred.
branches.cn: 清点发生的事：比率中的病例，以及写在一百上面的份额。

branches.en: POLYNOMIAL ON TOP: algebraic fractions keep the top polynomial in the same seat.
branches.cn: 上面的多项式：代数分式让上方多项式坐同一个位置。

branches.en: THE PERSON WHO COUNTS: the oldest sense, the reckoner with a tally.
branches.cn: 数数的人：最古老的义项，拿筹码清点的人。

intro.en: Numerator is a Latin agent noun on a counting verb; its root and suffix both build a large English family.
intro.cn: numerator 是建立在一个计数动词上的拉丁施动名词；其词根与后缀都构成一个很大的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin numerus gives numeral, numerical, numerous and enumerate; the agent suffix -tor gives numerator, denominator and operator.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 numerus 衍生 numeral、numerical、numerous 与 enumerate；施动后缀 -tor 衍生 numerator、denominator 与 operator。

items.example: The root names the number being counted.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名被数的数。

items.example: The verb supplies the act of counting.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供计数的动作。

items.example: The Latin noun names the person, then the top number.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词先指人，后指上面那个数。

items.example: Roman numerals use letters.
items.exampleCN: 罗马数字用字母。

items.example: The data are numerical.
items.exampleCN: 这些数据是数值性的。

items.meaning: to count; able to use numbers
items.example: She is numerate and quick.
items.exampleCN: 她懂数且反应快。

items.meaning: to count out one by one
items.example: The report enumerates every cost.
items.exampleCN: 报告逐项列出每笔成本。

items.meaning: the naming number below the bar
items.meaningCN: 横线下方负责命名的数
items.example: The denominator names the part size.
items.exampleCN: 分母命名每份的大小。

items.example: It also appears in operator and denominator.
items.exampleCN: 它也出现在 operator 与 denominator 里。

derivatives.zh: 数字；数字的（同出拉丁 numerus）
数字的；数值的（同出拉丁 numerus）
计算；识数的（同出拉丁 numerare）
列举；清点（同出拉丁 enumerare）

definition_zh: 纸莎草（生长在尼罗河沼泽的高大莎草）；用其茎芯压成的书写材料；写在纸草上的古代文献
definition_en: a tall sedge of Nile marshes; the writing material made from its pith; an ancient document written on it
core_image: 尼罗河边的浅水里立着一丛三角茎的高草，茎心被剖成薄片压平晾干
scene: 修复师把一片纤维交错的古老纸草铺在玻璃板上。 The account of the harvest survives on a roll of papyrus.
sceneCN: 这里 papyrus 指「用纸莎草茎芯制成的书写材料」（第 2 个义项：纸草书写材料）；句意为一份收获账目留存在一卷纸草上。

pos.zh: 纸莎草；纸草书写材料；纸草文献

derivatives.zh: papyrus 的拉丁式复数（-us → -i）→ 多卷纸草文献
papyrus + -aceous（性质后缀）→ 纸草质的；薄如纸的
papyrology + -ist（从业者后缀）→ 纸草学者
papyrus + -form（形状后缀）→ 纸草形的

senses.title: The reed plant
senses.definition: a tall sedge with triangular stems that grows in shallow water, especially along the Nile
senses.definitionCN: 一种茎呈三角形的髙大莎草，生长在浅水中，尤见于尼罗河沿岸
senses.example: Papyrus once grew thick along the riverbanks.
senses.exampleCN: 纸莎草曾在河岸一带长得十分茂密。
senses.why: the plant name is the oldest sense; the material and the documents are named after the plant.
senses.whyCN: 植物名是最早的义项；材料与文献都因这种植物得名。

senses.title: Writing material from the pith
senses.titleCN: 用茎芯制成的书写材料
senses.definition: sheets made by slicing the pith into strips, pressing them crosswise and drying them
senses.definitionCN: 把茎芯切成薄条、交叉压紧并晾干制成的纸页
senses.example: Scribes wrote on papyrus with a cut reed pen.
senses.exampleCN: 书吏用削好的芦苇笔在纸草上书写。
senses.why: the plant's pith was the industrial raw material, so the material simply took the plant's name.
senses.whyCN: 这种植物的茎芯就是工业原料，材料便直接沿用了植物名。

senses.title: A document written on papyrus
senses.definition: a scroll or sheet of papyrus bearing writing, especially an ancient record
senses.definitionCN: 写有文字的纸草卷或纸页，尤指古代记录
senses.example: The tax record is a papyrus from the temple archive.
senses.exampleCN: 这份税务记录是神庙档案中的一件纸草文献。
senses.why: material names routinely stand for the objects made from them, a metonymy seen with paper and parchment.
senses.whyCN: 材料名常转指其制成品，paper 与 parchment 都有这种转喻。

senses.title: Ancient texts studied as a group
senses.titleCN: 作为一组研究对象的古代纸草文献
senses.definition: ancient texts preserved on papyrus, especially those recovered from Egypt and studied by scholars
senses.definitionCN: 保存在纸草上的古代文本，尤指从埃及出土、由学者研究的那批
senses.example: The papyri include private letters, contracts and school exercises.
senses.exampleCN: 这批纸草文献包括私人信件、契约与学校练习。
senses.why: the Latin plural papyri marks the scholarly collection sense, where individual sheets become an archive.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁式复数 papyri 标出学术集合义，单张纸页在此变成一批档案。

senses.title: The ancient writing medium
senses.definition: the dominant writing surface of Egypt and the Mediterranean before parchment
senses.definitionCN: 在羊皮纸之前，埃及与地中海世界占主导的书写表面
senses.example: Papyrus gave way to parchment in late antiquity.
senses.exampleCN: 在古代晚期，纸草逐渐让位于羊皮纸。
senses.why: the material names a whole period of writing because it shaped how records were kept.
senses.whyCN: 这种材料塑造了记录方式，因此可以命名整个书写时代。

senses.title: The sedge family member
senses.definition: a member of the sedge family, related to reed grasses rather than to trees
senses.definitionCN: 莎草科的一员，与芦苇类草本相近，而非树木
senses.example: Botanists classify papyrus as a sedge, not a reed grass.
senses.exampleCN: 植物学家把纸莎草归入莎草，而不是芦苇。
senses.why: the plant sense narrows in botany to a family classification, a technical specialization of sense one.
senses.whyCN: 植物义在植物学中收窄为科属分类，是第一义的技术性细分。

senses.title: An emblem of fragile antiquity
senses.definition: a symbol used by museums and libraries for ancient and easily damaged records
senses.definitionCN: 博物馆与图书馆用来象征古老且易损记录的符号
senses.example: The library uses a papyrus as the emblem on its rare-book room.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆用纸草图案作为善本室的标志。
senses.why: a material that survives only in dry conditions becomes a natural emblem for fragile memory.
senses.whyCN: 只在干燥环境里幸存的材料，自然成为脆弱记忆的象征。

senses.title: A decorative plant motif
senses.definition: a stylized image of the papyrus plant used in painting, carving and architecture
senses.definitionCN: 绘画、雕刻与建筑中程式化的纸莎草形象
senses.example: The column capital is carved with papyrus and lotus buds.
senses.exampleCN: 柱头雕刻着纸草与莲花花蕾。
senses.why: Egyptian art used the plant as ornament, and the motif kept the name after the plant's everyday use faded.
senses.whyCN: 埃及艺术用这种植物作装饰，日常用途消失后纹样仍保留其名。

intro.en: Papyrus is Latin for the Nile reed and its writing sheet, borrowed from Greek papyros. The deeper origin of papyros is not established; suggestions linking it to Egyptian are plausible but unproven.
intro.cn: papyrus 是拉丁语，指尼罗河芦苇及其书写纸，借自希腊 papyros。papyros 更深来源未确立；把它与埃及语联系起来的说法看似合理，但未获证明。

items.en: Papyros named the reed and, by extension, the sheet made from it.
items.cn: papyros 指这种芦苇，也引申指用它制成的纸页。

items.en: Latin kept the Greek noun and passed it to the learned languages of Europe.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留这个希腊名词，并把它传给欧洲的学术语言。

items.en: English used papyrus first for the plant and the material, then for documents made from it.
items.cn: 英语先用 papyrus 指植物与材料，再指用其制成的文献。

items.en: The Latin plural papyri became the standard term for collections of ancient papyrus texts.
items.cn: 拉丁复数 papyri 成为古代纸草文献收藏的标准称呼。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the link between papyros and an Egyptian word is often suggested but not demonstrated, so any Egyptian form offered for it is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：papyros 与某个埃及语词的联系常被提出，却未获证实，因此为其给出的埃及语形式都只是假说。

note.en: Group one holds the plant, material and documents that share the same name; group two holds other ancient writing surfaces.
note.cn: 第一组是同名而分属植物、材料与文献的词；第二组是其他古代书写表面。

entries.definition: The Latin plural used for collections of ancient papyrus texts; the singular names one plant or sheet.
entries.definitionCN: 用于古代纸草文献收藏的拉丁复数；单数指一株植物或一张纸。

entries.definition: The study of texts written on papyrus; it names the field, not the material.
entries.definitionCN: 研究纸草文本的学科；它指领域，而非材料。

entries.definition: Prepared animal skin that replaced papyrus in many places; it is a different material.
entries.definitionCN: 在许多地方取代纸草的加工兽皮；是另一种材料。

entries.definition: Plant-fibre sheets made by industry; papyrus was an early pressed-pith sheet, not paper in the modern sense.
entries.definitionCN: 工业制造的植物纤维纸；纸草是早期压制的茎芯薄片，并非现代意义的纸。

entries.definition: A tall hollow grass of wet ground; papyrus is one specific sedge, not the general reed.
entries.definitionCN: 湿地上的髙大空心草；纸莎草是特定的一种莎草，而非泛指芦苇。

entries.definition: A document rolled for storage; it may be papyrus, parchment or paper.
entries.definitionCN: 卷起保存的文件；材料可为纸草、羊皮纸或纸。

entries.definition: A grass-like plant of wet ground with triangular stems; papyrus is a member of this family.
entries.definitionCN: 湿地中茎呈三角形的类草植物；纸莎草是该科成员。

entries.definition: A text written by hand; a papyrus may be a manuscript, but the words answer different questions.
entries.definitionCN: 手写的文本；纸草文献可能是手稿，但两词回答的问题不同。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Nile plant, the pressed pith and the real scholarly plural.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：尼罗河植物、压制的茎芯与真实的学术复数。

normal.en: Papyrus is a sedge, not a tree; its stem is triangular.
normal.cn: 纸莎草是莎草，不是树；它的茎呈三角形。

normal.en: The pith was cut into strips and pressed crosswise to make a sheet.
normal.cn: 茎芯被切成条，交叉压紧制成纸页。

normal.en: The Latin plural papyri is standard in scholarship.
normal.cn: 拉丁复数 papyri 在学术界是标准形式。

normal.en: Papyrus, parchment and paper name three different writing surfaces.
normal.cn: 纸草、羊皮纸与纸是三种不同的书写表面。

normal.en: Papyrology is the field that reads texts surviving on papyrus.
normal.cn: 纸草学是解读纸草文本的学科。

abstract.en: Papyrus is a river plant that became a library.
abstract.cn: 纸莎草是一种变成图书馆的河畔植物。

abstract.en: It is a sheet that lasts only where rain never falls.
abstract.cn: 它是一张只在无雨之处才能存活的纸。

abstract.en: A papyrus scroll is a conversation held across two thousand years.
abstract.cn: 纸草卷轴是一场跨越两千年的对话。

examples.en: The hieroglyphic text was written on a sheet of papyrus.
examples.cn: 那段象形文字写在一张纸草上。

examples.en: Papyrus grows wild in the marshes of the Nile delta.
examples.cn: 纸莎草在尼罗河三角洲的沼泽中野生生长。

examples.en: The papyri were stored in dry jars to protect them.
examples.cn: 这些纸草文献被存放在干燥的罐子里加以保护。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「papyrus（纸草）」——尼罗河边的三角茎莎草，剖开压平就成了书写的纸

root: 拉丁 papyrus ← 希腊 papyros，指尼罗河芦苇及其书写纸；papyros 更深来源不确定，与埃及语的联系仅为假说。英语 papyrus。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from one plant: the reed, its pith sheet, a written document, a scholarly collection, a whole era of writing, a botanical member, an emblem and an ornament.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一株植物展开：芦苇、茎芯纸、写成的文献、学术收藏、整个书写时代、植物分类、象征与纹样。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a triangular reed cut into strips, pressed flat and turned into a page that outlasts its writer.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根三角茎芦苇被切成条、压平，变成比书写者活得更久的一页。

branches.en: PLANT AND FAMILY: the Nile reed and the sedge classification are the living plant seen alone and in botany.
branches.cn: 植物与科属：尼罗河芦苇与莎草分类，是活植物在单独与植物学两个层面的样子。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND ERA: the pressed sheet and the age it dominated are one medium seen as object and as period.
branches.cn: 材料与时代：压制纸页与它主导的时代，是同一媒介的物件面与时期面。

branches.en: DOCUMENT AND COLLECTION: one written scroll grows into an archive of ancient texts.
branches.cn: 文献与收藏：一卷写成的纸草扩展成一批古代文本档案。

branches.en: FRAGILE EMBLEM: the material becomes a sign for records that easily crumble.
branches.cn: 脆弱象征：材料成为易碎记录的符号。

branches.en: ORNAMENT: the plant survives as a carved motif after its practical use ends.
branches.cn: 装饰：实用用途结束后，这种植物以雕刻纹样继续存在。

intro.en: Papyrus is a Greek plant name carried into English through Latin, and its family covers the material, the documents and the scholars who read them.
intro.cn: papyrus 是经拉丁语进入英语的希腊植物名，其词族覆盖材料、文献与解读它们的学者。

latinIntro.en: Latin papyrus kept the Greek noun unchanged; the Latin plural papyri became the scholarly standard.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 papyrus 原样保留希腊名词；拉丁复数 papyri 成为学术标准。

items.example: Greek named the plant before the sheet.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语先命名植物，后指纸页。

items.example: Latin carried the word to Europe.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这个词带到欧洲。

items.example: The ending marks the Latin form.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标出拉丁形式。

items.example: Papyri keeps the Latin plural.
items.exampleCN: papyri 保留拉丁复数。

items.example: Papyraceous describes a papery texture.
items.exampleCN: papyraceous 描述纸质质感。

items.example: Papyrology recovers lost literature.
items.exampleCN: 纸草学找回失落的文学。

items.example: The papyrologist repaired the scroll.
items.exampleCN: 这位纸草学者修复了卷轴。

items.example: The capital uses a papyriform design.
items.exampleCN: 柱头采用纸草形设计。

definition_zh: 断裂的；骨折的；分裂的；支离破碎的；受损的
definition_en: broken or cracked, or divided into parts that no longer hold together
core_image: 一张完整的合影被撕成几片，边缘参差，人物再也对不上
scene: 急诊室里，医生把片子举到灯下，指着腕骨上的一道细线。 The X-ray shows a fractured wrist that needs a cast.
sceneCN: 这里 fractured 是形容词「骨折的、断裂的」（第 1 个义项：骨头或硬物出现裂口）；句意为 X 光片显示腕部骨折，需要打石膏。

pos.zh: 断裂的；骨折的；分裂的；支离破碎的
（fracture 的过去式/过去分词）使断裂；使骨折

senses.title: Cracked or broken physically
senses.definition: having a crack or break, especially in bone, rock or a hard manufactured part
senses.definitionCN: 出现裂缝或断口，尤指骨头、岩石或坚硬制件
senses.example: The X-ray shows a fractured wrist that needs a cast.
senses.exampleCN: X 光片显示腕部骨折，需要打石膏。
senses.why: fractured is simply the past participle of fracture used as an adjective, so it names the state left after the breaking event.
senses.whyCN: fractured 就是 fracture 的过去分词作形容词，因此它命名的是断裂事件之后留下的状态。

senses.title: Split into opposing groups
senses.definition: divided into factions or camps that no longer act as one
senses.definitionCN: 分成若干不再作为一个整体行动的派别或阵营
senses.example: A fractured parliament passed nothing for six months.
senses.exampleCN: 一个分裂的议会六个月里什么也没通过。
senses.why: the participle keeps the image of a solid in pieces and applies it to a body that should act as one.
senses.whyCN: 这个分词保留了固体碎成数块的意象，并把它用于本应作为一个整体行动的机构。

senses.title: Disjointed in structure
senses.definition: lacking smooth continuity, so that the parts do not connect logically
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏顺畅的连续性，各部分在逻辑上接不上
senses.example: The novel's fractured timeline jumps between three decades.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说破碎的时间线在三十年间来回跳跃。
senses.why: a narrative that does not hold together has the same defect as a cracked slab: the parts no longer meet.
senses.whyCN: 接不上的叙事与裂开的石板有同样的缺陷：各部分不再咬合。

senses.title: Structurally damaged by cracks
senses.definition: weakened by cracks that run through a building, road or foundation
senses.definitionCN: 因贯穿建筑、道路或地基的裂缝而变弱
senses.example: Engineers closed the fractured bridge before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在黎明前封闭了这座出现断裂的桥。
senses.why: in engineering the adjective describes a structure whose load paths are cut by cracks, not merely a surface that looks bad.
senses.whyCN: 在工程语境里，这个形容词描述的是承力路径被裂缝切断的结构，而不只是外观难看。

senses.title: Divided into separate pieces of a market or land
senses.definition: broken into small separate units that do not form a single system
senses.definitionCN: 被分成互不构成单一系统的小单元
senses.example: Regulation left a fractured market of local monopolies.
senses.exampleCN: 监管留下一个由地方垄断拼成的割裂市场。
senses.why: the sense extends the physical split to systems whose parts are prevented from joining.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项把物理分裂扩展到那些各部分无法接合的系统。

senses.title: Strained or damaged in trust
senses.titleCN: 信任受损的、关系破裂的
senses.definition: damaged in trust or goodwill, so that cooperation is difficult
senses.definitionCN: 信任或善意受损，以致合作变得困难
senses.example: Years of silence left a fractured relationship between the cousins.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的沉默让这对表亲的关系出现裂痕。
senses.why: trust is treated as something with a surface, and a surface can be cracked without being destroyed.
senses.whyCN: 信任被当作有表面的东西，而表面可以裂开却尚未彻底毁掉。

senses.title: Broken and halting in speech
senses.definition: spoken in broken, interrupted phrases rather than complete fluent sentences
senses.definitionCN: 以破碎、被打断的短语说出，而非完整流畅的句子
senses.example: The witness gave a fractured account of the night.
senses.exampleCN: 目击者对那晚作了断断续续的叙述。
senses.why: speech that keeps stopping has the continuity of its phrases broken, which is the abstract version of a crack.
senses.whyCN: 不断停顿的言语，其短语的连续性被打断，这就是裂缝的抽象版本。

senses.title: Broken by many joints in rock
senses.titleCN: 岩体被多组节理破碎的
senses.definition: describing rock or an aquifer cut by many joints and small faults
senses.definitionCN: 描述被许多节理与小断层切割的岩体或含水层
senses.example: Water moves quickly through the fractured limestone.
senses.exampleCN: 水在破碎的石灰岩中流动得很快。
senses.why: geology uses the participle for rock whose network of breaks controls how fluids travel.
senses.whyCN: 地质学用这个分词描述岩体，其裂隙网络控制流体的运移。

intro.en: Fractured is the past participle of fracture, which comes from Latin fractura, a breaking, from frangere, to break. As an adjective it is a modern English formation, not a separate Latin word.
intro.cn: fractured 是 fracture 的过去分词；fracture 来自拉丁 fractura「断裂」，源自动词 frangere「打破」。作形容词是英语自身的构词，并非另一个拉丁词。

items.en: Frangere meant to break or shatter, with the participle fractus, broken, supplying the stem behind the whole English family.
items.cn: frangere 意为「打破、击碎」，分词 fractus「被打破的」提供了整个英语词族背后的词干。

items.en: Fractura named a breaking or the breach it produced; English borrowed it in the fifteenth century as the medical term for a broken bone.
items.cn: fractura 指一次断裂或它造成的破口；英语在 15 世纪借入，作为骨折的医学术语。

items.en: English added -ed to fracture to form the past participle, which then took on adjective work: a fractured bone, a fractured party.
items.cn: 英语给 fracture 加 -ed 构成过去分词，随后它承担形容词功能：骨折的骨头、分裂的政党。

items.en: In the twentieth century the adjective spread to narratives, markets and relationships, where the shared idea is lost continuity.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪，这个形容词扩展到叙事、市场与关系，共同的要点都是失去连续性。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the pre-Latin root of frangere is reconstructed rather than attested, and the exact first date of the adjective use is not recorded.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：frangere 的拉丁语之前词根属于重构而非有据形式，形容词用法的确切首见年代亦无记录。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the same breaking stem; group two holds adjectives of damage and division that are close in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「打破」词干的词形；第二组是意义相近、表示损坏与分裂的形容词。

entries.definition: The base form: a break, or the act of breaking; fractured is its participial adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 基础形式：断裂，或使断裂的动作；fractured 是它的分词形容词。

entries.definition: From fragment, same Latin stock: broken into many separate pieces, often used for data or habitats.
entries.definitionCN: 来自同出拉丁词干的 fragment：碎成许多独立小块，常用于数据或栖息地。

entries.definition: From fraction: relating to a small numerical part, with no sense of physical cracking.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 fraction：与数值上的小部分有关，不含物理裂开的意思。

entries.definition: From refract, re- plus frangere: bent at an angle, used of light or waves rather than solids.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 refract，即 re- 加 frangere：以一定角度弯折，用于光或波而非固体。

entries.definition: The common adjective for something in pieces; it is broader and less technical than fractured.
entries.definitionCN: 表示物件碎了的日常形容词；比 fractured 更宽泛、更不技术化。

entries.definition: Having a thin line of breakage, often on a surface; the parts may still be in place.
entries.definitionCN: 表面出现细裂线；各部分可能仍在原位。

entries.definition: Separated into two or more parts, often along a clean line, as a split log or a split vote.
entries.definitionCN: 分成两块或多块，常沿一条整齐的线，如劈开的木头或分裂的票数。

entries.definition: Lacking coherent connections between parts, used of speech, writing or policy; it does not imply physical damage.
entries.definitionCN: 各部分缺乏连贯衔接，用于言语、写作或政策；不含物理损坏之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: fracture + -ed: the -ed turns the event into a state.
normal.cn: fracture + -ed：这个 -ed 把事件变成状态。

normal.en: X-ray language fixes it: a fractured wrist, a fractured rib, a fractured femur.
normal.cn: X 光语境固定了它：腕部骨折、肋骨骨折、股骨骨折。

normal.en: The figurative set is equally fixed: a fractured society, a fractured party, a fractured relationship.
normal.cn: 比喻搭配同样固定：分裂的社会、分裂的政党、破裂的关系。

normal.en: Geologists write of fractured rock and fractured aquifers, where cracks control flow.
normal.cn: 地质学家写破碎岩体与裂隙含水层，其中裂缝控制水流。

normal.en: The base verb keeps the family: fracture, fractures, fracturing, fracturing fluid.
normal.cn: 基础动词维系着词族：fracture、fractures、fracturing、压裂液。

abstract.en: Picture a vase glued back together, still visibly lined.
abstract.cn: 想象一只被粘回的花瓶，裂纹仍清晰可见。

abstract.en: Picture a conversation that keeps restarting after every interruption.
abstract.cn: 想象一段对话每被打断一次就得重来。

abstract.en: Picture a map cut along provincial borders into separate sheets.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图沿省界被裁成几张分开的纸。

examples.en: The climber returned with a fractured ankle and a torn jacket.
examples.cn: 登山者带着骨折的脚踝和划破的夹克回来了。

examples.en: The documentary gives a fractured picture of the war.
examples.cn: 这部纪录片给出了这场战争支离破碎的图景。

examples.en: Rain soaks into the fractured bedrock within minutes.
examples.cn: 雨水在几分钟内渗入破碎的基岩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fract（断）+ ured」——已经被敲断的状态 → 断裂的、分裂的

root: fracture 的过去分词形容词：拉丁 frangere「打破」→ 分词 fractus → fractura「断裂」→ 英语 fracture + -ed。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe a state after a break: the bone, the rock, the building and the market are physical; the parliament, the narrative, the relationship and the halting speech are the same loss of wholeness in other materials.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述断裂之后的状态：骨头、岩石、建筑与市场是物理层面；议会、叙事、关系与断续的言语则是同一种「失去完整」发生在别的材料上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a torn photograph whose pieces no longer line up.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张被撕开的照片，碎片再也对不上。

branches.en: DIRECT STATE: the participle simply reports that a break has happened.
branches.cn: 直接状态：分词只是报告断裂已经发生。

branches.en: SOCIAL BODY: a group or a bond is no longer one piece.
branches.cn: 社会躯体：群体或关系不再是一整块。

branches.en: LOST FLOW: narrative and speech lose the joins that make them continuous.
branches.cn: 失去流畅：叙事与言语失去使它们连贯的接缝。

branches.en: BUILT SYSTEMS: bridges and markets fail as systems once their parts separate.
branches.cn: 人造系统：桥与市场一旦各部分分离，作为系统就失效。

branches.en: ROCK NETWORK: the cracks themselves become the structure that carries water.
branches.cn: 岩石网络：裂缝本身成了输送水的结构。

intro.en: Fractured is an English participle adjective: a Latin-derived base plus the native -ed suffix, with the Latin stem still readable inside.
intro.cn: fractured 是英语分词形容词：拉丁来源的词基加本族语 -ed 后缀，内部仍可读出拉丁词干。

latinIntro.en: The base fracture goes back to Latin frangere and fractura; the -ed is English, so the word is a hybrid of Latin stem and Germanic suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 fracture 上溯拉丁 frangere 与 fractura；-ed 属英语，因此这个词是拉丁词干与日耳曼语后缀的混合体。

items.example: The stem appears in fracture, fraction and fragment.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干出现在 fracture、fraction 与 fragment 中。

items.example: One fracture can end a season.
items.exampleCN: 一次骨折就能结束一个赛季。

items.example: The suffix turns the event into a state.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把事件转成状态。

items.example: The fractured pipe leaked for a week.
items.exampleCN: 破裂的管子漏了一周。

items.example: Fracturing the rock releases the gas.
items.exampleCN: 压裂岩体可释放气体。

items.example: Fragments filled the bottom of the tray.
items.exampleCN: 碎片铺满托盘底部。

items.example: A fraction of the class returned.
items.exampleCN: 班里只有一小部分人回来了。

items.example: The label reads fragile.
items.exampleCN: 标签上写着「易碎」。

items.meaning: to bend light at a boundary
items.example: The prism refracts the beam.
items.exampleCN: 棱镜使光束折射。
